title: Automatically try multiple llm for better success rate
body:
# Description
We have multiple challenges for using LLMs: AWS Anthropic had low rate limiting threshold, Azure OpenAI has tough content filtering policy, OpenAI APIs charge us money. By supporting multiple LLMs and try to run them one by one for a task allows us to leverage our credits with Azure, AWS more. By default, we try Azure OpenAI first, then AWS Anthropic. If one of those succeeds, the same task will try that LLM first in future. This approach allows quicker success (trying previously succeeded LLM first) and higher success rate (trying mulple LLMs increase success rate vs trying 1 LLM only).

# Tests
tested in dev and confirmed that social engagement rate is improved with this approach (it was rejected by Azure OpenAI)

## 🎯 Overview

This PR introduces **multi-LLM support** to the AgentWeb backend, enabling the system to work with different language models (OpenAI, Gemini, etc.) through a unified interface. This is part of the **Emma 2.0** initiative.

## 🔑 Key Changes

### 1. Centralized LLM Call Method
- Introduced `callLLM()` method in `agentModeService.ts` to centralize all LLM interactions
- All LLM calls now go through a single abstraction layer
- Explicit model parameter passing throughout the service layer

### 2. Multi-Provider Configuration
- Added Gemini API configuration (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_BASE_URL`)
- Added OpenAI base URL configuration option
- Updated `.env.example` with clear documentation

## 🧪 Testing

- ✅ Updated 4 test files to mock new `callLLM` method
- ✅ All existing tests passing
- ✅ No breaking changes

## 🚀 Deployment

### Required Environment Variables(Will be replaced with AWS Secretes Manager)
```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key
OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1  # Optional
GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key  # If using Gemini
GEMINI_BASE_URL=https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com  # Optional
```

# LinkedIn Integration & Social Agent Tools

## Summary
This PR implements a full-featured LinkedIn integration, allowing the AI agent to connect to, manage, and post content to both Personal Profiles and Organization/Company Pages. It includes secure OAuth flows, persistent account management, and agentic tools for social media interaction.

## Key Changes

### 🔗 LinkedIn Integration
- **Dual Authentication**: Supported OAuth 2.0 flows for both:
  - **Personal Profiles** (`w_member_social`, `openid`)
  - **Company Pages** (`w_organization_social`, `r_organization_admin`)
- **Connected Accounts Service**: Refactored `User` schema and `connectedAccountsDb` to securely store multi-platform credentials with support for multiple accounts per user.
- **Secure Token Handling**:
  - Implemented server-side token session storage during OAuth to prevent token leakage.
  - Added strict State verification with Signed JWTs to prevent CSRF attacks.
  - Credentials are fetched from **AWS Secrets Manager**, moving away from static env vars.

### 🤖 Agent Mode Enhancements
- **Social Tools**: Updated `agentModeService` with new tools:
  - `linkedin_post`: Create text or image posts.
  - `linkedin_analytics`: Fetch follower counts and page views.
  - `linkedin_list_posts`: Retrieve recent posts.
- **Image Support**: Added `LinkedInAdapter` support for multi-image uploads via URL (e.g., from S3 or generated content).

### 🛠 Technical Updates
- **Secrets Management**: Renamed and structured credential functions in `secretsManager.ts` to clearly distinguish between Personal and Company app credentials.
- **Documentation**: 
  - Updated `dev.md` with the new Secret paths.
  - Updated `.env.example` with required URL configurations.

## Verification
- ✅ **Tests**: Added comprehensive unit tests for `linkedinAuth`, `linkedInService`, and `linkedInAdapter`.

body:
🚀 Implement Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Dynamic Agent Tool Management
Summary
This PR introduces a comprehensive Model Context Protocol (MCP) implementation that enables dynamic tool management and execution for the AI agent. It allows external MCP servers to be connected and their tools to be seamlessly integrated into the agent's capabilities.

##Note:
Need to add MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN in .env  for securing our mcp server.

🎯 Key Features
1. MCP Server Implementation
New MCP Server Core (backend/src/mcp/server/mcpServer.ts, mcpServerCore.ts)
Exposes agent tools as MCP-compatible endpoints
Allows external clients to discover and invoke agent capabilities
Support for SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport
2. MCP Client Service
Dynamic MCP Client (backend/src/mcp/client/mcpClientService.ts)
Connects to external MCP servers (both SSE and database-configured)
Discovers and registers tools from connected servers
Namespaces tools to prevent conflicts between multiple MCP servers
3. Tool Registry
Centralized Tool Registry (backend/src/mcp/client/toolRegistry.ts, backend/src/mcp/server/registry.ts)
Manages tool registrations from multiple sources
Provides unified access to all available tools
Supports dynamic refresh when MCP server configurations change
4. Admin UI for MCP Server Management
New MCP Servers Tab (partner-portal/src/components/admin/McpServersTab.tsx)
Add, edit, and delete MCP server configurations
Discover tools from connected MCP servers
Support for SSE transport configuration
Access token authentication for secure connections
5. REST API Endpoints

title: Fix dropped assistant messages in agent mode
body:
## Summary
- **Fix stale `initialMessageCount`**: When `install_skills` is called mid-conversation, `updateConversationContext` splices context messages at the start of the array, changing its length. `initialMessageCount` (used to slice response messages for DB save) was never updated, causing the first assistant message to be silently excluded from `responseMessages`. This produced orphaned tool messages and 400 errors on all subsequent LLM calls.
- **Fix silent DynamoDB message loss**: `addMessagesToMessagesTable` ignored `UnprocessedItems` from `batchWrite`, silently dropping throttled writes. Added retry loop with exponential backoff (up to 3 retries).

  - Credentials are stored per-environment in AWS Secrets Manager (no hardcoded values)

  New files:
  - src/routes/linkedInOutreachAuth.ts — GET /api/oauth/linkedin-outreach/init (generates Unipile hosted-auth URL) and POST /api/oauth/linkedin-outreach/save-account (fetches account details
   from Unipile and persists to DynamoDB)
  - src/services/linkedInOutreachService.ts — Unipile SDK wrapper: getAccount(), listAccounts(), sendConnectionRequest(), sendMessage()

  Modified files:
  - src/app.ts — Registers new linkedInOutreachAuth router
  - src/routes/connectedAccounts.ts — Adds delete support for unipile platform
  - src/services/connectedAccountsDb.ts — Extends createAccount and deleteAccount to handle unipile platform type
  - src/utils/secretsManager.ts — Adds getUnipileCredentials() (reads from dev/AgentWeb/Unipile / prod/AgentWeb/Unipile)
  - src/services/agentModeService.ts — New linkedin_outreach tool: resolves a LinkedIn profile URL and sends a connection request or direct message

  Tests:
  - src/routes/__tests__/linkedInOutreachAuth.test.ts — OAuth init, save-account success/failure, validation errors
  - src/routes/__tests__/connectedAccounts.unipile.test.ts — Delete account flow for unipile platform

  ---
  ⚙️  Setup Required Before Deploying

  1. Create a Unipile Account

  1. Sign up at https://app.unipile.com
  2. Create a new Datasource and select LinkedIn
  3. Note your DSN (e.g. https://api3.unipile.com:13311) and generate an API Key from the dashboard

  2. Create the AWS Secrets Manager Secret

  Development:
  aws secretsmanager create-secret \
    --name "dev/AgentWeb/Unipile" \
    --secret-string '{"dsn":"https://api3.unipile.com:13311","apiKey":"your_dev_api_key_here"}'

  Production:
  aws secretsmanager create-secret \
    --name "prod/AgentWeb/Unipile" \
    --secret-string '{"dsn":"https://api3.unipile.com:13311","apiKey":"your_prod_api_key_here"}'

  The secret must contain exactly two keys: dsn and apiKey. The backend will throw on startup if either is missing.

  3. Configure the Unipile Redirect URL

  In the Unipile dashboard, set the OAuth callback / success redirect URL to:
  https://<your-frontend-domain>/oauth/linkedin-outreach/callback
  For staging: https://<staging-domain>/oauth/linkedin-outreach/callback

title: Fix publish session crashes
body:
## Summary

- **Context trimming**: Add `trimToolMessagesForContext()` to truncate old large tool-result messages before LLM calls, preventing context window overflow (200K token limit) in sessions with many tool calls
- **LLM retry**: Add `isTransientLLMError()` helper and retry logic to `callLLM()` — 3 attempts with exponential backoff for 503, 429, timeout, and throttling errors
- **Worker requestId**: Fix uncaught exception/rejection handlers in the worker to include `requestId` so the parent process can match error responses to pending requests

Root cause: Production session `f93a6518` crashed twice during a blog publish workflow — first from exceeding the 200K token limit after accumulating massive tool results (10+ search_web, 17 read_file_content, 7 read_page_source, 9 update_html_file, 4 publish_blog_article), then from an unretried Gemini 503 error.

## Test Results

### Unit Tests (19 new, 3267 total)

```
Test Suites: 240 passed, 240 total
Tests:       3267 passed, 3267 total
```

| Area | Tests | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| `isTransientLLMError()` | 11 (503, 429, 502, timeout, throttling, null, 400, 401, context-limit, string, code/response.status) | Pass |
| `callLLM()` retry | 3 (retry-then-succeed, no-retry-on-400, max-retries-exhausted) | Pass |
| `trimToolMessagesForContext()` | 4 (truncate old, preserve recent, immutability, non-tool untouched) | Pass |
| Worker requestId | 1 (source verification of currentRequestId tracking) | Pass |

### Coverage (agentModeErrors.ts)

Statements: 100% | Branches: 91.89% | Functions: 100% | Lines: 100%

- **After fix**: HTTP 200, coherent 2529-char response summarizing session history in 11.3s

- No data migration needed — trimming operates on in-memory copy at runtime

title: Skill-Gated Tool Discovery for Emma MCP Server
body:
## Summary

Implements progressive skill discovery for Emma's MCP server to reduce cognitive overload for external AI assistants:

- **Foundation tools only by default**: External MCP clients (Claude Code, OpenClaw) now see only 17 foundation tools instead of 100+
- **Progressive discovery**: New `list_available_skills()` tool allows browsing Emma's skill catalog before installation
- **Skill installation**: Enhanced `install_skills()` now works with external MCP clients to unlock tools on-demand
- **GTM-focused identity**: MCP server now identifies as "Emma - GTM Automation Specialist" to signal GTM expertise
- **Foundation tools refactored**: Removed generic tools (redundant with Claude Code) and focused on Emma's unique GTM infrastructure:
  - Brand guidelines & market strategy (read/write)
  - Knowledge base access
  - Work plan management
  - GTM discovery tools (leads, connected accounts)
- **Internal clients unaffected**: Agent Mode bypasses skill gating and continues to see all tools
- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Added 19 tests covering ListTools filtering, tool execution validation, skill installation, and session isolation

## Architecture

### Session State
- Extended `SessionEntry` to track `installedSkills`, `agentUserId`, and `isInternal` flag
- Session state shared between transport initialization and server request handlers
- Ephemeral storage (no DynamoDB writes needed)

### Internal vs External Detection
- External clients (aw_* API keys, OAuth) → `isInternal: false`
- Internal clients (MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN) → `isInternal: true`
- Flag set during authentication middleware

### Tool Filtering
- `ListToolsRequestSchema` handler filters tools based on installed skills for external clients
- `CallToolRequestSchema` handler validates tool access before execution
- Foundation tools always accessible (no skill required)

### Foundation Tool Set (17 tools)

```typescript
// Discovery
'install_skills', 'list_available_skills',

// GTM Context
'update_brand_guidelines', 'read_brand_guidelines',
'update_market_strategy', 'read_market_strategy',

// Knowledge Base
'search_knowledge_base', 'list_knowledge_base_files', 'read_knowledge_base_files',

// Work Plans
'create_work_plan', 'modify_work_plan', 'set_work_plan_status',

// GTM Discovery (capability teasers)
'search_leads', 'get_lead_lists', 'list_connected_accounts'
```

## UX Flow Example

1. User connects Emma → Sees server name "Emma - GTM Automation Specialist"
2. Lists tools → Sees brand guidelines, market strategy, leads → "Oh, this is a GTM tool!"
3. User asks: "Help me write a blog post"
4. AI assistant calls `list_available_skills()` → Sees Blog Publishing skill
5. Installs skill → Unlocks blog tools
6. Uses brand guidelines + blog tools together → Consistent, on-brand content

body:
## Summary

Removes skill-gating from Emma's MCP server and exposes all 92 tools to external clients immediately.

## Changes

- ✅ **Remove skill-gating logic** from MCP server core ()
  - External clients now see all tools without calling `install_skills()`
  - Eliminates 2-step discovery workflow (list skills → install → use tools)
  
- ✅ **Dramatically improved tool descriptions**
  - Added "when to use" guidance for ambiguous tool pairs
  - Added decision trees (e.g., `get_leads` vs `search_leads`)
  - Added concrete examples and workflow chains
  - Added prerequisites and related tools sections

- ✅ **Rewrote skill.md** (15,000+ words)
  - Comprehensive agent-readable guide
  - Decision trees for tool selection
  - Complete end-to-end workflows
  - Best practices and troubleshooting
  
- ✅ **Updated release notes** (March 5, 2026)

## Research Backing

Extensive research shows large tool catalogs work well with Claude:
- **Apify MCP server:** 6,000+ tools (no issues)
- **Paragon MCP server:** 130+ tools (no issues)
- **Token usage:** 92 tools = ~18K tokens = only 9% of 200K context window
- **Official guidance:** No documented limits; focus on description quality

See `reports/tool-exposure-research-report.md` (10,000+ word research report for Rui).

## Problem Solved

**Old behavior (skill-gating):**
1. External client connects → sees 16 foundation tools only
2. Must call `list_available_skills()` → discover available skills
3. Must call `install_skills(['skill-id'])` → unlock tools
4. Finally can use tools
5. **Extra friction:** 2 API calls + session isolation issues

**New behavior (no gating):**
1. External client connects → sees all 92 tools immediately
2. Can use any tool right away
3. **Zero friction:** No discovery overhead

## Why This Is Safe

The perceived "cognitive overload" problem was actually about **tool description quality**, not tool count:

### Issues Found (and Fixed):
- ❌ **Ambiguous descriptions:** `get_leads` vs `search_leads` both mentioned "search"
  - ✅ **Fixed:** Clear distinction in descriptions + decision tree
  
- ❌ **Flat namespace:** 92 tools in alphabetical list, hard to browse
  - ✅ **Fixed:** Hierarchical organization in skill.md + grouped by domain
  
- ❌ **Missing context:** No "when to use" guidance
  - ✅ **Fixed:** Every tool now has "when to use vs similar tools" section

### No Evidence of Actual Problems:
- ❌ No benchmarks showing tool selection errors with 100+ tools
- ❌ No user reports of Claude picking wrong tools
- ❌ No performance degradation with large tool sets

title: Harshit/Gmail-Integration
body:
This PR adds full Gmail OAuth 2.0 integration, enabling users to connect their Gmail accounts and allowing Emma (the AI agent) to read and send emails on their behalf. Credentials
  are stored securely in AWS Secrets Manager.

  ---
  What's Included

  1. Google Cloud Console App Setup Required

  Before deploying, create a new OAuth 2.0 Client ID in Google Cloud Console:

  - Application type: Web application
  - Authorized redirect URIs:
    - Dev: https://api-stage.agentweb.pro/api/oauth/gmail/callback
    - Prod: https://api.agentweb.pro/api/oauth/gmail/callback
  - Required OAuth scopes (enable in API & Services → OAuth consent screen):
    - https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly
    - https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send
    - https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email
    - https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.profile
  - Enable APIs: Gmail API, People API (for profile)

  2. AWS Secrets Manager Setup Required

  Store the Google OAuth app credentials in Secrets Manager as JSON:

  ┌─────────────┬────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Environment │        Secret Name         │                    Format                    │
  ├─────────────┼────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Dev/Staging │ dev/AgentWeb/Google/Gmail  │ { "clientId": "...", "clientSecret": "..." } │
  ├─────────────┼────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Production  │ prod/AgentWeb/Google/Gmail │ { "clientId": "...", "clientSecret": "..." } │
  └─────────────┴────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  The backend reads these at runtime via getGmailCredentials() in secretsManager.ts and caches them for 5 minutes to avoid per-request Secrets Manager calls.

  ---
  Backend Changes

  New Files

  - backend/src/routes/gmailAuth.ts — Gmail OAuth flow (4 endpoints):
    - GET /api/oauth/gmail/init — generates Google authorization URL with CSRF-protected JWT state
    - GET /api/oauth/gmail/callback — receives Google redirect, forwards code+state to frontend
    - POST /api/oauth/gmail/finalize — exchanges authorization code for tokens, validates required scopes, stores tokens in a short-lived server-side session (never exposed to browser)
    - POST /api/oauth/gmail/connect — consumes one-time token session, persists OAuth tokens to connected accounts in DynamoDB
  - backend/src/services/gmailService.ts — GmailService class implementing IEmailService:
    - Token auto-refresh (5-minute buffer before expiry) with per-account mutex locks to prevent concurrent refresh races
    - searchEmails() — Gmail query syntax search, uses batch API for efficient metadata fetching
    - getEmail() — full email content with multipart body parsing (plain text preferred, HTML fallback), body size safety limits (50KB HTML cap, 8K char truncation)
    - listEmails() — folder listing (INBOX, SENT, TRASH, SPAM, custom labels) via batch API
    - getEmails() — bulk fetch up to 100 emails per batch request using Gmail batch API
    - sendEmail() — compose and send with reply threading, HTML/plain text, CC/BCC support, built as RFC 2822 MIME message encoded as base64url
    - Structured error types: GmailNotConnectedError, GmailTokenRevokedError, GmailQuotaError, GmailBodyTooLargeError, GmailSendNotAuthorizedError
  - backend/src/services/emailProviderService.ts — provider registry abstraction:
    - IEmailService interface for pluggable email providers
    - registerEmailProvider() / getEmailProvider() for runtime registration
    - resolveEmailAccount() — resolves a connected account ID to its email provider
    - Lazy bootstrapping to avoid circular imports at module load

  Modified Files

  - backend/src/utils/secretsManager.ts — added getGmailCredentials() function; reads dev/AgentWeb/Google/Gmail (or prod/...) and returns { clientId, clientSecret }
  - backend/src/config/integrations.ts — added gmail static config (OAuth URLs, scopes, redirect URI) and getGmailConfig() async function with 5-minute in-memory cache
  - backend/src/services/connectedAccountsDb.ts — added gmail to PlatformType union and GmailConfig interface extending BaseOAuthConfig with Gmail-specific fields
  - backend/src/routes/connectedAccounts.ts — registered gmailAuth router
  - backend/src/app.ts — mounted /api/oauth/gmail route
  - backend/src/mcp/server/tools.ts — added unified email MCP tool (search, list, get, send) backed by emailProviderService

  New Tests

  - __tests__/gmailAuth.test.ts — OAuth flow (init URL generation, callback redirect, finalize scope validation, CSRF state verification, connect account persistence)
  - __tests__/gmailService.test.ts — token refresh, search, get, list, send, batch API, error handling
  - __tests__/connectedAccounts.test.ts — connected accounts CRUD with Gmail platform
  - __tests__/emailProviderService.test.ts — provider registry and account resolution
  - __tests__/integrations.gmail.test.ts — Gmail config loading from Secrets Manager

  ---
  Security Design

  - Tokens never touch the browser — after /finalize, OAuth tokens are stored server-side in an in-memory session (TTL: 10 min, one-time use). The frontend only receives a
  tokenSessionId opaque handle, which is submitted to /connect to persist tokens.
  - CSRF protection — OAuth state parameter is a short-lived JWT (15 min expiry) signed with JWT_SECRET, containing userId + random nonce. Verified before any token exchange.
  - Scope validation — /finalize checks that Google actually granted gmail.readonly and gmail.send before saving. Returns 422 with missingScopes if any are absent.
  - Token refresh locking — per-account Promise lock prevents concurrent refresh races when multiple requests hit an expired token simultaneously.

  ---
  Test Plan

  - Create Google Cloud OAuth app; store credentials in dev/AgentWeb/Google/Gmail in Secrets Manager
  - Connect a Gmail account via Settings → Connected Accounts → Add Gmail
  - Verify OAuth consent screen shows correct scopes (read + send)
  - Ask Emma: "Search my Gmail for emails from [someone]" — verify results
  - Ask Emma: "Send an email to [address] with subject X and body Y" — verify delivery
  - Ask Emma: "List my inbox" — verify folder listing works
  - Disconnect and reconnect Gmail account; verify token refresh works after ~1 hour
  - Run unit tests: cd backend && npm test
  - Run TypeScript check: cd backend && npx tsc

title: Fix: Add search_web to foundation tools for scheduled chats
body:
## Summary
- Fixed issue where `search_web` tool was not available to scheduled chat sessions
- Moved `search_web` from skill-gated tools to `FOUNDATION_TOOLS` 
- Added test coverage for `search_web` in foundation tools
- Updated CLAUDE.md with Basic subscription test account

## Root Cause
The GlobalReads account (`cc21acba-963a-43ce-a417-551e0be82534`) has "GlobalReads Blog Article" scheduled chat requiring `search_web`, but:
1. `search_web` was NOT in `FOUNDATION_TOOLS`
2. `search_web` was NOT in any published skill
3. User has Basic subscription (default) which includes `__other_skills__`, but the subscription check at `runScheduledChat` (lines 810-867) runs BEFORE auto-install logic
4. Result: scheduled chats failed with "Required function calls are not allowed by your subscription: search_web"

## Solution
Added `search_web` to `FOUNDATION_TOOLS` as it's:
- A core research capability described in system prompt as always available
- Does not require user confirmation
- Should be accessible to all users like `search_knowledge_base`

title: Replace direct MCP tools with REST API wrapper layer
body:
## Summary

Implements **Approach B** from the IDOR vulnerability writeup (dev.md, March 6): migrate from 90+ internal Emma tools exposed directly via MCP to ~30 REST API wrapper tools that go through `authenticateToken` middleware.

- **Replaced `tools.ts` (75 tools) and `portalTools.ts` (12 tools)** with `apiTools.ts` (~30 tools) that call backend REST APIs via `mcpFetch()` — a helper that generates short-lived JWTs and makes HTTP self-calls to localhost
- **Added `routes/emmaApi.ts`** with REST endpoints for AI operations (search, image gen, email, etc.) that previously had no HTTP route
- **Internal tools hidden from external MCP clients**: `install_skills`, `list_available_skills`, `search_web`, `generate_image`, `send_email`, `save_file` are registered with `internal: true` — available to Emma internally but filtered out of MCP `ListTools` responses
- **MCP Emma sessions use the same skill-first flow as the customer portal** — no MCP-specific behavior (removed `installAllSkills` hack)
- **Fixed `emma_send_message`** to pass `userMessage` (not `message`) matching the backend API contract
- **Net reduction**: ~5,500 lines removed, ~3,000 added (deleting tools.ts and portalTools.ts)

Architecture:
```
MCP Client → MCP Server (API key auth) → mcpFetch() → localhost REST API → authenticateToken → route handler → service → DB
```

External MCP: 26 tools. Emma internal registry: 32 tools.

## Test plan

title: docs: Add disaster recovery readiness investigation
body:
## Summary

- Comprehensive DR readiness assessment of the AgentWeb production platform, verified against live AWS environment
- Covers all 10 areas: DynamoDB (29 tables), S3 (5 buckets), IaC, HA/multi-region, auth/tokens, secrets, monitoring, network security, CI/CD, and incident response
- Overall finding: **POOR** — near-zero production-grade DR capabilities with risk of permanent data loss
- Includes prioritized remediation plan (P0 immediate through P3 medium-term)

- Deletion protection DISABLED on all 29 DynamoDB tables
- 2 S3 buckets publicly accessible (`agentweb-user-files`, `agentweb-execution-gifs`)
- Zero CloudTrail trails, zero CloudWatch log groups
- 51 secrets with zero rotation enabled
- No IaC, no incident response runbooks, no multi-region failover

title: feat: Add list_my_landing_pages tool for lightweight LP editing
body:
## Summary
- Adds `list_my_landing_pages` Emma tool that returns the user's generated landing pages (id, name, status, githubRepoUrl, deployedUrl)
- Bridges the v0 data model to the existing GitHub MCP tools, enabling free edits (read file → edit → commit → Vercel auto-deploys) without burning v0 iterate credits
- Includes 6 tests (2 failure cases, 1 empty result, 2 success cases, 1 registration check)

## How it works
1. `list_my_landing_pages` → gets repo URLs from AW-LandingPages DynamoDB
2. `github_get_file_contents({ owner, repo, path })` → reads file + SHA (via existing GitHub MCP server)

title: feat: Batch email preview and send endpoints
body:
## Risk Level: High

This PR adds endpoints that send real emails to real people via Resend. No batch size limit means a single API call could trigger hundreds or thousands of emails. Accidental or malicious use could burn through Resend quota, damage sender reputation, or spam external recipients.

## What was wrong (before)
No way to preview or send batch emails from the CRM. Users had to send emails individually or use external tools for outreach campaigns.

## What this fixes (after)
Two new endpoints on the CRM routes:
- `POST /api/crm/lists/:listId/batch-email/preview` — generates email previews with template variable substitution (safe, read-only)
- `POST /api/crm/lists/:listId/batch-email/send` — sends batch emails via Resend with engagement logging per lead

Template variables (`{{fundName}}`, `{{partnerName}}`, custom fields) are substituted per-lead. Engagement events are logged after each successful send.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 214 CRM tests passed, 0 failures (1 suite skipped due to disk space on runner, unrelated)
- TypeScript compiles clean
- No dedicated tests for the new batch-email endpoints exist yet

## Files changed
- `backend/src/routes/crm.ts` (+281 lines) — two new route handlers appended

## What was NOT tested
- Actual email delivery via Resend — no integration test or mock verifying the send path
- Batch size limits — no cap on leadIds array length; a request with 10,000 lead IDs would attempt 10,000 sends
- Rate limiting — Resend service has a 500ms internal queue interval, but no endpoint-level rate limit or concurrency control
- Input sanitization on template variables — custom field values are injected into HTML without escaping (potential XSS in email clients, though most strip scripts)
- Error recovery — if the endpoint crashes mid-batch (e.g., at email 150 of 300), there is no idempotency key or resume mechanism
- Authorization on senderAccountId — sender email is resolved from user settings, but if settings are manipulated, a user could send as someone else's email address

## Recommendations before merge
1. Add a batch size cap (e.g., if leadIds.length > 100 return 400) to prevent accidental mass sends
2. Add dedicated unit tests for both endpoints (mock resendService, verify variable substitution, test edge cases)
3. Consider a dry-run/confirmation flow — the preview endpoint exists but nothing prevents the send endpoint from being called directly without previewing first

No free trial — new users had to pick a paid plan immediately or use the product without any trial period. No mechanism for admins to grant extended access for onboarding calls.

title: fix: Prevent email enumeration in login and register endpoints
body:
## Risk Level: Medium

Security fix on auth endpoints. Low code complexity (4 lines changed in controller), but touches login/register error responses that the frontend reads.

## What was wrong (before)

The login endpoint returned a **404 with "User not found"** when the email didn't exist, and a **401 with "Invalid credentials"** when the password was wrong. An attacker could send login requests and tell from the different status codes (404 vs 401) and messages which emails are registered. Same issue on register — it returned **"User already exists"** for taken emails.

This is OWASP A01:2021 (Broken Access Control) — email enumeration.

## What this fixes (after)

- **Login**: Both "user doesn't exist" and "wrong password" now return **401 + "Invalid credentials"** with code `invalid_credentials`. Identical response either way — no way to tell the difference.
- **Register**: Returns **"Unable to create account. Please try again or use a different email."** instead of "User already exists". Doesn't confirm whether the email is taken.
- The `forgotPassword` endpoint already handled this correctly (same generic message regardless).

## Frontend impact

The customer portal Login page (`Login.tsx:72`) has a `if (errorCode === "user_not_found")` branch that shows a "Sign up here" link. After this fix, that branch **never triggers** because the backend no longer returns `user_not_found`. This is **intentionally correct** — showing "Sign up here" would itself reveal that the email isn't registered, defeating the purpose of this fix.

The `AuthErrorCode` type in `AuthContext.tsx` still includes `"user_not_found"` — now dead code but harmless. Could be cleaned up later.

Other "User already exists" / "User not found" references in the frontend are unrelated (Stripe session check, stale session suppression).

## Test evidence

- **4 new tests** in `auth.emailEnumeration.test.ts` — all pass:
  1. Non-existent user gets generic 401 (not 404, not "not found")
  2. Wrong password and non-existent user get identical status + message + code
  3. Valid login still returns 200 with token
  4. Existing email on register gets generic error (not "already exists")
- **All 168 existing auth tests pass** (12 suites, 0 failures)

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `backend/src/controllers/auth.ts` | 4 lines — login returns 401/invalid_credentials instead of 404/user_not_found; register returns generic message instead of "User already exists" |
| `backend/src/__tests__/auth.emailEnumeration.test.ts` | 133 lines — new test file with 4 tests for enumeration prevention |

## What was NOT tested

- **Frontend behavior**: The Login page "Sign up here" link no longer appears. Not verified via E2E/Playwright — only confirmed by code reading. Should be fine (it is the intended behavior) but worth a quick manual check.
- **Google OAuth flow**: Not changed in this PR, but also returns different responses for new vs existing users. Worth a follow-up audit.
- **Rate limiting**: This PR makes error messages generic, but does not add rate limiting or account lockout. An attacker could still brute-force passwords. Separate concern.
- **Timing attacks**: No constant-time comparison was added. An attacker could theoretically measure response times (user-not-found returns faster because it skips bcrypt.compare). Low risk but worth noting.

## Notion task

https://www.notion.so/31f09247c9518131806bc7b9d94bad9b

title: fix: Redact API keys in MCP server config GET responses
body:
## Risk Level: Medium

Security fix — changes what data is returned from an admin API endpoint. Low blast radius (admin-only endpoint, read path only), but incorrect redaction could either leak keys or break the admin UI.

## What was wrong (before)

The GET /api/admin/mcp-servers endpoint returned MCP server configs with plaintext API keys in accessToken, env values, CLI args, and URL query params. Anyone with admin API access (or an XSS in the admin panel) could harvest third-party API keys (Brave Search, SerpAPI, etc.) from the response body.

## What this fixes (after)

All sensitive values are now masked before the response is sent:
- accessToken -> first2***last2
- env values where key name matches KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/API -> masked
- CLI args following --api-key, --token, --secret, --password -> masked
- URL query params like api_key, token, secret -> masked
- Non-sensitive values (ports, commands, NODE_ENV) are preserved as-is

Redaction uses a first2***last2 pattern (or just *** for values 4 chars or less).

## Test Evidence

- 5 new unit tests (all pass): accessToken redacted, env keys redacted, args after sensitive flags redacted, non-sensitive args preserved, URL query params redacted
- 13 existing mcpServers tests (all pass): no regressions
- CI: All checks green (backend tests + deploy to staging)

Test Suites: 2 passed, 2 total | Tests: 18 passed, 18 total

## Files changed

- backend/src/routes/mcpServers.ts (+57 -1) — Added redactConfig(), redactValue(), sensitive flag/param lists. Applied to GET route.
- backend/src/__tests__/mcpServers.redaction.test.ts (+133 new) — 5 test cases covering all redaction paths

## What was NOT tested

- PUT/POST paths: Redaction only applies to GET. The write path still stores raw values (by design — you need the real key to connect).
- Admin UI impact: Did not verify the admin panel still renders correctly with redacted values.
- Edge cases: Keys exactly 4 chars get fully masked. Keys embedded in URL paths (not query params) are not redacted.
- Header-based keys: If an MCP config stores keys in custom headers, those are not redacted (no headers field exists today).

## Notion task

https://www.notion.so/31f09247c951815fa1e3fdc09948614e

title: fix: Add rate limiting on login/register endpoints
body:
## Risk Level: High

Auth endpoints are the front door to the product. This is a security fix — if misconfigured, it could lock out real users or fail to stop attackers.

## What was wrong (before)

Login and register endpoints had **zero rate limiting**. An attacker could try unlimited passwords against any account (brute-force attack) or spam account registrations without any throttling.

## What this fixes (after)

Added rate limiting: **10 attempts per 15 minutes per IP address** on `/api/auth/login` and `/api/auth/register`. After 10 failed attempts from the same IP, the server returns HTTP 429 ("Too many requests") with a Retry-After header. Other auth endpoints (like /me) are not affected.

Uses express-rate-limit v8.3.1 (well-maintained, industry-standard middleware).

## Test Evidence

- Unit tests: **5 passed, 0 failed**
- Test 1: Login returns 429 after 11 requests from same IP
- Test 2: Register returns 429 after 11 requests from same IP
- Test 3: 429 response includes Retry-After header
- Test 4: Normal login still works within the limit
- Test 5: GET /me is NOT rate-limited (only login/register are)

## Files changed

- \`backend/src/routes/auth.ts\` — Added authRateLimiter middleware to login + register routes (10 lines)
- \`backend/src/__tests__/auth.rateLimit.test.ts\` — New test file with 5 tests covering rate limit behavior (172 lines)
- \`backend/package.json\` — Added express-rate-limit dependency
- \`backend/package-lock.json\` — Lock file update

## What was NOT tested

- **Load testing under real traffic** — rate limiter uses in-memory store by default, not Redis. Works for single-server but will not share state across multiple backend instances
- **Proxy/CDN behavior** — relies on X-Forwarded-For header for real IP detection. If the app sits behind a proxy that does not set this header, all users share the same rate limit bucket
- **Window reset behavior** — tests do not wait 15 minutes to verify the window actually resets
- **Frontend UX** — no user-facing message telling the user they have been locked out and when to try again

## Notion task

https://www.notion.so/31f09247c95181d7867ceded9fde8666

## Risk Level: Medium

Modifies core SSE progress pipeline. Backward compatibility verified via existing test suite (13 controller tests + 19 existing unit tests all pass).

## What was wrong (before)
When Emma executes tools like `update_brand_guidelines` or `create_landing_page`, the SSE progress stream only reports tool status (thinking → executing → complete). The frontend has no way to know which page to navigate the user to after a tool completes — users have to manually navigate.

title: fix: restrict CORS Access-Control-Allow-Methods header
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
Every endpoint responded to OPTIONS preflight requests with `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE,OPTIONS`, advertising OPTIONS as an allowed method even though it's handled implicitly by the CORS middleware. This violates the principle of least privilege.

## What this fixes (after)
Removed `OPTIONS` from the explicit CORS `methods` list. The `cors` middleware still handles OPTIONS preflight requests automatically — it just no longer advertises it as a user-callable method. The header now reads: `GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE`.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 6 passed, 0 failed (`backend/src/__tests__/cors.test.ts`)
- Tests verify: no OPTIONS in Allow-Methods, no TRACE/CONNECT/HEAD, credentials support, public endpoint restrictions

## Files changed
- `backend/src/app.ts` — removed `OPTIONS` from CORS methods array
- `backend/src/__tests__/cors.test.ts` — new: 6 tests covering CORS method advertisement

## What was NOT tested
- Per-route method restriction (future improvement — would require auditing all 50+ route files)
- Production deployment verification with real browsers
- Socket.IO CORS (already correctly restricted to `GET, POST` in `server.ts`)

title: feat: Warmly webhook payload mapping + enrichment fields
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
The `/api/webhooks/forward-lead` endpoint only accepts leads in our standard schema. Warmly sends visitor data with different field names (`visitor_email`, `visitor_first_name`, `warmly_visitor_id`, etc.), so Warmly webhooks would fail with "Email is required" since the `email` field is named `visitor_email`.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds a `normalizeWarmlyPayload()` function that detects Warmly payloads (by `source: 'warmly'` or presence of `warmly_visitor_id`) and maps Warmly-specific fields to our standard Lead schema. Enrichment fields (pages_viewed, time_on_site, visitor_location, referrer, etc.) are stored in `customFields`. Non-Warmly payloads pass through completely unchanged.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 22 passed, 0 failed
- 4 new Warmly-specific test cases:
  1. Maps Warmly visitor_* fields to standard Lead fields
  2. Auto-detects Warmly payload by warmly_visitor_id (no explicit source)
  3. Stores enrichment fields in customFields
  4. Non-Warmly payloads unchanged (regression)

## Files changed
- `backend/src/routes/webhooks.ts` — added `normalizeWarmlyPayload()` function (~50 lines) + call before field extraction
- `backend/src/__tests__/webhooks.leadForwarding.test.ts` — added 4 Warmly test cases (~130 lines)

## What was NOT tested
- End-to-end with real Warmly webhook (no test env integration yet)
- Dedup/merge behavior with Warmly payloads for existing leads

title: Critical: Concurrency gate + orphan recovery for multi-task generation
body:
## Risk: High | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Users could start unlimited concurrent AI generations regardless of their subscription tier, leading to resource exhaustion and no enforcement of tier-based limits. Server crashes could leave sessions permanently stuck in 'generating' status, exhausting concurrency slots forever.

## What this fixes (after)
Enforces per-user concurrent generation limits (Basic:1, Pro:3, Super Premium:5) with a 429 response that includes active session IDs for frontend "switch to session" UX. Adds startup orphan recovery that resets sessions stuck in 'generating' for >1hr to 'error'.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 11 passed, 0 failed (concurrencyGate.test.ts)
- Existing tests: 4488 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing flaky timing test)
- Tested as: mock-based unit tests with chatbotDb and subscriptionService mocks

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/concurrencyGate.ts` (NEW) — Gate check with fail-open design
- `backend/src/services/orphanRecovery.ts` (NEW) — Startup scan + recovery
- `backend/src/__tests__/concurrencyGate.test.ts` (NEW) — 11 tests
- `backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts` — Gate enforcement in generateResponse + verifiedGenerate, generation status lifecycle
- `backend/src/server.ts` — Orphan recovery on startup
- `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeController.*.test.ts` (3 files) — Added missing mock signatures

## What was NOT tested
- End-to-end with real DynamoDB (mock-based only)
- Frontend 429 handling UX (frontend changes not in scope)
- Orphan recovery DynamoDB scan performance under high session volume
- Interaction with WebSocket progress updates during 429 rejection
- Race condition between concurrent gate check and status update (window is small but theoretically possible)

## Rollback plan
Revert this commit — the system returns to unlimited concurrent generations (no data migration needed, generationStatus field from Part 1 remains harmless).

- Backend Part 2 (concurrency limits): merged

title: feat: LinkedIn auto-connection trigger on new leads
body:
## Risk: High | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
When deanonymized leads with LinkedIn URLs arrived via the forward-lead webhook, no automated LinkedIn outreach was triggered. Sales had to manually find and connect with leads on LinkedIn.

## What this fixes (after)
When `linkedInAutoConnectEnabled` is true on a lead list and a new lead arrives with a LinkedIn URL, a personalized connection request is automatically queued via the existing Unipile/LinkedIn integration. Includes dedup to prevent duplicate connection requests.

title: fix: improve satisfaction scoring to distinguish content vs chat formatting
body:
## Summary
Fixes [session 148324f0 with satisfaction score 2](https://app.agentweb.pro/ishare/148324f0-0573-4eda-9f32-cf25f9b5479e?conversable=fdadd3d0230050225cc69e355e48af1002fff92c7c15417ac11017e8dc026778) where Emma correctly generated a plain text LinkedIn post but was incorrectly penalized by the satisfaction scoring system.

## Problem
The user requested "create LinkedIn post with no markdown and plain text only". Emma correctly:
- ✅ Generated the LinkedIn post in plain text (no markdown)
- ✅ Used HTML formatting in the chat response to present the content clearly
- ✅ Used `create_social_media_posts` tool which returned a file link (standard behavior)

However, the satisfaction scoring LLM incorrectly penalized Emma for:
- ❌ Using HTML formatting in chat responses (thought "plain text only" applied to chat format)
- ❌ Providing a file link instead of inline content (didn't understand this is standard tool behavior)

Result: Score of 2/5

## Solution
Updated the `SCORING_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `sessionScoringService.ts` with two key clarifications:

### 1. Content vs Chat Response Formatting
- When users request formatting for content (e.g., "create post with no markdown"), those requirements apply to the GENERATED CONTENT only
- The assistant can still use HTML tags in chat responses to present information clearly
- Example: "create LinkedIn post with no markdown" means the post content should be plain text, but chat formatting can use HTML

### 2. File Links from Tool Functions
- Tools like `create_social_media_posts`, `create_blog_article` often return file URLs as standard output
- Providing content via file links is acceptable and does not violate user requirements
- Focus should be on whether the content itself (when accessed) meets the user's specifications

## Changes
- **Modified**: `backend/src/services/sessionScoringService.ts` - Added two clarification sections to SCORING_SYSTEM_PROMPT
- **Modified**: `backend/src/__tests__/sessionScoring.contentFormatting.test.ts` - Added 5th test for file link scenario (5/5 passing)

## Verification
✅ **Fix confirmed!** Rescored session 148324f0 in dev:
- **Before fix**: Score 2/5 - "assistant failed to follow formatting rules... provided link to external file"
- **After fix**: Score 5/5 - "successfully followed instructions... correctly interpreted formatting requirements by providing content via link"

title: fix: landing page generation retry + rate limit resilience
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Three real users (Fangfang, Matt x2) experienced landing page generation failures:
1. **No retry on transient errors** — `generate_landing_page` failed with "fetch failed" network errors and gave up immediately. Fangfang's session had 4+ failed attempts with zero automatic recovery.
2. **Rate limit death spiral** — failed API calls counted against the hourly quota. When Matt hit errors trying to fix design fidelity (fonts, colors, calculator), each failed retry consumed rate limit, eventually locking him out entirely. Emma told him to "start a fresh session" as the only workaround.
3. **No exponential backoff** — retries happened immediately with no delay, increasing the chance of hitting the same transient issue.

## What this fixes (after)
1. **Exponential backoff retry** (3 attempts, 2s→4s→8s) on all v0 API calls: chat creation, chat fetch, and zip download. Only retries on transient network errors (fetch failed, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, socket hang up, ECONNRESET).
2. **5xx errors no longer count against rate limit** — only successful responses (< 500) consume quota. This prevents the death spiral where transient failures eat up a user's 10/hour limit.
3. Non-retryable errors (auth, validation) still fail immediately on first attempt.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 33 passed, 0 failed (25 existing + 8 new)
- New tests cover: retry on fetch failed, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, socket hang up; no retry on auth/validation errors; exhaust retries; 5xx not counting against rate limit; 4xx still counting

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/v0Service.ts` — `withRetry()` helper + wrapped v0 API calls
- `backend/src/routes/landingPageGeneration.ts` — rate limiter counts on response, not request
- `backend/src/__tests__/routes.landingPageGeneration.test.ts` — 2 new rate limit tests
- `backend/src/__tests__/v0Service.withRetry.test.ts` — 8 new retry behavior tests

title: fix: preserve existing satisfaction scores in get_chat_history
body:
## Summary

- Fixed bug where `get_chat_history` with `sync=true` would not return satisfaction scores for sessions that were already scored
- Added fix to copy existing `satisfactionScore` from `fullSession` to response object when `scoreSessionIfNeeded` returns null (skipped)
- Updated release notes

## Problem

When `getAdminChatHistory` is called with `sync=true`:
1. It queries sessions from the GSI (lightweight projections)
2. For each session, loads full session data and calls `scoreSessionIfNeeded`
3. If session is already scored, `scoreSessionIfNeeded` returns `null` (skipped)
4. **Bug**: The existing score from `fullSession` was never copied to the response `session` object
5. Result: Already-scored sessions showed `satisfactionScore: undefined` in the API response

## Solution

When `scoreSessionIfNeeded` returns `null`, copy the existing `satisfactionScore` from `fullSession` to `session`:

```typescript
} else {
  scoringResults.push({ sessionId: session.sessionId, status: 'skipped' });
  // Copy existing score from fullSession if present
  if (fullSession.satisfactionScore) {
    session.satisfactionScore = fullSession.satisfactionScore;
  }
}
```

## Test Results

Tested with API calls against dev backend:
- Queried 45 sessions with `sync=true`
- 28 sessions returned with scores (62%)
- 17 sessions without scores (38% - expected, not enough messages)
- ✅ Session with score=5 returned correctly
- ✅ Session with score=2 returned correctly
- ✅ Both newly scored and previously scored sessions work correctly

## Files Changed

- `backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts` - Added fix to copy existing scores
- `backend/src/docs/user-release.ts` - Added release notes for the fix

- **Remove redundant `marketData`** from the tool result — `formattedContent` is what the LLM sees (via line 1107), so returning both was doubling the payload (~100K → ~45K)

- **Fix email prompt builder** to use `formattedContent` directly instead of falling back to `JSON.stringify(marketData)`

### Root Cause
Session `75577be0` (xCures "Weekly Competitor News Researcher") failed because:
1. `readMarketStrategy` returned ~100K of data (37 competitors × ~1K description each, sent twice as both `formattedContent` and `marketData`)
2. `trimToolMessagesForContext` truncated it to 8K after the first LLM turn
3. The LLM only saw 7 of 37 competitors for the rest of the session

## Auto Test Environment & Testing Plan on PRs

This PR adds automation so that every pull request automatically gets a **detailed testing plan** posted as a comment. The goal: when you come back to review a PR (especially after overnight autonomous work), the environment is ready and you know exactly what to verify.

title: Harshit/linkedin auto engagement
body:
Summary                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                            
  Adds automated LinkedIn social engagement — the system periodically discovers new posts from connected accounts and schedules likes, comments, and comment replies, with randomised
  delays to mimic natural behaviour. All engagement is strictly same-user scoped: a user's accounts only engage with other accounts belonging to the same user.                         
   
  New: Scanner + Executor pipeline                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                            
  - SocialEngagementScanner (runs every 60 min): scans users with engagement-enabled connected accounts, fetches recent posts, and queues engagement actions into AW-TaskSchedules with 
  a random delay within the configured window                               
    - For actions due within 30 min, fires the executor directly via onActionScheduled callback without waiting for the next TimerScheduler poll                                        
  - SocialEngagementExecutor + SocialEngagementTimerScheduler: the scheduler polls every 30 min and registers a precise setTimeout per upcoming action; the executor processes the queue
   with a claimAction conditional write to prevent duplicate execution across server instances                                                                                          
  - Uses Gemini to generate contextual comments/replies and select the most appropriate reaction type (LIKE, PRAISE, EMPATHY, INTEREST, APPRECIATION, ENTERTAINMENT)                    
  - Rate-limit errors (HTTP 429) trigger a 30-min retry; all other failures are marked permanent                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  New: Per-account engagement config                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  engagementSettings stored inline on each connected_accounts entry, separating two independent roles:                                                                                  
  - Owner role (enablePostDiscovery): this account's posts can receive engagement from the user's other accounts — with per-post caps and preferred action types (like, comment)
  - Engager role (enableAsPostEngager): this account will engage on the user's other accounts' posts                                                                                    
  - Comment auto-reply (enableCommentDiscovery): account auto-likes/replies to comments on its own posts, with per-post lifetime caps
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  New: AW-SocialEngagementTracking table                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  Tracks all engagement activity per userId + postId/commentId + engagingAccountId:                                                                                                     
  - Deduplication — hasEngaged() blocks re-queuing already queued/completed actions                                                                                                     
  - Fail-count tracking with atomic ADD increment — allows up to 3 retries before permanently blocking                                                                                  
  - GSIs: EngagingAccountIndex (account-level history) and PostEngagementIndex (post-level history)   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  New: API endpoints                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  - GET /social-posts/config — returns all connected accounts with their engagement settings                                                                                            
  - PUT /social-posts/config — saves engagement settings for a single account, with input validation and backward-compat handling for legacy autoEngagement boolean
  - GET /social-posts/activity/account/:accountId — engagement history for a specific account                                                                                           
  - GET /social-posts/activity/post/:postId — engagement history for a specific post (URN-encoded)                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  Supporting changes                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  - linkedInService.ts bug fix: getComments was returning bare el.id as the comment URN; now correctly constructs urn:li:comment:(postUrn,id) — required for comment reply/reaction     
  targeting to work
  - linkedInAdapter.ts: new getPost() — O(1) DynamoDB lookup for personal accounts (getPostById), falls back to listPosts scan for org accounts                                         
  - linkedInPostsDb.ts: new getPostById() — direct primary-key get by userId + postId                                                                                                   
  - db.ts fix: scanWithFilter was always passing ExpressionAttributeValues to DynamoDB even when empty — DynamoDB rejects this; now conditionally omitted                               
  - db.ts: updateScheduleAfterRun now issues REMOVE claimedAt, claimedBy alongside the status update, releasing the claim lock atomically on completion                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  Security                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  - IDOR fix on GET /social-posts/activity/post/:postId: getEngagementsByPost now requires userId and applies it as a DynamoDB FilterExpression — users only receive engagement records 
  for their own posts; no cross-user data is returned
                                                                                                                                                                                        
  Test plan                                                                                                                                                                             
  
  - Connect two LinkedIn accounts under the same user; enable enablePostDiscovery on one and enableAsPostEngager on the other — verify actions are queued in AW-TaskSchedules after     
  scanner run                                                               
  - Verify executor picks up due actions, posts to LinkedIn, and records completion in AW-SocialEngagementTracking                                                                      
  - Verify hasEngaged dedup prevents re-queuing the same post/account pair on subsequent scanner runs                                                                                   
  - Enable enableCommentDiscovery and verify comment auto-replies are scheduled and executed from the same account                                                                      
  - Simulate a 429 response — verify action is rescheduled 30 min out rather than marked failed                                                                                         
  - Call GET /social-posts/activity/post/:postId with a post URN belonging to another user — verify empty response (no foreign data returned)                                           
  - Call GET /social-posts/activity/account/:accountId with an account not owned by the requesting user — verify 403

title: Fix: prevent duplicate actions on partial failures and improve cron executor robustness
body:
## Problem

Two related bugs in the social engagement auto-engagement system caused actions to be duplicated or retried indefinitely:

### Bug 1 — Duplicate comments/replies on partial failure

When an action type involved both a primary action (comment or reply) **and** a secondary action (like), and the primary succeeded but the like failed, the action was marked `failed`. On the next cron run the same action was retried — but the comment/reply had already been posted, resulting in **duplicate comments or replies** on the same post.

Affected action types:
- `comment_and_like` — comment posted successfully, like fails → comment gets posted again on retry
- `like_and_reply_comment` — reply posted successfully, like fails → reply gets posted again on retry

### Bug 2 — Compound action types prevented independent retry

The scanner was scheduling combined `comment_and_like` and `like_and_reply_comment` action types using a **single dedup key** for both sub-actions. If like-only was already done, comment was still blocked (and vice versa) because they shared the same dedup record. There was no way to retry only the failed sub-action.

### Bug 3 — `failCount` reset on scanner re-queue

When the scanner re-queued a failed action, `recordEngagement` was called with `status: 'queued'` using a DynamoDB `PUT`, which **overwrote** the entire item including `failCount`. This reset the retry counter to 0 on every re-queue, making the 3-retry cap (`SOCIAL_ENGAGEMENT_MAX_RETRIES = 3`) unreachable — actions would retry indefinitely.

### Bug 4 — `hasEngaged` dedup key collision

The per-action dedup key was `{postId}#{engagingAccountId}`, shared across all action types. A completed `like` would block a `comment` from being scheduled for the same post+account, and vice versa.

---

## Fix

### Executor: degrade gracefully when like fails after primary action succeeds

In `socialEngagementExecutor.ts`, wrap the `createReaction` call (for `comment_and_like` and `like_and_reply_comment`) in a try/catch. If the like fails **and** the primary action (comment/reply) already succeeded, log a warning and continue — the action is marked `completed` rather than `failed`. This prevents the retry from re-posting the comment or reply.

If the like is the **only** action (action type `like` or `like_comment`), the error is still thrown and the action is retried normally.

### Scanner: emit separate atomic actions instead of compound types

`schedulePostEngagers` and `scheduleCommentReplyEngagers` now schedule individual `like`, `comment`, `reply_comment`, and `like_comment` actions independently. Compound types (`comment_and_like`, `like_and_reply_comment`) are no longer emitted by the scanner. Each action gets its own dedup record and can be retried independently.

A shared `scheduleOneAction` helper records the tracking entry **before** creating the schedule (record-first pattern), so the dedup guard is in place even if `createSchedule` throws.

### DB: per-action dedup keys and UPDATE for queued status

- **New atomic action types** use key `{postId}#{engagingAccountId}#{actionType}` so like and comment can coexist on the same post+account pair.
- **Legacy compound types** (`comment_and_like`, `like_and_reply_comment`) retain the old key format for backward compatibility with any already-queued items.
- `hasEngaged` checks both the action-specific key and the legacy key, so existing records still block reschedules.
- `recordEngagement` now uses `UPDATE` (not `PUT`) for `status: 'queued'`, preserving `failCount` across retries and making the 3-retry cap effective.
- `executedAt` is set on queued items so they appear in the GSI used by the per-post cap count (DynamoDB excludes items with missing GSI sort keys).

---

## Tests

56 tests pass across `socialEngagementExecutor.test.ts` and `socialEngagementScannerCron.test.ts`, covering:

- Comment succeeds, like fails → action marked completed (no duplicate on retry)
- Reply succeeds, like fails → action marked completed (no duplicate on retry)
- Comment fails → action still marked failed (retried correctly)
- Scanner schedules separate `like` and `comment` actions (never `comment_and_like`)
- Scanner schedules separate `reply_comment` and `like_comment` actions (never `like_and_reply_comment`)
- Already-replied comment can still have `like_comment` scheduled independently
- Per-post cap is enforced correctly using counts that include queued items

title: fix: LinkedIn token refresh updates wrong account for company pages
body:
## Summary
- **Root cause**: When a company page token expired and was refreshed via `getValidToken()`, the refreshed token was saved to the wrong connected account (first LinkedIn match, typically personal) because `account_id` was not passed to `updateAccountTokens`. This left the company page with a stale expired token.
- **Fix**: Pass `account.account_id` to `updateAccountTokens` in `linkedInAdapter.ts` so the correct account gets updated.
- **Also**: Improved 403 error messages for company page comment failures with actionable guidance, and preserved detailed permission errors through the agent mode error handler instead of replacing them with a generic message.

## Root Cause Analysis
When a user has both a personal LinkedIn account and a company page connected, both share the same OAuth token from a single authorization flow. When the token expires and `getValidToken()` refreshes it, `updateAccountTokens()` was called without an `account_id`, causing it to fall back to the first LinkedIn account found (personal). The company page's token remained expired, causing subsequent API calls (especially comments) to fail.

## Files Changed
- `backend/src/services/adapters/linkedInAdapter.ts` — Pass `account_id` to token update; improve 403 error messages
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` — Preserve detailed permission errors in comment/react error handlers

title: fix: prevent duplicate subscriptions on plan upgrades
body:
## Risk: High | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
When existing subscribers changed plans via the Pricing page, the `create-checkout-session` endpoint created a NEW Stripe subscription instead of updating the existing one. This caused duplicate subscriptions, webhook confusion (stale subscription events overwriting the active one), and users unable to access features they paid for after upgrading.

## What this fixes (after)
- **New `/api/stripe/upgrade` endpoint**: Uses `stripe.subscriptions.update()` with proration for existing subscribers changing plans
- **`has_used_trial` flag**: Prevents trial abuse when users hop between tiers. First checkout sets the flag; subsequent checkouts skip the 14-day trial
- **Webhook guard**: `handleSubscriptionUpdated()` now ignores webhook events for non-current subscriptions, preventing stale duplicates from overwriting active subscription state
- **Duplicate cleanup**: `handleCheckoutSessionCompleted()` now cancels duplicate active/trialing subscriptions for the customer, keeping only the latest
- **Exported `deriveSubscriptionTypeFromPriceId`**: Used by the upgrade endpoint to map price IDs to tier names

## Test Evidence
- Backend unit tests: 12 passed, 0 failed (`stripeUpgrade.test.ts`)
- Existing stripe tests: 7 passed, 0 failed (`stripeSubscription.test.ts`)
- Tested as: backend service layer (mocked Stripe SDK)

## Files changed
- `backend/src/routes/stripe.ts` — New `/upgrade` endpoint + `has_used_trial` check on checkout
- `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts` — New `upgradeSubscription`, `cancelDuplicateSubscriptions`, `findActiveSubscription` methods + webhook guard + `has_used_trial` on checkout completion
- `backend/src/__tests__/stripeUpgrade.test.ts` — 12 new tests covering upgrade, trial gating, and webhook handling

## What was NOT tested
- End-to-end Stripe API integration (mocked SDK — real Stripe calls need test env)
- Proration amount accuracy (delegated to Stripe's calculation)
- Race condition: two concurrent upgrades for the same user
- Downgrade-specific proration behavior
- Multi-subscription edge case where user already has 3+ subscriptions from past bugs

## Related PRs
- Customer Portal: fix/stripe-upgrade-duplicates (frontend changes)
- Backend: this PR (standalone)

## Rollback
`git revert <merge-commit>` — the upgrade endpoint is additive. Removing it reverts to old behavior (checkout creates new subscription). No data migration needed.

title: fix: Stripe webhook retry + subscription field backfill
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Stripe webhook handler always returned HTTP 200, even on processing failures. This told Stripe "all good, don't retry" — so any transient failure (DynamoDB throttle, network blip) permanently lost the webhook. Additionally, `handleSubscriptionUpdated` never wrote `stripe_subscription_id` or `has_payment_method`, so monthly billing events couldn't backfill records where the checkout webhook failed.

Result: 6 paying customers (including sidd@datascoop.ai paying $99/mo since Dec 2025) had null `subscription_status` and `has_payment_method` in DynamoDB, showing as "bounced" in admin views despite active Stripe subscriptions.

## What this fixes (after)
- Webhooks return 500 on transient errors (Stripe retries for up to 3 days) and 200 on permanent errors (user not found)
- `handleSubscriptionUpdated` backfills `stripe_subscription_id` when null and always syncs `has_payment_method`
- New admin endpoint `POST /api/stripe/reconcile` for manual audits
- All 6 affected customer records manually fixed in prod DynamoDB

## How to test
1. Deploy to test env
2. Trigger a `customer.subscription.updated` webhook via Stripe CLI: `stripe trigger customer.subscription.updated`

title: fix: use self-profile lookup to detect disconnected Unipile accounts
body:
## Root cause

`account.getOne()` and `account.getAll()` from the Unipile SDK return `status=undefined` for both connected and disconnected LinkedIn accounts. The previous implementation read `item.status` from these responses, which was always falsy — so every account appeared as "OK" / "connected" regardless of actual session state.

The actual disconnection only surfaces when making a real LinkedIn API call (e.g. a profile lookup returns HTTP 401 with `errors/disconnected_account`).

## Fix

`isAccountConnected()` now:
1. Calls `account.getOne(accountId)` to get the account's own LinkedIn `publicIdentifier`
2. Performs a self-profile lookup (`GET /users/{publicIdentifier}`) — this returns 401 if the LinkedIn session is dead

`getStatusesForAccounts()` now delegates to `isAccountConnected()` in parallel instead of reading the unusable `item.status` field from `account.getAll()`.

## Verified

- `isAccountConnected('zSqd7St2Qfy-9RaX38Yxvg')` (Rui Wang, disconnected) → false
- `isAccountConnected('2LDFtVAPS1SpxeAqU54Miw')` (Fangfang Tan, connected) → true
- 126 tests pass across linkedInOutreach, siteWideUnipile, crmEnrichment, connectedAccounts

Services at rest consume ~3.6 GB (esbuild ×2, ts-node-dev, Playwright MCP, Notion MCP, Vite ×2, Claude process). Memory spikes during `npx tsc` (+2–4 GB), `npm test` (+1–2 GB), and hot reloads make it easy to exhaust 16 GB + 4 GB swap, causing OOM kills that destabilize sessions.

With 32 GB RAM, there's ~28 GB of headroom for all simultaneous workloads. The 8 GB swap backs up any remaining edge cases.

title: fix: View Live Site shows Vercel URL after subdomain is set
body:
## Summary
- **Root cause**: `customDomainUrl` was never written to `AW-LandingPages` in Rankai's case (and other historical records). The DB update in `POST /api/domains/subdomain` can silently be skipped (if `landingPageId` isn't sent) or fail without surfacing the failure. On reload, the GET /generated returned pages without `customDomainUrl`, so the frontend fell back to the Vercel URL.
- **Fix 1 (domains.ts)**: Wrap the `customDomainUrl` DB update in try/catch so a `ConditionalCheckFailed` or other DynamoDB error doesn't break the whole request. The Vercel subdomain was already configured successfully — we log the error and return 201 anyway.
- **Fix 2 (landingPageGeneration.ts)**: Enrich pages at listing time — for any page with a `vercelProjectId` but no `customDomainUrl` in `AW-LandingPages`, look up the most recent domain in `AW-CustomDomains` and populate it on-the-fly. This compensates for both historical records and any future DB update failures.

## Evidence
- `AW-CustomDomains` has `rankai.agentwebforms.com` (active, set 2026-04-02T17:30 UTC)
- All 7 `AW-LandingPages` records for Rankai have `customDomainUrl: null`
- nginx log confirms the Apr 2 17:30 POST returned 201 — Vercel got the domain, DB update was silently dropped
- Fix 2 (enrichment) was committed in a previous branch (`rui/subdomain-setup-not-working`) but never merged to main

title: fix: use --resume <session-id> in relay to maintain single Claude session
body:
## Problem
`claude --continue -p` always creates a new JSONL session, so follow-up prompts via the Notion relay lose all context from the initial `.claude-run.sh` task run.

## Fix
- **`user-data-dev-auto.sh`**: After the initial run, extract session ID from the JSONL and save to `.claude-session-id`
- **`test-env-access/server.js`**: Relay reads `.claude-session-id` and uses `--resume <id>` instead of `--continue`, keeping all turns in the same session. Falls back to `--continue` if the file doesn't exist.
- Relay also persists `session_id` from JSON output on each turn.

## Result
Initial task run + all follow-up relay prompts now share one Claude session JSONL, giving Claude full context throughout the conversation.

title: fix: subscription downgrades no longer incorrectly marked as canceled
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
When a subscription was downgraded by canceling the old sub and creating a new cheaper one, the `customer.subscription.deleted` webhook handler unconditionally set `subscription_status` to `"canceled"` and `subscriptionType` to `"Free"` — without checking if the customer had another active subscription. This caused GoaldenHour's subscription (and potentially other downgraded customers) to appear as "canceled" in the partner portal despite having an active subscription in Stripe.

## What this fixes (after)
`handleSubscriptionDeleted` now checks Stripe for remaining active/trialing subscriptions before marking the user as canceled. If another subscription exists (indicating a downgrade, not a cancellation), it syncs the user to that subscription's status, tier, and period end. Only genuine cancellations (no remaining active subs) set status to "canceled".

## How to test
1. In the Stripe test dashboard, create a customer with a "Complete" (Super Premium) subscription
2. Cancel that subscription and immediately create a new "Starter" (Basic) subscription for the same customer
3. Observe the webhook logs — should see "treating as downgrade, not cancellation"
4. **Expected**: User's `subscription_status` remains `"active"`, `subscriptionType` changes to `"Basic"`, `allowedPages` is updated to Basic tier pages
5. Verify in the partner portal (AdminDashboard) — the customer should NOT show as "Canceled"

### Genuine cancellation still works:
1. Cancel a customer's only subscription (no replacement)
2. **Expected**: User's `subscription_status` is set to `"canceled"`, `subscriptionType` is `"Free"`

## Edge cases to check
- Full cancellation still correctly sets status to "canceled" ✅ (tested)
- Downgrade from Super Premium to Basic ✅ (tested)
- Deletion when customer has a trialing (not active) replacement sub ✅ (tested)
- Stripe API failure during remaining-sub check — falls through to cancel (safe default)

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 5 passed, 0 failed (stripeDowngrade.test.ts)
- Tests cover: downgrade with active sub, downgrade with trialing sub, tier change verification, genuine cancellation, and price change via subscription update

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts` — `handleSubscriptionDeleted` now checks for remaining subs before canceling
- `backend/src/__tests__/stripeDowngrade.test.ts` — New test file with 5 tests

## Production data correction needed
GoaldenHour's user record in the `AW-Users` DynamoDB table needs manual correction:
- Set `subscription_status` to match the Stripe subscription status (likely `"active"`)
- Set `subscriptionType` to match the current Stripe price (check `stripe_customer_id` in Stripe dashboard)
- Set `stripe_subscription_id` to the current active subscription ID
- Alternatively, use the existing `/api/stripe/reconcile` admin endpoint to auto-fix all drifted users

**DO NOT touch production tables directly.** Use the admin reconcile endpoint or have the admin manually trigger it from the partner portal.

## What was NOT tested
- Production data correction for GoaldenHour (requires manual admin action)
- Race condition: if both `customer.subscription.deleted` and `checkout.session.completed` fire simultaneously for the same customer during a downgrade

No `invoice.payment_succeeded` handler in the Stripe webhook dispatcher. Monthly renewals and first payments had no positive confirmation loop -- the system relied entirely on `customer.subscription.updated` which doesn't always fire for payment events.

4. Send the same event for a user whose `stripe_subscription_id` is null

6. Send event with unknown `customer` ID
7. **Expected**: Warning logged, 200 returned, no DB update
