title: fix(stripe): phase 1 follow-ups — security + kill 14-day trial
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Post-merge senior review on Phase 1 Stripe Reconciliation (PRs #1260–#1267) flagged several security and correctness follow-ups: `/api/stripe/upgrade` accepted arbitrary `newPriceId` from the request body (malicious user could downgrade to any active price including legacy $1 test prices); `customers.search` interpolated emails into Stripe's search DSL without escaping `"` or `\` (attacker could link another user's saved card); `/api/stripe/reactivate-subscription` couldn't find trialing subs and crashed on null `current_period_end`; and `reconcileAllStripeUsers` clobbered the `"canceling"` pseudo-status during admin sweeps. Separately, the 14-day free trial is no longer part of the product.

## What this fixes (after)
Whitelists `newPriceId` against env-configured IDs, escapes email input before the Stripe search query, mirrors the cancel-subscription patterns (trialing fallback + defensive period_end read) on reactivate, preserves `"canceling"` in reconcile, and rips out the 14-day trial entirely. New users now pay on first checkout.

## How to test

### 1. Upgrade whitelist (Fix 1)
1. Log in as `test1@example.com` / `Test123!` on the test env.
2. Open browser devtools. Call `POST /api/stripe/upgrade` with body `{"newPriceId": "price_totally_made_up_999"}` and the user's bearer token.
3. **Expected**: 400 `{"error": "Invalid plan or price ID."}`.
4. Repeat with body `{"plan": "starter"}`.
5. **Expected**: 200 with `subscriptionType` set (normal upgrade flow, no 400).

### 2. Email escape (Fix 2)
1. Register a new account with email `test+"quote@example.com` (this requires direct DB / API creation because the signup form may reject it — use the admin panel or `curl` against `/api/auth/register`).
2. Log in as that user, hit `POST /api/stripe/create-checkout-session` with `{"plan": "starter"}`.
3. Check backend logs for the Stripe search query: `email:"test+\"quote@example.com"`.
4. **Expected**: 200, checkout session created, no Stripe API error, no customer linkage to anyone else.

### 3. Reactivate during trial (Fix 3a) and null period_end (Fix 3b)
1. Log in as `test@example.com` / `Test123!`, ensure they have a trialing sub in Stripe dashboard.
2. Call `POST /api/stripe/cancel-subscription`.
3. **Expected**: 200, `subscription_status = "canceling"` in DB.
4. Call `POST /api/stripe/reactivate-subscription`.
5. **Expected**: 200 with `cancel_at_period_end: false`. Before this fix, step 4 returned 404 because it only looked at `status=active`.
6. Bonus: if `current_period_end` is null on the returned sub, endpoint returns 200 with `current_period_end: null` instead of 500.

### 4. Reconcile preserves canceling (Fix 4)
1. Log in as admin (`ruiwangwarm@gmail.com` / `12345678`).
2. On a user that's currently `subscription_status: "canceling"` in DB (with cancel_at_period_end=true in Stripe), fire `POST /api/stripe/reconcile`.
3. **Expected**: user's `subscription_status` stays `"canceling"` (NOT flipped back to `"active"`).

### 5. Kill trial (Fix 5)
1. Wipe `test2@example.com` or create a brand-new user with no `has_used_trial` in DB.
2. Start checkout on `/settings?upgrade=1`.
3. **Expected**: Stripe Checkout loads with "Pay now" (no "14-day free trial"). Card is charged on submission — no 14-day grace period.

## Edge cases to check
- `newPriceId` with a typo that matches a valid Stripe price outside the whitelist → 400.
- Reactivate when both active AND trialing subs exist (unlikely, but the active wins — unchanged behavior).
- `customers.search` with a brand-new email containing only safe chars still finds existing customer (regression check).
- Admin `/reconcile` on a user whose Stripe sub truly went active (no cancel_at_period_end) correctly flips DB `canceling` → `active` (forward direction still works).

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 15 passed in stripeUpgrade.test.ts (+1 pre-existing skip, +1 pre-existing "Super Premium" naming failure unrelated to this PR). 9 passed in stripeSubscription.test.ts. 2 new reconcile tests pass.
- Baseline on harsha/dev: same set of stripe tests — 3 pre-existing failures (tier naming in upgrade test, 2 trial-gating tests that are now replaced). This PR replaces the 2 broken trial tests with 3 working ones (no-trial × 2 + whitelist × 2 + email escape × 1 + reactivate trialing × 1 + reactivate null period_end × 1 + reconcile canceling × 2).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Tested as: unit tests only (backend). End-to-end manual test-env run pending QA.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/routes/stripe.ts` — whitelist, email escape, reactivate fallback + defensive period_end, remove trial
- `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts` — effectiveStatus in reconcile, remove has_used_trial write
- `backend/src/__tests__/stripeUpgrade.test.ts` — no-trial tests, whitelist tests, email-escape test, reconcile tests
- `backend/src/__tests__/stripeSubscription.test.ts` — reactivate trialing + null period_end tests

## What was NOT tested
- Live Stripe API behavior — all tests use mocks. Trialing-fallback path and null-period_end defensive read need real Stripe verification via the test env.
- No manual DB inspection for existing `has_used_trial: true` values (they're harmless residue but we didn't backfill-clean).
- `seed-stripe-test-data.ts` still creates trialing subs for testing Stripe → DB reconcile. Not touched because it's a test-fixture script, not production code.

## Related PRs
- Backend (this repo): Phase 1 Stripe Reconciliation (merged): #1260, #1262, #1266, #1267
- Customer Portal: standalone

## Notion task
Surface in next sprint review.

title: fix(agent-mode): prevent orphaned user messages when worker restarts during ishare
body:
## Summary

- **Worker shutdown leaves orphaned user messages**: When the backend worker process shuts down while handling a request, the user message is saved to DynamoDB before the worker is called, but the error handler was explicitly skipping the assistant error-message write for `isWorkerShutdownError`. Users who reloaded the page after a worker restart would see their message with no response and no error feedback.

- **Fixed**: Removed `isWorkerShutdownError` from the skip-list in both `generateResponse` and `generateSharedResponse`. A specific "The server restarted while processing your request. Please send your message again." error message is now persisted as an assistant message so the orphaned user message always has a response.

- **Missing concurrent request guard on ishare**: `generateSharedResponse` was missing the `activeSessionGenerations` concurrency guard that `generateResponse` already had. Two concurrent POST requests could both save a user message and start competing worker jobs. Guard added.

## Root cause

Investigated production session `9c45904c` (ishare) where message idx=11 at 18:56 had no assistant response. Found the worker shutdown error at 14:15:54 in prod logs, and confirmed the code path that skips error message persistence for `isWorkerShutdownError`.

title: fix(stripe): schedule tier downgrades for period-end (Stripe Subscription Schedules)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
`/api/stripe/upgrade` called `subscriptions.update` with the cheaper price on downgrades, so Stripe issued `proration_behavior=create_prorations` and prorated the unused portion of the paid tier into an account-balance credit. On the customer's invoice this surfaced as a ~$299 "refund" line, triggering support tickets.

## What this fixes (after)
New `changeSubscriptionPrice()` routes by price delta:
- **Upgrade (pricier)** — immediate `subscriptions.update` with proration (unchanged).
- **Downgrade (cheaper)** — creates a Stripe `subscriptionSchedule` with 2 phases + `end_behavior: 'release'`. User keeps the paid tier until period end, then Stripe auto-switches. No proration, no credit line, clean ledger (same pattern Vercel/Linear/Stripe Billing use).

The `/upgrade` route returns a discriminator (`kind: 'upgrade_immediate' | 'downgrade_scheduled'`). For scheduled downgrades the DB is NOT updated — the current tier stays until the schedule fires, at which point our existing `customer.subscription.updated` webhook handler syncs state.

## How to test
1. As a **Pro** user on the test env, go to `/pricing`.
2. Click "Switch to Starter".
3. **Expected**: Confirm modal title reads "Schedule downgrade to Starter?" with body explaining "You'll keep your current plan until the end of the billing period, then automatically switch to Starter. No prorated charges or credits."
4. Click "Schedule downgrade".
5. **Expected**: Toast: "Scheduled! You'll keep your current plan until `<date>`, then switch to starter."
6. **Expected**: In Stripe dashboard, open the customer -> Subscriptions -> see an active subscription_schedule with 2 phases (current price through period end, then starter price).
7. **Expected**: `user.subscriptionType` in DynamoDB is still "Pro" — no DB write happened.
8. Now click "Upgrade to Pro" from a Starter account.
9. **Expected**: Toast reads "Successfully switched to Pro! Changes take effect immediately." — DB updates to Pro, Stripe subscription flipped to Pro price with proration.

## Edge cases to check
- **User already has a scheduled downgrade, clicks downgrade again**: `subscriptionSchedules.create({ from_subscription })` will fail with `subscription_schedule_already_exists` on the second call. Currently this surfaces as the generic "Failed to upgrade subscription." 500 from the route. Not a data-corruption risk (Stripe blocks the double-write) but the error message isn't friendly. Flagged for a follow-up PR — not critical because the UI already disables the action once the user is `canceling`, but multi-tier scheduled downgrades (Pro -> Starter while already Pro -> Free scheduled) would hit this.
- **User cancels the scheduled downgrade via Customer Portal**: Stripe's Customer Portal can release the schedule. Webhook will fire `subscription_schedule.released` which we do not currently handle; the subscription naturally stays on the current price (correct behavior), so no code needed.
- **`current_period_end` missing on the subscription**: function throws `Cannot schedule downgrade: no current_period_end` and the route returns 500. Unlikely in practice — every active sub has one — but defensively handled so we don't silently fall through to an immediate update.

## Test Evidence
- New `stripeChangeSubscriptionPrice.test.ts`: 3 passed, 0 failed (service-level routing + same-price no-op).
- Updated `stripeUpgrade.test.ts`: 23 passed, 0 failed (includes new route-level downgrade-scheduled test asserting `userDb.updateUser` is NOT called and `subscriptions.update` is NOT called on downgrades).
- `stripeBillingAnchor.test.ts`: 3 passed, 0 failed (existing `upgradeSubscription` still green — kept for back-compat with webhook handlers).
- Other stripe test failures seen in the suite (`stripeDowngrade.test.ts`, `lazySyncAdditiveOnly.test.ts`) are pre-existing on `harsha/dev` — confirmed by running the same tests on baseline before any changes. Tier name drift (`Super Premium` -> `Pro`), unrelated to this PR.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts` — new `changeSubscriptionPrice()` function (existing `stripeService.upgradeSubscription` kept for back-compat with webhook-adjacent callers).
- `backend/src/routes/stripe.ts` — `/upgrade` route now delegates to `changeSubscriptionPrice`, returns `kind` discriminator, skips DB write on `downgrade_scheduled`.
- `backend/src/__tests__/stripeChangeSubscriptionPrice.test.ts` — new service-level tests (3).
- `backend/src/__tests__/stripeUpgrade.test.ts` — updated for new response shape, added end-to-end downgrade-scheduled test.

## What was NOT tested
- Real Stripe API smoke test against the live test env (API-level, not unit). Needs a real Stripe test-mode customer + subscription — would be the QA loop's job.
- Schedule-already-exists error path (see Edge cases above).
- Webhook flow when the schedule fires and customer.subscription.updated comes in — relies on existing `handleSubscriptionUpdated` which is unchanged.
- Non-English locale for the "end of current period" date (`toLocaleDateString()` will format based on user's browser locale — correct but untested).

## Related PRs
- Customer Portal: [fix/pricing-scheduled-downgrade-copy](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/pull/new/fix/pricing-scheduled-downgrade-copy) — UI copy for the new `kind: downgrade_scheduled` response.

## Notion task
(none — ad-hoc fix in response to $299 prorated-credit UX issue)

title: fix(agent-mode): propagate original error through worker IPC to oncall alerts
body:
## Summary
- The real underlying error from the LLM/tool call was being swallowed when `generateMarketingResponse` wrapped it in a user-friendly message
- That wrapped message was the only thing sent back through the worker IPC, so oncall alerts showed "I apologize, but I encountered an error..." instead of the actual cause
- Now `originalMessage` is forwarded through worker → worker service → controller so both oncall alerts display the root cause error

## Root cause
`agentModeService.generateMarketingResponse` wraps all errors with a user-friendly message and stores the real error in `wrappedError.originalMessage`. But `generateMarketingResponseWorker.ts` only forwarded `error.message` (the wrapper) in the IPC payload — `originalMessage` was dropped. The worker service then reconstructed the error from that message string, losing the original.

## Changes
- `workers/generateMarketingResponseWorker.ts`: include `originalMessage` in IPC error payload
- `services/generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.ts`: preserve `originalMessage` on reconstructed error
- `controllers/agentModeController.ts`: surface `originalMessage` in both "Generate Response" and "Generate Shared Response" oncall alerts

## Test plan
- [ ] TypeScript compiles clean (`npx tsc --noEmit`)
- [ ] Existing agent mode tests pass
- [ ] Future oncall alerts for unknown errors will show "Original Error" field with the real LLM/API error message

title: feat(stripe): cache scheduledChange + cancel-scheduled-downgrade endpoint
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
When a user scheduled a downgrade via `/api/stripe/upgrade` (kind=`downgrade_scheduled`), the backend stored nothing about the pending change. `/auth/me` couldn't tell the UI a change was queued, and there was no way for the user to cancel the scheduled change short of clicking through the Stripe customer portal.

## What this fixes (after)
Caches the queued `subscription_schedule` on the user record, exposes it through `/auth/me`, and adds a dedicated cancel endpoint that releases the Stripe schedule + clears the cache. Webhook handlers for `subscription_schedule.{released,canceled,completed}` clear the cache on the way out so it never gets stale.

## How to test
1. As a Pro user on `test@example.com` / `Test123!`, POST `/api/stripe/upgrade` with `{ "plan": "starter" }`.
2. **Expected**: response `kind: "downgrade_scheduled"` + `effectiveAt` ISO string.
3. GET `/api/auth/me`.
4. **Expected**: the response includes `scheduledChange: { stripeScheduleId, toPriceId, toTier: "Starter", effectiveAt }`.
5. POST `/api/stripe/cancel-scheduled-downgrade`.
6. **Expected**: 200 `{ message: "Scheduled change canceled..." }`. Calling `/auth/me` again returns `scheduledChange: null`.
7. POST `/api/stripe/cancel-scheduled-downgrade` with no scheduled change on file.
8. **Expected**: 404 `{ error: "No scheduled change to cancel." }`.
9. Simulate `subscription_schedule.completed` webhook (or wait for the real one to fire at period-end).
10. **Expected**: `scheduledChange` on the user is cleared; the user's tier field still updates via the parallel `customer.subscription.updated` webhook.

## Edge cases to check
- Out-of-order webhook: user queues schedule A, cancels, queues schedule B. Late `.released` webhook for A arrives after B is cached — A's event does NOT clobber B. (Covered by unit test + guarded by a schedule-id match.)
- Stripe release fails: the cached `scheduledChange` is NOT cleared, so the user can retry.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 13 new tests in `stripeCancelScheduledDowngrade.test.ts` + updated the downgrade assertion in `stripeUpgrade.test.ts`. 30 stripe tests in the affected files pass. (Pre-existing failures in `stripeDowngrade.test.ts` / `lazySyncAdditiveOnly.test.ts` use old tier names "Basic"/"Super Premium" — unrelated to this PR; also fail on `harsha/dev`.)
- TypeScript: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/db.ts` — `scheduledChange` field on `User`
- `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts` — return schedule from `changeSubscriptionPrice`, add `handleSubscriptionScheduleEnded`
- `backend/src/routes/stripe.ts` — write `scheduledChange` on downgrade, new `/cancel-scheduled-downgrade` endpoint
- `backend/src/controllers/stripeController.ts` — wire the 3 webhook events
- `backend/src/__tests__/stripeCancelScheduledDowngrade.test.ts` — new
- `backend/src/__tests__/stripeUpgrade.test.ts` — updated downgrade assertion

## What was NOT tested
- The real Stripe webhook flow end-to-end against a live Stripe test account (dev env needed + webhook events enabled first — see Deploy-time action below).
- Playwright UX verification on `/settings` + `/pricing` (separate frontend PR lands this; Playwright is QA's job per the task spec).
- Concurrent cancel + webhook race (optimistic clear + webhook both try to clear the same field — both write `null`, outcome identical).

## Deploy-time action (human)
Enable these 3 webhook events on the Stripe dev + prod webhook endpoints:
`subscription_schedule.released`, `subscription_schedule.canceled`, `subscription_schedule.completed`.
Stripe → Developers → Webhooks → edit endpoint → tick the 3 boxes.

## Related PRs
- Customer Portal: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#636

Not filed — task came directly from Harsha.

title: Mega PR: harsha/dev → main — Stripe Phase 1 Reconciliation + scheduled downgrades
body:
## Sprint Review: 2026-04-22 — 9 PRs (Stripe Phase 1 Reconciliation)

**How to review**: Go through the testing plan below. Comment on this PR with fix/revert notes.
Anything you don't mention = approved to ship.

**Comment format**:
- `fix #NNN: what's wrong` — swarm will fix it
- `revert #NNN` — will be removed before shipping

All 9 sub-PRs in this review are Harsha-authored (`harshmoney123`). Rui-authored direct-to-main PRs (about 60 of them, e.g. #1264, #1265, #1268, #1270, #1272–#1274 and many more) were back-merged into `harsha/dev` today for conflict resolution but are **NOT** in the review scope below — they shipped independently to `main` earlier.

**Base**: `main` @ `4a4c4cb2` · **Head**: `harsha/dev` @ `d092cc4a`

### Summary

This mega PR ships **Stripe Phase 1 State Reconciliation** + completeness fixes + scheduled-downgrade UX. The underlying issue (surfaced 2026-04-22): users' `subscription_status` and `subscriptionType` could drift independently because multiple code paths wrote the fields without coordination, and the webhook handler had gaps. 9 PRs address:

- Lazy Stripe init (module-load race)
- Find-or-reuse Stripe customers by email (dedup + stale-ID recovery)
- Derive tier from subscription (not session) + fail loud on unknown price (kills the silent Super Premium fallback)
- Cancel endpoint null-period_end defensive read
- Webhook completeness: `canceling` pseudo-status, `customer.subscription.created`, `invoice.paid` alias
- New-sub guard bypass (so webhook-created subs can actually write)
- Kill the 14-day free trial + whitelist `newPriceId` + email-escape Stripe search + reactivate-during-trial + reconcile preserves `canceling`
- Schedule downgrades for period-end via Subscription Schedules (no prorated credits)
- Cache + cancel scheduled downgrades (new endpoint + new webhook handlers)

---

### Sub-PRs (grouped by theme, sorted by risk then priority)

#### Stripe Reconciliation — bootstrap + customer layer

##### PR #1258: fix(stripe): lazy-init Stripe client — fixes 'not configured correctly' on dev/test env
**Risk**: Low | **Type**: fix | **Files**: 1 | **Author**: harshmoney123

**What changed**: `routes/stripe.ts` initialized the Stripe SDK with a module-level const that captured `process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` at import time — before `server.ts` bootstrap loaded the secret from AWS Secrets Manager. Every `/api/stripe/*` request then returned "Stripe integration is not configured correctly" even though secrets were populated. Replaced the module const with a lazy `getStripe()` getter that reads `process.env` per-request and memoizes the client.

**How to test**:
1. Merge + wait for backend test env redeploy (or force sync via `test-env.sh sync`)
2. Log in as `testnewrandonb@test.com` / `123123` on test env (burned Free account)
3. Open Agent Mode → send any message → token-limit modal opens
4. Click **Upgrade to Starter** → redirects to `/checkout`
5. **Expected**: Stripe Checkout form loads. Enter test card `4242 4242 4242 4242` / any future expiry / any CVC → subscription starts → redirect to `/checkout/success`
6. Verify: reload `/settings/subscription` → Plan now shows Starter, Manage Billing button appears, `subscription_status=active`

**Edge cases**:
- Env never populates → `getStripe()` returns `null` → handlers fall through to "not configured" error path (no regression)
- Prod not affected (sets `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` directly in env, not Secrets Manager)

---

##### PR #1260: fix(stripe): verify customer exists + dedup by email before creating new one
**Risk**: Medium | **Type**: fix | **Files**: 1 | **Author**: harshmoney123

**What changed**: `/api/stripe/create-checkout-session` had two bugs. (1) A stale `stripe_customer_id` stored in the DB (deleted from Stripe dashboard, historical drift) would crash checkout with `"No such customer: 'cus_XYZ'"`. (2) When the DB had no customer ID, we called `stripe.customers.create` without checking whether a Stripe customer already existed for that email — causing duplicate customers to leak. Fix adds a two-step defensive block: verify existing DB ID via `stripe.customers.retrieve`, then fall back to `stripe.customers.search({ query: 'email:"..."' })` before creating new.

**How to test**:
1. Log in as `testnewrandonb@test.com` / `123123` on test env (account just had DB `stripe_customer_id` flipped to `cus_UNaBVqVQLbKdQQ`)
2. Go to `/pricing` → click "Start Free Trial" on Starter
3. **Expected**: Stripe embedded checkout renders with "Try Starter — 14 days free — then $199.00/mo" *(note: trial copy still shown here; the trial was killed in a later PR #1271, so verify after all merges)*
4. **Negative path — stale DB ID**: use admin endpoint to set `stripe_customer_id` to a bogus deleted ID like `cus_deleted_test_1`. Retry step 2. **Expected**: checkout still succeeds (Step 1 detects `deleted: true` / 404, Step 2 searches by email, reuses the live customer)
5. **Duplicate prevention**: on a fresh account, click Starter twice. **Expected**: only ONE Stripe customer created
6. Full suite: `npm test`

**Edge cases**:
- Live-in-prod-but-not-test customer ID → Step 1 gets 404 → Step 2 searches → creates test-mode one
- Email with special chars → `query:"email:\"${userEmail}\""` quoting handles it (email-escape added in #1271)
- Race on concurrent checkouts → both runs may create a customer; steady-state orphans prevented; proper fix needs a lock (out of scope)

---

##### PR #1261: fix(stripe): derive tier from subscription, remove Super Premium fallback
**Risk**: Medium | **Type**: fix | **Files**: 1 | **Author**: harshmoney123

**What changed**: Every successful Stripe checkout was landing users in `"Super Premium"` tier regardless of plan. Two chained bugs: (1) `deriveSubscriptionType(session)` read `session.line_items.data[0].price.id` but the `checkout.session.completed` webhook does NOT expand `line_items` by default — it was `undefined`. (2) The fallback silently promoted users to Super Premium (internal-only tier). Fix derives tier from the subscription (already fetched in the handler for `status`/`current_period_end`), removes Super Premium from the paid mapping, and returns `null` on unknown price (handler preserves prior tier + loud `console.error`).

Tier mapping: Starter price → `"Basic"` tier, Complete (Pro) price → `"Pro"` tier.

**How to test**:
1. Log in as `testnewrandonb@test.com` / `123123` on test env
2. Go to `/pricing` → click Start Free Trial on Starter → complete Stripe checkout with test card `4242 4242 4242 4242`
3. **Expected**: webhook fires → derives Starter price → maps to `"Basic"` tier → user record: `subscriptionType: "Basic", subscription_status: "trialing", has_payment_method: true`
4. `/settings` → Subscription card → shows Basic tier + Trial badge
5. **Negative test — unknown price**: temporarily set `STRIPE_STARTER_PRICE_ID=price_fake_123` in env. Retry checkout. **Expected**: webhook logs `[STRIPE] Unknown priceId 'price_...' ... Not writing subscriptionType.` User's prior subscriptionType is preserved. Restore env var.
6. `npm test`

**Edge cases**:
- Subscription retrieve fails → falls back to `session.line_items` → probably null → tier preserved (safe failure)
- `STRIPE_*_PRICE_ID` env vars unset → falls to unknown-price branch → loud log

---

#### Stripe Reconciliation — endpoint + webhook correctness

##### PR #1262: fix(stripe): cancel-subscription survives null current_period_end
**Risk**: Low | **Type**: fix | **Files**: 1 | **Author**: harshmoney123

**What changed**: `/api/stripe/cancel-subscription` crashed with `Error canceling subscription: Invalid time value` → HTTP 500, blocking every paid→Free transition. Root cause: `new Date(updated.current_period_end * 1000).toISOString()` assumed the field was always a number, but Stripe 2025-05-28.basil moved `current_period_end` to `items.data[0].current_period_end` AND trialing subs have `null` in both places. Fix: read from both locations, fall back to `null`, only write the DB field when a timestamp exists.

**How to test**:
1. On test env, log in as a user with an active trialing subscription
2. `POST /api/stripe/cancel-subscription`
3. **Expected**: `{ message: 'Subscription will be canceled at the end of the billing period.', cancel_at_period_end: true, current_period_end: null }`
4. Verify DB: `subscription_status: 'canceling'`, `current_period_end` unchanged from before (or set if Stripe provides one)
5. Then let Stripe fire `customer.subscription.deleted` at period end → webhook handler clears the fields

**Edge cases**: none beyond happy path.

---

##### PR #1266: fix(stripe): webhook completeness — canceling status, created handler, invoice.paid
**Risk**: Low | **Type**: fix | **Files**: ~2 | **Author**: harshmoney123

**What changed**: Three webhook gaps found during the 8-step tier-transition smoke test:
1. **Canceling overwritten** — Stripe fires `customer.subscription.updated` when `cancel_at_period_end` flips true; handler blindly copied back `subscription.status` (`active`/`trialing`). UI showed `Active` immediately after cancel. Fix: derive `effectiveStatus = canceling` when `cancel_at_period_end && status ∈ {active, trialing}`.
2. **`customer.subscription.created` unhandled** — admin/API/reconciliation paths fire this directly; previously left DB stale. Now routed through `handleSubscriptionUpdated`.
3. **`invoice.paid` unhandled** — Stripe's current event name; monthly renewals weren't syncing. Switch now accepts both `invoice.paid` and the legacy `invoice.payment_succeeded`.

**How to test**:
1. Cancel a paid sub → UI shows 'Canceling' (not 'Active') — see CP #633 for UI
2. Create sub via Stripe API (not checkout flow) → fires `customer.subscription.created` → DB auto-syncs to correct tier
3. Monthly renewal payment → `invoice.paid` event → payment history records

**Edge cases**: none — all happy-path webhook completeness.

---

##### PR #1267: fix(stripe): bypass stale-webhook guard for customer.subscription.created
**Risk**: Low | **Type**: fix | **Files**: 2 | **Author**: harshmoney123

**What changed**: Follow-up to #1266. When `customer.subscription.created` fired for a BRAND NEW sub, `handleSubscriptionUpdated` returned early on the `stripe_subscription_id !== subscription.id` guard because the DB still carried the old (canceled) sub ID. Fix: add `options.isNew` parameter; the `customer.subscription.created` case passes `{ isNew: true }` which bypasses the guard and writes `stripe_subscription_id` unconditionally. Normal `.updated` events keep the guard.

**How to test**:
1. Customer has `DB.stripe_subscription_id = sub_OLD` (canceled)
2. `stripe.subscriptions.create` for same customer with a new price → fires `customer.subscription.created`
3. Webhook runs with `isNew=true` → bypasses guard → writes new `sub_id` + `subscriptionType` + `status`
4. **Expected**: DB reflects the new active sub

**Edge cases**: none — this only affects the `.created` path which was broken for any user with prior canceled subs.

---

#### Stripe Reconciliation — security + trial removal

##### PR #1271: fix(stripe): phase 1 follow-ups — security + kill 14-day trial
**Risk**: Medium | **Type**: fix | **Files**: 4 | **Author**: harshmoney123

**What changed**: Post-merge review flagged several correctness / security follow-ups to Phase 1:
- `/api/stripe/upgrade` accepted arbitrary `newPriceId` from body → malicious user could downgrade to any active price (legacy $1 test prices, etc.). Now whitelisted against env-configured IDs.
- `customers.search` interpolated email into Stripe's search DSL without escaping `"` / `\` → attacker could link another user's saved card. Now escaped.
- `/api/stripe/reactivate-subscription` couldn't find trialing subs + crashed on null `current_period_end`. Mirrored cancel-subscription's defensive patterns.
- `reconcileAllStripeUsers` clobbered `"canceling"` pseudo-status during admin sweeps. Now preserves it.
- **14-day free trial removed entirely.** New users now pay on first checkout.

**How to test**:
1. **Upgrade whitelist**: Log in as `test1@example.com` / `Test123!`. Via devtools, `POST /api/stripe/upgrade` with `{"newPriceId": "price_totally_made_up_999"}` + bearer token. **Expected**: 400 `{"error": "Invalid plan or price ID."}`. Repeat with `{"plan": "starter"}` — **Expected**: 200 normal upgrade.
2. **Email escape**: Register `test+"quote@example.com` via admin/curl, log in as them, hit `/api/stripe/create-checkout-session` with `{"plan":"starter"}`. **Expected**: 200, checkout session created, no Stripe error; backend log shows `email:"test+\"quote@example.com"`.
3. **Reactivate during trial**: Log in as `test@example.com` / `Test123!` with trialing sub. `POST /api/stripe/cancel-subscription` → 200, `subscription_status = "canceling"`. Then `POST /api/stripe/reactivate-subscription` → **Expected**: 200 with `cancel_at_period_end: false` (used to be 404 — only looked at `status=active`).
4. **Null period_end on reactivate**: If the returned sub has null `current_period_end`, endpoint returns 200 with `current_period_end: null` instead of 500.
5. **Reconcile preserves canceling**: Log in as admin (`ruiwangwarm@gmail.com` / `12345678`). On a user that's `subscription_status: "canceling"`, fire `POST /api/stripe/reconcile`. **Expected**: status stays `"canceling"` (NOT flipped to `"active"`).
6. **Kill trial**: Wipe `test2@example.com` or create new user with no `has_used_trial`. Start checkout on `/settings?upgrade=1`. **Expected**: Stripe Checkout loads with "Pay now" (no 14-day free trial). Card charged on submission.

**Edge cases**:
- `newPriceId` typo matching a valid Stripe price outside whitelist → 400
- Reactivate when both active AND trialing subs exist — active wins (unchanged)
- Admin `/reconcile` on user whose Stripe sub truly went active → correctly flips `canceling` → `active`

---

#### Stripe Reconciliation — scheduled downgrades

##### PR #1277: fix(stripe): schedule tier downgrades for period-end (Stripe Subscription Schedules)
**Risk**: Medium | **Type**: fix | **Files**: 4 | **Author**: harshmoney123

**What changed**: `/api/stripe/upgrade` used to call `subscriptions.update` with the cheaper price on downgrades → Stripe issued `proration_behavior=create_prorations` → user's invoice showed a ~$299 "refund" line → support tickets. New `changeSubscriptionPrice()` routes by price delta:
- **Upgrade (pricier)** — immediate `subscriptions.update` with proration (unchanged).
- **Downgrade (cheaper)** — creates Stripe `subscriptionSchedule` with 2 phases + `end_behavior: 'release'`. User keeps the paid tier until period end, then Stripe auto-switches. No proration, no credit line.

Route returns `kind: 'upgrade_immediate' | 'downgrade_scheduled'`. Scheduled downgrades DO NOT write DB — current tier stays until the schedule fires, at which point the existing `customer.subscription.updated` webhook syncs state.

**How to test**:
1. As a **Pro** user on test env, go to `/pricing`
2. Click "Switch to Starter"
3. **Expected**: Confirm modal reads "Schedule downgrade to Starter?" with body "You'll keep your current plan until the end of the billing period, then automatically switch to Starter. No prorated charges or credits."
4. Click "Schedule downgrade"
5. **Expected**: Toast: "Scheduled! You'll keep your current plan until `<date>`, then switch to starter."
6. **Expected**: Stripe dashboard shows an active `subscription_schedule` with 2 phases (current price → period end, then starter price)
7. **Expected**: `user.subscriptionType` in DynamoDB is still "Pro" — no DB write happened
8. Now click "Upgrade to Pro" from a Starter account
9. **Expected**: Toast reads "Successfully switched to Pro! Changes take effect immediately." — DB updates to Pro, Stripe subscription flipped with proration

**Edge cases**:
- User already has a scheduled downgrade → second `subscriptionSchedules.create` fails with `subscription_schedule_already_exists` → generic 500 "Failed to upgrade subscription" (flagged for follow-up, UI already guards in #636)
- User cancels via Stripe Customer Portal → Stripe fires `subscription_schedule.released` (now handled in #1279)
- Missing `current_period_end` → `Cannot schedule downgrade: no current_period_end` throw → defensive route-level 500 (doesn't silently fall through to immediate update)

---

##### PR #1279: feat(stripe): cache scheduledChange + cancel-scheduled-downgrade endpoint
**Risk**: Low | **Type**: feat | **Files**: 6 | **Author**: harshmoney123

**What changed**: `/auth/me` couldn't tell the UI that a schedule was queued, and there was no way to cancel short of the Stripe customer portal. This PR caches the queued `subscription_schedule` on the user record, exposes it through `/auth/me`, adds a `/api/stripe/cancel-scheduled-downgrade` endpoint that releases the Stripe schedule + clears the cache, and wires `subscription_schedule.{released,canceled,completed}` webhook handlers to clear the cache so it never gets stale.

**How to test**:
1. As Pro user (`test@example.com` / `Test123!`), `POST /api/stripe/upgrade` with `{"plan":"starter"}`
2. **Expected**: response `kind: "downgrade_scheduled"` + `effectiveAt` ISO string
3. `GET /api/auth/me` → **Expected**: includes `scheduledChange: { stripeScheduleId, toPriceId, toTier: "Starter", effectiveAt }`
4. `POST /api/stripe/cancel-scheduled-downgrade` → **Expected**: 200 `{ message: "Scheduled change canceled..." }`. Subsequent `/auth/me` returns `scheduledChange: null`
5. `POST /api/stripe/cancel-scheduled-downgrade` with no scheduled change on file → **Expected**: 404 `{ error: "No scheduled change to cancel." }`
6. Simulate `subscription_schedule.completed` webhook (or wait for real one at period-end) → **Expected**: `scheduledChange` on user is cleared; tier still updates via parallel `customer.subscription.updated` webhook

**Edge cases**:
- Out-of-order: queue A → cancel → queue B → late `.released` webhook for A — does NOT clobber B (schedule-id match guard + unit test)
- Stripe release fails → cache NOT cleared → user can retry

---

### High-Risk Items — Test these first

- **#1260 — customer dedup**: Medium risk because it adds a defensive search-by-email that touches the customer creation hot path for every new checkout. Pre-existing behavior (create-only) is preserved when no email match; regression would surface as "new customer should have been created but reused an old one". Rollback: `git revert <merge-commit>` on `harsha/dev`.
- **#1261 — tier derivation**: Medium risk because this is the money path. Wrong derivation → wrong tier → wrong allowance. Mitigation: returns `null` on unknown price rather than a silent promotion; preserves existing tier on ambiguity. Rollback: `git revert`.
- **#1271 — security + kill trial**: Medium risk because it touches the `/upgrade`, `/reactivate`, and `/reconcile` endpoints and removes the trial gate entirely. Mitigation: tests cover whitelist, email-escape, reactivate-trialing, null-period-end, reconcile-canceling. Rollback: `git revert` — restores trial + previously open price-ID acceptance.
- **#1277 — scheduled downgrades**: Medium risk because it introduces Stripe Subscription Schedules (a separate Stripe primitive). Mitigation: only triggers on downgrade (cheaper price delta); upgrades unchanged. Rollback: `git revert` — restores immediate downgrade with proration (the $299-credit bug).

### Test Status

- `harsha/dev` vitest: 2768 passed, 2 pre-existing failures (`PricingUpgrade.test.tsx` success-message regex, `Settings.test.tsx` Emma Setup copy drift) — confirmed present on `harsha/dev` baseline before today's changes, unrelated.
- Backend Stripe suite: 30+ new tests added across `stripeUpgrade.test.ts`, `stripeSubscription.test.ts`, `stripeChangeSubscriptionPrice.test.ts`, `stripeCancelScheduledDowngrade.test.ts`. 0 new failures introduced.
- Playwright QA passes (documented on individual PRs): #1277 (scheduled downgrade), #1279 + CP #636 (scheduled-change UX).

### What was NOT tested

- **Period-end activation of scheduled downgrades** — Stripe schedule correctly configured (phases 0 & 1 verified) but actual May 22 firing can't be fast-forwarded in test mode.
- **Real prod checkout with real card** — test env Stripe test-mode only.
- **Invoice.paid webhook on real renewal cycle** — signature handling tested, end-to-end renewal flow not wired.
- **Concurrent checkout race** — per-user lock out of scope for #1260.
- **`has_used_trial` DB residue** — harmless, not backfill-cleaned per #1271.
- **`seed-stripe-test-data.ts`** — still creates trialing subs (test-fixture script, not production).

### Prod deploy actions (Stripe dashboard — before merging this mega PR)

Before merging this mega PR to `main`, Harsha should enable these 3 webhook events on the prod endpoint `api.agentweb.pro/api/stripe/webhook`:
- `subscription_schedule.released`
- `subscription_schedule.canceled`
- `subscription_schedule.completed`

Stripe → Developers → Webhooks → edit endpoint → tick the 3 boxes. Without these, the `scheduledChange` cache in #1279 won't auto-clear when Stripe fires the terminal events. Current behavior without them: cache goes stale after the schedule fires, UI shows "Scheduled to change" forever until the parallel `customer.subscription.updated` webhook + cache-clear endpoint handle it. Non-blocking (defense-in-depth) but recommended.

### Rollback

- **Single sub-PR**: `git revert <merge-commit>` on `harsha/dev`
- **Whole mega PR**: `git revert -m 1 <mega-merge-sha>` on `main`

title: feat(knowledge-base): date filtering and pagination for list_knowledge_base_files

## Summary

- Adds `modified_after`, `modified_before`, `limit`, `offset`, and `kb_type` parameters to `list_knowledge_base_files` so Emma can filter Google Drive files by date range and type without loading all 100+ files into context
- Google Drive date filters are pushed down to the Drive API (`modifiedTime >= 'date'`), results sorted newest-first; pagination slices the result

title: fix(tests): align tier-name assertions with Starter/Pro rename (PR #1261)

## Risk: Low | Priority: High (mega PR #1280 blocker)

## What was wrong (before)
PR #1261 renamed the Stripe price → tier derivation from the legacy
\"Basic\"/\"Super Premium\" names to \"Starter\"/\"Pro\" so the tier name
written to the user record matches what the customer saw on the pricing
page. Four test files still asserted the old names and were logged as
pre-existing failures during the Phase 1 mega PR senior review. They
now block mega PR #1280's CI.

## What this fixes (after)
Updates 4 test files to expect the current tier names. **Zero production
code changes** — `deriveSubscriptionTypeFromPriceId` in
`backend/src/services/stripeService.ts:910` has been correct since
PR #1261 merged.

## How to test

4. `npm test` (full backend suite)

   the 12 previously-failing tests in the `backend` job should be green.

title: fix(crm): CRM page crash fix for large lead accounts (Murray)
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause:** The `contactDedupService` was loading all lead pages across all lists in parallel with no memory cap. Murray's account has 132k and 39k lead lists, causing ~250k rows to load simultaneously → Node.js OOM crash. When the backend crashed, InboxView's fallback path fired parallel per-list requests, cascading into DynamoDB throttling.
- Added a `maxRawLeads` cap (default 50k) distributed evenly across lists, with lists sorted by `updatedAt` desc so recently-active lists get priority within the cap budget.
- Added release note for 2026-04-23.

- [ ] All 465 test suites pass (7,148 tests)
- [ ] Coverage: statements 99.22%, branches 95.73%, functions 98.18%, lines 99.28% — all ≥ 95%

title: fix(agent-mode): 403 loop on /session/:id/progress under admin delegation
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
When an admin used delegate access to inspect a customer, every poll of \`/api/agent-mode/session/:id/progress\` returned **403**. Since the UI polls this endpoint continuously while an agent-mode message is generating, the chat appeared to hang forever under impersonation. Repro: prod nginx log for \`Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3\` on 2026-04-23 between 23:52 and 23:55 UTC — 26 consecutive 403s across four session IDs while Harsha was impersonating \`eric@sentriq.io\`.

**Root cause**: the ACL check was \`session.userId !== req.user.userId\`. Under delegation \`req.user.userId\` is the TARGET customer (per \`middleware/auth.ts:56-77\`), so any session shown in the admin's UI that was actually admin-owned (which happens whenever the session list bridges the admin's own sessions and the target's) fell through to 403 instead of streaming SSE progress.

## What this fixes (after)
Allow a delegated admin to read sessions owned by either the target (primary path, unchanged) OR the admin's own \`userId\` exposed via \`req.delegateInfo.adminUserId\`. Non-delegated strangers still 403 — the new path is gated on \`delegateInfo.isDelegated === true\`.

## How to test
1. Log in as admin (\`test@example.com\`). On the test env: \`http://\${TEST_IP}:5174/login\`.
2. Go to partner portal → Users → find \`eric@sentriq.io\` → "Delegate Access".
3. Browser tab opens as Eric. Navigate to Agent Mode → open an existing in-flight session OR start a new message.
4. **Expected (before fix)**: Network tab shows \`GET /api/agent-mode/session/<id>/progress\` returning **403** on a loop; chat appears stuck.
5. **Expected (after fix)**: \`/progress\` returns **200** and streams \`text/event-stream\`; chat progresses normally.
6. Regression check: as a different customer, try to hit \`/api/agent-mode/session/<someone-else's-id>/progress\` — still 403.

## Test Evidence
- \`backend/src/__tests__/agentModeController.progress.test.ts\`: 16 passed, 0 failed. Three new tests cover delegated-admin-reads-own-session (allow), delegated-admin-reads-target-session (allow, regression guard), delegated-admin-reads-stranger's-session (still 403).
- \`npx tsc\` clean on backend.

## Files changed
- \`backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts\` — loosen the 403 check in \`getProgress\` to also permit \`delegateInfo.adminUserId\` ownership
- \`backend/src/__tests__/agentModeController.progress.test.ts\` — 3 new tests

## What was NOT tested
- End-to-end SSE streaming through delegation against the test env (that's the Harsha test above). The Jest tests assert the 403 short-circuit is gone and SSE setup is attempted — real SSE behavior should be validated live.

## Related PRs
- Frontend: https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/pull/645 (upgrade CTA silent-failure + stale trial copy). Frontend fix addresses the customer-visible upgrade path; this backend fix addresses admin impersonation observability.

## Rollback
Single commit — \`git revert b523abf1\` on \`harsha/dev\`.

title: feat(onboarding-v2): Phase 1 — brand build status state machine + API
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Brand generation was synchronous/blocking. Onboarding v2 Phase 1 needs it to be async so the user can answer Phase 2 questions while brand builds in parallel (the whole "latency hiding" mechanism depends on this).

No client-visible signal for when a build is in progress vs done, and no latency instrumentation.

## What this fixes (after)
- State machine on the User record (`brandBuildStatus` + `startedAt` / `completedAt` / `durationMs` / `error`)
- Thin REST surface the frontend polls: `POST /api/onboarding/brand-build/start`, `GET /api/onboarding/brand-build/status`, `POST /api/onboarding/brand-build/fail`
- Ready-patch hooks in the two existing `brandGuidelines` write paths (`routes/brand.ts` + `agentModeService`), so completion + latency are recorded without re-architecting the brand pipeline
- Pure service (`brandBuildStatusService`) for state transitions + metrics logging

Paired with the frontend PR (same branch name in customer-portal repo) which renders the "Brand: building / ready" pill and handles polling.

## How to test
1. `cd agentweb && npm run test:run -- src/__tests__/brandBuildStatusService.test.ts src/__tests__/brandBuildRoute.test.ts`
2. **Expected**: 22/22 tests pass (13 unit + 9 integration)
3. Start backend locally, authenticated as any user
4. `curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/onboarding/brand-build/start -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` → **Expected**: `{status: "running", startedAt: "..."}`
5. `curl http://localhost:3001/api/onboarding/brand-build/status -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` → **Expected**: returns same running state
6. Save brand guidelines via the existing `/api/brand` route → **Expected**: status flips to `ready`, `durationMs` populated
7. `GET /api/onboarding/brand-build/status` again → **Expected**: `{status: "ready", completedAt: "...", durationMs: <ms>}`

- Concurrent `/start` calls for same user → idempotent, single running job
- Status poll after build completed hours ago → returns stable "ready" state
- `/fail` after `/start` → transitions to `failed` with error reason, prevents duplicate `ready` flips

## What was wrong (before)
Phase 1 (PR #1298) persists a narrow set of per-User onboarding events (`goal_selected`, `brand_submitted`, `channel_connected`, etc.) but (a) the allowlist is too narrow for the full Onboarding v2 event stream, and (b) nothing writes the event log to the matched Lead row, so Fangfang has to cross-reference User records manually and Emma can't reason over onboarding behavior at the Lead level.

## What this fixes (after)

Extends `ALLOWED_ONBOARDING_EVENTS` with 11 new event names (Phase 2): `channel_selected`, `channels_skipped`, `icp_selected`, `value_prop_edited`, `ads_generated`, `ads_regenerated`, `welcome_offer_shown`, `welcome_offer_outcome`, `brand_build_status`, `onboarding_abandoned`, `deviation`. Every Phase 1 event still validates.
2. New `onboardingLeadSync.mirrorOnboardingEventToLead` service — after writing to the User record, fire-and-forget mirrors the full event log + derived stage + deviation count to the matched Lead row in the founders@ "AgentWeb Signups" list. Creates the Lead if missing (handles pre-existing users and signup race conditions).
3. New `crmDb.updateLeadOnboardingAnalytics` DynamoDB helper — atomic update of `onboardingEvents`, `onboardingStage`, `onboardingDeviationCount` on the Lead row.
4. `POST /api/onboarding/events` wiring — calls the mirror after the User write, wrapped in `.catch(() => {})` so the Lead path can never fail the user-facing request.

2. Navigate to `/onboarding-v2`.
3. Pick a goal (e.g. Paid Ads). Type a freeform question into the chat (anything that is NOT a button/form submit — e.g. "what about ecommerce?").
4. Complete brand, skip data, skip channels.
5. **Expected**: In DevTools Network tab, each step fires `POST /api/onboarding/events` with the matching event name and 200 responses.
6. Hit `GET /api/onboarding/events/me` with the logged-in token.
7. **Expected**: response has `onboardingEvents` with `goal_selected`, `deviation`, `brand_submitted`, `data_skipped`, `channels_skipped` entries; `onboardingStage` is set.
8. As admin (`test@example.com` / `Test123!`), inspect the Lead row in the founders@ Signups list for that email.
9. **Expected**: Lead has `onboardingEvents` array mirroring the User's, `onboardingStage`, and `onboardingDeviationCount >= 1`.

- Users who signed up before the mirror existed — first onboarding event auto-creates the Lead row rather than no-op'ing.
- Lead-mirror failure (founders list missing, DynamoDB throttle): the User POST still returns 200 and the UI advances normally.

title: feat(onboarding-v2): Phase 4 — ad gen status state machine + variants backend
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Onboarding v2 Phase 4 — the "aha moment" where Emma generates 3 real ad creatives for the user's business — had no async state machine backing it. Without a persisted status, the UI couldn't show a progress pill or re-render variants on reload.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds the Phase 4 foundation: a separate `adGenStatus` state machine on the User record (`generating → ready | failed`), a `/api/onboarding/ad-gen/*` REST surface the UI polls, and persisted `adGenVariants` so a page reload shows the exact 3 variants the LLM returned — no re-generation on refresh.

Mirrors the Phase 1 brand-build pattern but with a separate axis (the two runs are concurrent during Phase 3→4 and have different timeout budgets — brand ~90s, ad gen ~3min for image + copy).

**Not in this PR** (intentional follow-up slice): the actual LLM invocation that runs the "B2B lead gen ad" work plan prompts. Per the phase task body, those prompts MUST be reused from DynamoDB `AW-WorkPlans` — that wiring lands once Phase 3 (ICP + value prop selection) is merged so we can pass the picked ICP into the ad-gen call.

## How to test
1. Start backend: `cd backend && npm run dev`
2. Log in as `test@example.com` / `Test123!` to get a JWT.
3. `POST /api/onboarding/ad-gen/start` with the token.
   - **Expected**: 200 with `{ status: { adGenStatus: "generating", inFlight: true, ... } }`

title: fix(crm): improve LinkedIn URL fidelity in lead enrichment
body:
## Summary

Investigation of why LinkedIn URL fidelity was <30% for enriched lead lists uncovered three root causes, all fixed here:

**1. Existing LinkedIn URLs being overwritten with "Unknown"**
- Enrichment was bypassing the existing URL check when `isEnrichingLinkedin=true`, then the LLM returned "Unknown" with no context, destroying valid URLs already in the database.
- Fix: Always try `get-profile` on the existing URL first (it's almost always correct). Also pass the existing URL in LLM context as a fallback even if the Unipile call fails.

**2. "Unknown"/"N/A" placeholder values being written back to DB**
- `splitFields()` was persisting LLM placeholder outputs as real values, overwriting good data.
- Fix: `splitFields()` now skips any value that is empty, "Unknown", or "N/A".

**3. Unipile search skipping leads with names only in `customFields`**
- For leads imported from sources like webinar platforms (e.g. Every), names are in `customFields.first_name` / `customFields.last_name` rather than standard `firstName` / `lastName`. The search-people lookup requires `name && company`, but with empty standard fields the name was `""` so the search never ran.
- Fix: Name/company resolution now falls back to `customFields.first_name`, `customFields.last_name`, `customFields.company_name`.

## Test plan
- [ ] All 75 existing `crmEnrichmentService` tests pass
- [ ] 5 new `splitFields` tests cover Unknown/N/A/empty rejection
- [ ] 2 new `execute` tests cover existing-URL preservation when Unipile returns nothing
- [ ] Browser verified: enrichment on `list_1777036456882_qyvoil5rf` processed 115/115 leads with 0 failures (previously leads would have their LinkedIn URLs overwritten with "Unknown")

title: fix(agent-mode): fall back to adAccount when Meta connected account is absent
body:
## Root cause

When a user's Meta Marketing **connected account is removed** (e.g. `connected_accounts: []`), but `user.adAccount` is still populated (e.g. `"883347640787043"`), `getMetaCredentials()` immediately threw:

> "Meta Ads account is not connected."

This broke `call_meta_ads_insights_api`, `call_meta_marketing_api`, and `list_meta_ads_campaigns` for users managed via the agency/admin pattern — where credentials come from a centralized Secrets Manager token rather than a per-user OAuth connection.

The session that surfaced this: `067533c0-b2a7-4649-ba01-02c1a79d96cf` (Waldium Meta Ads scheduled report). The user (`1a9a40c5-…`) has `adAccount: "883347640787043"` and `connected_accounts: []`.

## Fix

In `getMetaCredentials()`, before throwing the "not connected" error, check whether `user.adAccount` is set. If it is, fall back to that account ID + `getMetaAccessToken()` from Secrets Manager — the same pattern already used by `getMetaAdsMetrics`.

- Connected account present → use it (no change)
- No connected account, `adAccount` set → fall back to `adAccount` + Secrets Manager token
- No connected account, no `adAccount` → throw as before

## Test plan
- [x] 8 new tests in `agentModeService.metaCredentialsFallback.test.ts` covering the fallback path, edge cases, and priority of connected accounts over the fallback
- [x] All 252 existing Meta tests still pass
- [x] `npx tsc` clean

## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
PR #1300 shipped the Phase 4 state machine + REST endpoints but explicitly deferred the actual LLM invocation:
> Not in this PR (intentional follow-up slice): the actual LLM invocation that runs the "B2B lead gen ad" work plan prompts.
That meant \`/ad-gen/start\` flipped a status flag with no motor behind it — \`/status\` would forever report \`generating\`, never flipping to \`ready\`.

## What this fixes (after)
Ships the missing motor. \`POST /ad-gen/start\` now:
1. Flips \`adGenStatus\` to \`generating\` and returns the snapshot immediately.
2. Kicks off a background Bedrock/Claude call that projects brand + ICP + channel + ad goal out of the User record, asks for 3 variants with a tight performance-marketing prompt, and patches the User with \`adGenReadyPatch(..., variants)\` on success or \`adGenFailedPatch(msg)\` on failure.

The UI polls \`/status\` the same way it did before — no client-side changes needed for this PR. The Phase 4 UI is a separate PR on the customer-portal side.

## How to test
1. Run backend locally: \`cd backend && npm run dev\`
2. Log in as \`test@example.com\` / \`Test123!\` to get a JWT.
3. \`POST /api/onboarding/ad-gen/start\` with the token.
   - **Expected**: 200 with \`status.adGenStatus === "generating"\` and \`inFlight: true\`.
4. Wait ~10-20s, then \`GET /api/onboarding/ad-gen/status\`.
   - **Expected**: \`status.adGenStatus === "ready"\`, \`adGenVariants.length === 3\`, each variant has \`id\`, \`headline\`, \`primaryText\`, \`cta\`.
5. Inspect the backend logs for \`[metrics] ad_gen_complete status=ready duration_ms=...\`.
6. Call \`/start\` again — should reset status to \`generating\` and produce a fresh set of variants (regenerate path).

## Edge cases to check
- User record has no brandGuidelines yet — extractor falls back to companyName + productDomain.
- onboardingEvents has multiple channel_selected events — the most recent wins.
- LLM returns 7 variants — capped at MAX_AD_VARIANTS (3).
- LLM returns no \`variants\` key — patches User with \`failed\` status, error message \`/variants/\`.
- Bedrock throws a network error — patches User with \`failed\`, error captured.

title: feat(backend): per-step state machines on User (icp/competitor/creativeDir/adImage/adCopy) + endpoints
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Onboarding only had a single-axis `adGenStatus` state machine that mixed image + copy in one axis. The Epic needs 5 SEPARATE state machines running concurrently so each onboarding screen can fire the step it hides without guessing what's already in flight, and so a failure on one axis doesn't block the others.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds five pure state-machine modules (icp / competitor / creativeDir / adImage / adCopy) each with `startPatch` / `readyPatch` / `failedPatch` / `snapshot` and 20 REST endpoints (5 axes × 4 verbs) under `/api/onboarding/`. User type extended with 30 new optional fields. Foundation task — all other backend tasks under the Onboarding Epic block on this.

## How to test
1. Pull this branch, `cd backend`, run `npx tsc --noEmit` — **Expected**: clean.
2. Run `npm test` — **Expected**: 503 suites pass, 7740 tests pass (full suite).
3. Run `npx jest src/__tests__/icpStatusService src/__tests__/competitorStatusService src/__tests__/creativeDirStatusService src/__tests__/adImageStatusService src/__tests__/adCopyStatusService src/__tests__/onboardingSteps` — **Expected**: 76 tests pass across 6 suites.
4. Sync test env to this branch and curl an endpoint to smoke it (auth needed):
   ```
   POST /api/onboarding/icp/start            -> 200, status.icpStatus="running"
   GET  /api/onboarding/icp/status           -> 200, status snapshot
   POST /api/onboarding/icp/complete         (with valid personas) -> 200, status.icpStatus="ready"
   POST /api/onboarding/icp/complete         (when not running)    -> 409
   POST /api/onboarding/icp/complete         (with personas: [])   -> 400
   POST /api/onboarding/icp/start            (no auth header)      -> 401
   ```
   Same shape for `/competitor/*`, `/creative-dir/*`, `/ad-image/*`, `/ad-copy/*`.
5. **Expected**: Each axis is independently driven — kicking off ICP doesn't change competitor status, completion of one doesn't reset another.

## Edge cases to check
- DynamoDB write failure surfaces as 500 (already covered by the `start failed when DB throws` test).
- Result sanitization: long strings truncated, malformed entries dropped, arrays capped (covered by service-level tests).
- Negative clock skew (server clock moves backward between `start` and `complete`) coerces duration to 0.

## Test Evidence

Identity model: personas are identified by INDEX (`icp-{n}`) in the user's `icpResult` array. The FE backfills the id when rendering, and the backend parses the index here. This avoids a persona-id schema migration; future stable-id work can wrap these without changing the FE contract.

Also adds a new `valueProp?: string` field on the User record (separate from `marketStrategy.icp[].valueProposition` which is per-ICP, not brand-level).

3. LLM regen prompt extension — `triggerAdCopyForUser` now pulls the latest 5 rejects, cross-references the previous `adCopyResult.variants`, and prepends a "User REJECTED these recent ad copy directions" block to the per-variant user prompt. The LLM sees concrete negative examples.

title: fix(onboarding): robust JSON extraction unblocks Phase 4 ad-gen pipeline
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The Phase 4 ad-gen pipeline (ICP → Competitor → Creative direction → Ad copy) cascade-failed on the test environment whenever Claude returned a conversational preamble (e.g. `It looks like...`) instead of strict JSON. The naked `JsonOutputParser` threw on `JSON.parse`, which surfaced as `icpStatus='failed'` and hung the Phase 4 reveal screen behind the GeneratingHeader. PR #666 (Ads Tinder swipe deck) was unreachable on test env because of this.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds a layered defence that recovers JSON from prose preambles, fenced markdown, and other LLM-formatting drift, with a single retry-with-strict-prompt fallback before failing. All four onboarding services now use the new robust path.

Three layers:
1. **`extractJson` helper** (`backend/src/services/util/extractJson.ts`) — strips markdown fences, parses, falls back to a string-aware balanced-brace scan. Throws `JsonExtractError` carrying a 500-char raw snippet on failure.
2. **`LLMService.generateJsonRobust`** — invokes the model, runs `extractJson`, retries ONCE with a strict suffix (`"You MUST respond with only valid JSON..."`) on extraction failure. Non-extraction errors (network/auth) bubble up untouched.
3. **Service migration** — `onboardingIcpService`, `onboardingCompetitorService`, `onboardingCreativeDirService`, `onboardingAdCopyService` now call `generateJsonRobust` instead of `generateJSONContent`. `onboardingAdImageService` is image-only and skipped per the task spec.

No schema or DB change — the existing `icpError`, `competitorError`, etc. fields already capture the failure message (capped at 512 chars by the existing `*FailedPatch` helpers), so when extraction does exhaust the retry, the raw snippet lands in those fields verbatim for debugging.

## How to test
1. **Unit:** `cd backend && npm test -- onboardingIcpService onboardingCompetitorService onboardingCreativeDirService onboardingAdCopyService extractJson llmService.generateJsonRobust`
   **Expected:** 134 tests pass, 0 failures.
2. **Service-level prose recovery (ICP):** the new test "reaches ready when the robust LLM call recovers from a prose-then-JSON response" simulates the happy retry path; "reaches failed with a debuggable error when the robust LLM call exhausts retries" simulates the hard-fail path.
   **Expected:** Both tests green; `icpStatus='ready'` with 5 personas in one case, `icpStatus='failed'` with snippet-bearing `icpError` in the other.
3. **End-to-end (manual, post-deploy):** kick off a fresh onboarding on test env, watch `/api/onboarding/icp/status` poll. Even with a model that prefaces prose, the status reaches `ready` and Phase 4 cascade (Competitor → CreativeDir → AdImage → AdCopy) completes. PR #666 swipe deck becomes reachable.
   **Expected:** No `icpStatus='failed'` due to JSON parse cascade; the swipe deck renders.

## Edge cases NOT covered
- Did not unit-test the strict-suffix prompt against a real Bedrock response (mocked at the LangChain layer instead — prompt-content assertion verifies the suffix lands in the second call).
- `LLMService.generateJSONContent` is left intact for backward compatibility with all the OTHER services in the codebase that aren't in this fix's scope. They still use the old parser. If a similar cascade shows up there, the same migration is one-line per service.
- Did not add `response_format: { type: "json_object" }` — the LangChain `ChatBedrockConverse` adapter does not expose it cleanly, and the layered extractor + retry already neutralises the failure mode in practice. Can be added as a follow-up if Anthropic exposes it.

- Unit tests: **7965 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** (full backend suite)

title: [CRITICAL] fix(onboarding): gate competitor on icpStatus=ready + cascade-fire from icp
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High | 3 SP

## What was wrong (before)
The FE called `/icp/start` and `/competitor/start` back-to-back. ICP took ~20s; competitor fired immediately, read `user.icpResult`, saw `[]`, threw `"no ICPs persisted — Step 2 must complete first"`, and persisted `competitorStatus: failed`. CreativeDir gates on competitor; AdImage gates on creativeDir; AdCopy gates on adImage — so a single bad write on competitorStatus stalled the whole cascade and Phase 4 reveal rendered GeneratingHeader forever. **100% of onboarding users currently fail to see ads.**

## What this fixes (after)
1. **Gate** — `triggerCompetitorStrategyForUser` now bails with `[onboardingCompetitorService] gated by icp step` when `icpStatus !== 'ready'` or `icpResult` is empty/non-array. Does NOT mark `failed`. Mirrors the gate-on-creative-dir pattern in `onboardingAdImageService`.
2. **Cascade** — `triggerIcpDiscoveryForUser` fires `startCompetitorStrategyForUser` (after a 2s GSI propagation delay) immediately after persisting `icpStatus: 'ready'`. Removes the 20s+ polling-tick latency.

Together these make the handoff race-free in both directions: even if `/competitor/start` fires too early, the gate keeps it harmless; and the cascade trigger ensures competitor research begins the moment ICPs are ready.

## TDD commit order
- **Commit 1** (`f471a459`) — failing tests. 8 new gating + cascade assertions encoded the contract before any implementation. All failed against `harsha/dev`.
- **Commit 2** (`bac37f70`) — initial fix. Gate logic + cascade kickoff (used `trigger*`, no GSI delay).
- **Commit 3** (`b98c34ba`) — refinement caught by live E2E. Switched cascade to `start*` (so `competitorReadyPatch` accepts the result), added 2s GSI propagation delay (so the cascade trigger sees the just-written icpReadyPatch).

## Live E2E test passing output

The live integration test (`backend/src/__tests__/onboardingPipeline.live.test.ts`) creates a fresh DynamoDB user with `linear.app` brandGuidelines, kicks off the cascade through the same code path the FE uses, and asserts the chain reaches `adCopyStatus='ready'` with 3 ad-copy variants and 3 image variants. Real Bedrock + real Gemini + real Google Search.

The full cascade reaches `adCopyStatus: ready` in ~2 minutes — the NON-NEGOTIABLE acceptance criterion is met.

## How to test on test env
1. After merge + redeploy: sign up as a fresh user at `34.222.47.141:5174`.
2. Run through onboarding goal=Paid Ads → brand → Phase 2 questions → Phase 3.
3. Watch backend logs:

## Summary

- Root cause found in prod logs: Azure OpenAI `gpt-5.4` returns HTTP 400 `"Invalid 'tools': array too long. Expected an array with maximum length 128, but got an array with length 143 instead."` when too many tools are sent after skill installation

```
}
```
Session `48932abd` ran `install_skills` once (5s), then the second LLM call with the full 143-tool list caused the 400. Previous morning run (04:59) succeeded because it was a shorter session that didn't hit the limit.

title: fix(playwright): make Playwright MCP connection reliable
body:
## Summary

Fixes the recurring "Connection timeout for playwright — External Service Unavailable" error reported in session `94ce2575-3aa4-4175-8d37-a24d46f54153` (LinkedIn login).

Four root causes were identified and fixed:

- **Fix 1 — Eliminate npx @latest on cold start**: Added `@playwright/mcp@0.0.70` as a real `package.json` dependency. `createStdioTransport` now rewrites the DB-configured `npx @playwright/mcp@latest` command to use `node_modules/.bin/playwright-mcp` directly, skipping the npm registry lookup + download that was the primary timeout trigger on EB cold starts.

- **Fix 2 — 45s timeout for stdio**: Local subprocess startup (Node.js init + MCP handshake) needs more time than an HTTP connection. Stdio transports now get 45s; HTTP stays at 15s.

- **Fix 3 — Disable circuit breaker for stdio**: The circuit breaker was designed for external HTTP services (BraveSearch). A new subprocess spawn is independent of prior failures — applying the circuit to stdio meant one user's bad spawn blocked **all users** for 5 minutes. Now only non-stdio servers trip the circuit.

- **Fix 4 — Evict pool on transport close**: When the Playwright subprocess crashed between tool calls, `transport.onclose` only logged a warning. The dead `Client` stayed in the user's session pool (keyed by `userId`) and was reused on the next call. The `onclose` handler now evicts the entry immediately so the next call triggers a fresh reconnect.

title: perf(infra): cap DynamoDB retry budget at 3 (was SDK default 10)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
The DynamoDB \`DocumentClient\` was instantiated with no config, defaulting to \`maxRetries: 10\` and exponential backoff (50ms base). A single throttled GSI query burned through:

\`\`\`
50 + 100 + 200 + 400 + 800 + 1600 + 3200 + 6400 + 12800 + 25600 = ~51s of pure wait time
\`\`\`

…on top of each round-trip's actual latency.

Observed during the 2026-04-26 onboarding baseline run on test env: every \`/api/onboarding/ad-image/status\` poll baseline ~100ms but occasionally hit ~9s. Shape matches 'one throttle + partial retry budget burn'. The same bug shape exists on every authenticated route polling DDB (icp / competitor / creative-dir / ad-image / ad-copy status), since they all share this client.

## What this fixes (after)
\`maxRetries: 3\` on both \`DocumentClient\` instances:
- \`backend/src/services/db.ts\` (the hot one — userDb, leadsDb, etc.)
- \`backend/src/config/aws.ts\` (secondary)

Worst-case retry wait drops from ~51s to ~350ms (50+100+200). Most queries succeed first try and pay nothing — only the throttled ones see the difference.

**Per-attempt timeout deliberately untouched.** Tightening \`httpOptions.timeout\` without case analysis risks breaking legitimate slow ops (BatchWrite, multi-page scans). The next layer of fix — removing the *duplicate* getUserById call that's actually causing the throttle — needs CTO review since it touches auth middleware. Filed as Notion task [34e09247c95181cf96a5c0fb00867a13](https://www.notion.so/34e09247c95181cf96a5c0fb00867a13).

## How to test
1. Deploy to test env, redeploy via \`./test-env/test-env.sh sync\`
2. Sign up a fresh user, walk through onboarding paid_ads goal
3. Open browser DevTools → Network → filter to \`/api/onboarding/.*/status\`
4. **Expected**: poll latency consistent ~100ms, no 9s outliers
5. (Optional) Force a throttle by sending bursts via curl to the status endpoint while monitoring CloudWatch for \`UserIdIndex\` throttle metrics
6. **Expected**: throttled requests fail at ~350ms after retry budget vs ~10s today

## Edge cases to check
- BatchWrite / multi-page scan paths — should be unaffected since the per-request timeout is unchanged. Only the retry count drops.
- Long-running migration scripts (\`backend/src/scripts/*\`) — these instantiate their own \`DocumentClient\` so they're unaffected by this change.

## Test Evidence
- \`npx tsc --noEmit\` clean
- No unit tests added — change is pure SDK config, not logic. Asserting the config in a test would be a tautology against the constant.

## Files changed
- \`backend/src/services/db.ts\` (+7/-1)
- \`backend/src/config/aws.ts\` (+4/-2)

## What was NOT tested
- Confirmed throttle scenario on test env with CloudWatch metrics — diagnosis is hypothesis-only. The retry-cap is still net-positive regardless of whether throttling is the actual root cause; ~51s worst-case retry budget is too generous for a poll-heavy endpoint either way.
- Production-grade load test

## Related PRs
- Backend: standalone
- Customer Portal: standalone

## Notion task
Side finding from baseline measurement Sub-task 0 ([Notion link](https://www.notion.so/34e09247c951817e9aaffff6cd5bbc40)). The follow-up duplicate-read fix is filed at [34e09247c95181cf96a5c0fb00867a13](https://www.notion.so/34e09247c95181cf96a5c0fb00867a13) and needs CTO review.

title: fix(onboarding): icp/start + regenerate-one return start patch instead of stale GSI read
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Root cause of the Maya regen-spinner-stuck bug observed during the **2026-04-27 post-fix baseline rerun** (Notion sub-task [34e09247…](https://www.notion.so/34e09247c951817e9aaffff6cd5bbc40)).

\`/icp/regenerate-one\` route flow was:
1. \`await startIcpDiscoveryForUser(userId)\` — updateUser sets icpStatus='running' on the base table
2. \`await userDb.getUserById(userId)\` — reads via \`UserIdIndex\` GSI
3. \`return icpSnapshot(user)\`

Step 2 hits an **eventually-consistent GSI**. Immediately after step 1 flips icpStatus to 'running', the GSI may still surface the pre-update row showing \`icpStatus='ready'\` + old \`icpResult\`. The FE trusts the response, sees 'ready', stops polling, and the regen spinner sticks indefinitely. Reproduced reliably during today's Maya run.

Same shape on \`/icp/start\` (less visible there because the prior state is usually 'idle', but still racy).

This is the user-visible failure the FE fix #675 was supposed to address — but #675 was only half the story. PR #675 made the click fire the POST (was a silent no-op before). This PR fixes the polling-stops-because-of-stale-GSI side, which is what Maya hit in today's rerun.

## What this fixes (after)
Don't read the user back via the GSI. We just persisted the \`icpStartPatch\` synchronously in step 1 — return it directly as the snapshot.

\`\`\`typescript
await startIcpDiscoveryForUser(userId);
return res.json({ status: icpSnapshot(icpStartPatch()) });
\`\`\`

Strongly correct, no 200-1000ms delay-then-read workaround. The trigger function continues to do real work asynchronously and update the record when ICPs are ready; the FE will see status='ready' on a subsequent poll once the GSI catches up.

## How to test
1. Sign up new test user on \`http://34.222.47.141:5174\`, complete brand-build + Phase 2 → land on icpReview
2. Click "Regenerate this one" on any ICP card
3. **Expected**: card flips to "Emma is researching your ICPs…" stall
4. Wait ~30-60s for backend regen LLM call
5. **Expected**: stall swaps back to a fresh ICP card with new content, NOT stuck forever (was: stuck forever)
6. Open DevTools → Network: confirm \`/api/onboarding/icp/regenerate-one\` 200 OK, then \`/api/onboarding/icp/status\` polls every ~1500ms returning \`status: 'running'\` until the LLM finishes
7. **Expected**: polling returns \`status: 'ready'\` with new icpResult; spinner clears; FE renders new persona

## Edge cases to check
- Two regen clicks in quick succession — both should result in 'running' polls; second click increments icpStartedAt
- Regen on a fresh user (no prior icpResult) — should still flip to 'running' and trigger the LLM
- Backend startIcpDiscoveryForUser throws — route returns 500 (existing catch path; unchanged)

## Test Evidence
- 45 passed, 0 failed across \`onboardingBrandReview.test.ts\` + \`onboardingSteps.test.ts\`
- Added new test: \"returns icpStatus='running' even when getUserById returns stale GSI data\". Verified failing on old code (\`Expected: 'running' / Received: 'ready'\`), passing on new code.
- \`npx tsc --noEmit\` clean
- Companion FE fix #675 already merged to harsha/dev

## Files changed
- \`backend/src/routes/onboardingSteps.ts\` (-8/+17 — both /icp/start and /icp/regenerate-one routes)
- \`backend/src/__tests__/onboardingBrandReview.test.ts\` (+32 — stale-GSI test case)

## What was NOT tested
- Live test env walkthrough — recommended before merging the next mega PR. The persona rerun agent confirmed this exact bug pattern today; fix should be re-verified against test env.
- Other status routes (\`/competitor/start\`, \`/creative-dir/start\`, \`/ad-image/start\`, \`/ad-copy/start\`) use the same \`updateUser → getUserById\` pattern and theoretically have the same bug, but only \`/icp/regenerate-one\` is user-visible during onboarding (the others fire automatically and the FE doesn't need an immediate-response status). Filed as follow-up.

## Related PRs
- Customer Portal: #675 already merged (FE half of the fix)
- Backend: standalone

## Notion task
Discovered during persona baseline rerun — see Notion comment titled "BASELINE RESULTS (POST-FIX) — 2026-04-27" on sub-task [34e09247…](https://www.notion.so/34e09247c951817e9aaffff6cd5bbc40). With this fix shipped, Maya's regen path should complete end-to-end on the next rerun.
