title: feat(crm): Tier 0 cross-tenant sibling enrichment + 4-tier company resolution
body:
## Summary

CRM enrichment upgrade — adds **Tier 0 cross-tenant sibling lookup** before Apollo/enrich.so in identity resolution, plus a **4-tier company resolution** waterfall for LinkedIn find-leads.

### Tier 0 — cross-tenant sibling enrichment
- **Tier 0a (identity fields):** before any external call, query siblings via the new GSIs by email / linkedin / nameCompanyKey, filter by a 90-day TTL on `updatedAt`, and copy `firstName / lastName / email / linkedin / company / website / title` with per-field merge across all matching siblings.
- **Tier 0b (config-requested fields):** new post-identity stage that copies any config-requested field from the same sibling set (zero extra DDB queries). Field matching is two-phase: canonical `aliasFor` match first (free), then a single batched LLM call per run for unaliased custom fields. TTL is per-field via `FIELD_GROUPS[group].ttlDays` (default 90d). Implemented in `enrichmentSiblingConfigFields.ts`.
- **Audit trail:** `EnrichedFieldMeta` (source / lastVerifiedAt) recorded per field; sanitized out of customer-portal lead responses.
- **Schema:** new `AW-Leads` attributes `userId`, `nameCompanyKey`, `linkedin` (sparse) + three new GSIs — see Deploy steps below.
- **Backfill:** one-shot script `backfillLeadsUserId.ts` to populate `userId` + `nameCompanyKey` on legacy rows so they become eligible for sibling matching.
- **Resolver hardening:** Apollo no longer overwrites Tier 0 fills (missing `!resolved.*` guards added on the LinkedIn-first and people-by-email steps); Apollo / enrich.so throws now log-and-continue instead of aborting the resolver and discarding Tier 0 work.

### 4-tier company resolution (LinkedIn find-leads)
When Unipile search results lack a company on the lead:
- Tier 1: existing cache → Tier 2: regex on title → Tier 3: one batched Gemini Flash call (with robust JSON-array extraction — handles preamble/postamble/markdown wrapping) → Tier 4: Unipile getProfile fallback.
- LLM tier batches every unresolved title for the page into a single call — negligible cost even at the 20-lead import cap.
- Web-search support added to the enrichment tier via Gemini + Azure OpenAI.

### Other
- Apollo LLM extraction normalization improvements (`enrichmentNormalizer.ts`).
- v3.1 enrichment: push `leadIds` filter into `deps.loadLeads`.
- Email lowercased once at resolver entry; enrich.so reverse-lookup now reads `firstName / lastName` when earlier tiers didn't fill them.

## Deploy steps / Migration

**1. Activate the three new GSIs on `AW-Leads`** (prod + staging tables both need this — `create-tables.ts` only adds them on fresh creation; existing tables require `UpdateTable`):
- `EmailLookupIndex` — PK `email`, SK `updatedAt`, sparse
- `LinkedinLookupIndex` — PK `linkedin`, SK `updatedAt`, sparse
- `NameCompanyLookupIndex` — PK `nameCompanyKey`, SK `updatedAt`, sparse

GSI creation runs in the background and can take minutes-to-hours on a populated table; Tier 0 queries return empty (no error) until each index reaches `ACTIVE`. Test-env GSIs are already partially active.

**2. Run the backfill once GSIs are ACTIVE:**
```
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/backfillLeadsUserId.ts
```
Backfills `userId` + `nameCompanyKey` on legacy `AW-Leads` rows so they're queryable by `NameCompanyLookupIndex` and consistent with the new `populate userId on writes` path. Safe to re-run (idempotent).

**3. No env-var changes required.** UI changes ship in the companion PR (`agentweb-customer-portal#762`).

## Test plan
- [ ] Tier 0a GSI queries return cross-tenant siblings within the 90-day TTL window
- [ ] Tier 0b copies config-requested fields without firing extra DDB queries
- [ ] Per-field merge produces correct freshest-wins ordering
- [ ] Apollo / enrich.so failure mid-resolve preserves Tier 0 fills (no fills:[] regression)
- [ ] LinkedIn find-leads resolves company via all 4 tiers (regex / LLM / getProfile fallbacks all hit)
- [ ] Tier 3 LLM tier handles JSON wrapped in markdown / preamble
- [ ] Audit fields (`enrichedFieldMeta`) stripped from customer-portal lead responses
- [ ] Backfill script populates `userId` + `nameCompanyKey` on legacy rows; idempotent on re-run
- [ ] `npx tsc` passes
- [ ] `npm test` passes — new suites: `enrichmentIdentityResolver.tier0`, `crmDb.findLeadsBy`, `crmDb.createLead.userId`, `leadSchema.nameCompanyKey`, `backfillLeadsUserId`, `crmDb.batchGetLeads`, `agentModeService.importLeadsFromSearch.companyFallback`, `enrichmentMetadataPresentation`

title: fix(local-agent): remove false-positive safety regex and add worker probe
body:
## Summary

- **Bug 1 — false-positive safety filter:** `\bpost.*form\i` was matching across distant words in a task string (e.g. `"posted ... formatted"`), incorrectly blocking legitimate screenshot tasks. Removed this pattern — `\bsubmit.*form\i` and `\bfill.*form\i` already cover the actual form-submission concern.

- **Bug 2 — misleading health check:** `check_local_agent_status` only hit `/health`, which the HTTP server always answers even when the Codex worker queue is hung. Added a worker probe: a trivial `/task` call (`"Return the single word: ping"`, 15s timeout). If the worker is stuck, the status now returns `{ reachable: false, workerHung: true }` instead of falsely reporting healthy.

Both bugs were diagnosed from session `bc83cef7` where Emma got a false-positive rejection on a LinkedIn screenshot task and then correctly diagnosed a hung worker, but `check_local_agent_status` kept returning healthy, confusing the debug flow.

title: fix(crm): self-heal legacy empty-string GSI keys in updateLead
body:
## Summary
- `AW-Leads` has three sparse cross-tenant lookup GSIs (`EmailLookupIndex`, `LinkedinLookupIndex`, `NameCompanyLookupIndex`) that all use `updatedAt` as the range key. Every `updateLead` SETs `updatedAt`, which forces DDB to re-project the GSI entry — and rows carrying `email` / `linkedin` / `nameCompanyKey` as `""` (legacy data written before the sparse-index guards landed) fail with *"AttributeValue for a key attribute cannot contain an empty string value"*, blocking the whole update.
- Observed impact on the test env: HubSpot CRM pulls reported `Failed to update` for the affected rows, and `hubspotAdapter.syncDeal` could not persist `hubspot_contact_id` / `hubspot_deal_id` — so every subsequent push created a fresh duplicate deal in HubSpot.
- Fix: `updateLead` now reads the existing row once up-front and queues a `REMOVE` for any of `email` / `linkedin` / `nameCompanyKey` that is `""` on the stored row, skipping fields the caller is already writing (no `SET`+`REMOVE` conflict in one `UpdateExpression`). The pre-existing `nameCompanyKey` recompute block was rewired to reuse the same read, so no extra DDB call.

## Test plan
- [x] New: `backend/src/__tests__/crmDb.updateLead.legacyEmptyGsiKeys.test.ts` — 7 cases (REMOVE per GSI key field, multi-field, no-op when valid, SET-vs-REMOVE conflict, null-row safety).
- [x] Existing `crm.db.test.ts` updated: `skipFieldNamesUpdate` assertion narrowed to "no `get` on `AW-LeadLists`" (we now always read the lead row itself).
- [x] `npx jest --testPathPattern="crm\.db|crmDb.updateLead"` — 63 / 63 pass.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — no new errors (pre-existing `voiceService` / `remotionService` errors unrelated).
- [x] Verified end-to-end on test env: cleared the two stuck rows (`hshah@argusoft.com`, `ruiw@agentweb.pro`), then a direct `SET updatedAt` update on both succeeded — confirming the GSI no longer rejects them.

title: fix(research-reports): truncate searchableText in API response to cut payload 63%

## Root Cause

The `/api/tasks/executions/with-html-reports` endpoint was returning **~415KB payloads** for accounts with ~136 reports. Each report's `searchableText` was stored at up to 3000 chars and sent in full.

Production nginx logs showed the symptom:

an upstream response is buffered to a temporary file while reading upstream,
request: "GET /api/tasks/executions/with-html-reports"

Truncate `searchableText` to 500 chars in the API response before sending. 500 chars is more than sufficient for client-side keyword matching. The full text remains stored in DynamoDB.

**Payload reduction:** 415KB → 154KB (−63%)

title: fix(nginx): increase proxy buffers to prevent API responses buffering to disk
body:
## Summary
- Added `.platform/nginx/conf.d/proxy_buffers.conf` to increase nginx proxy buffer size from 4KB default to 16KB (256KB total)
- Root cause: nginx's default proxy buffers (8×4KB = 32KB) are too small; any response larger than that spills to a temp file on disk, causing the page to freeze until the full response is written to disk
- The sessions endpoint returns ~220KB and the reports endpoint returns ~154KB — both exceed the 32KB default, which is why both endpoints were being buffered to disk
- Setting `proxy_buffer_size 16k` + `proxy_buffers 16 16k` (256KB total) handles both endpoints in memory

## Test plan

body:
## Summary

title: fix(enrichment): allow duplicate-canonical fields with fan-out + warning UX
body:
## Summary

- Legacy CRM lists often have the same data in multiple columns (e.g. `company` + `company_name`). Previously the validator hard-blocked saves when two fields routed to the same canonical, leaving users with no way to enrich. Now the validator emits a soft warning and the orchestrator fans a single canonical fill out to every user-facing column.
- Adds a `knownColumns` hint to the GET response so the frontend can distinguish standard / list-schema rows (auto-resurface on next save) from manually-added rows (delete is destructive).

## Why

User report: an existing list where standard `company` and custom `company_name` both held partial data couldn't be saved — the dialog showed a red error every time. Old CRM-import flows commonly produce this shape, so it's the legitimate case, not a config mistake.

## Changes

**Validator (`enrichmentConfigService.validateConfig`)**
- Canonical-collision check now produces warnings instead of throwing. Other validation (duplicate names, reserved names, bad `aliasFor`, schema version) still throws.
- Warning payload is just the duplicate-group descriptor (e.g. `'company' and 'company_name'`); the frontend wraps it with a single shared header + bullets.

**Orchestrator (`crmEnrichmentServiceV3.routeFields`)**
- `userNameByCanonical: Map<string,string>` → `userNamesByCanonical: Map<string,string[]>`.
- Per-group canonical list is deduped, so the waterfall runs once per canonical (no quota/cost change).
- Rename loop emits one fill per user-facing name so each colliding column receives the same enriched value.

**API**
- GET `/api/crm/lists/:listId/enrichment-config` adds `knownColumns: string[]` (standard CRM cols ∪ list-schema cols, minus excluded/reserved).
- PUT response includes `warnings: string[]`.

## Tests

- `enrichmentConfigService.test.ts`: replaced the two old `rejects.toThrow(/both map to/)` cases with `.resolves` + warning-payload checks. Added: standard-column + canonical case (`company` + `company_name`), 3-way collision, no-collision baseline, new `knownColumns` cases (standard ∪ list-schema, manual saved-only excluded). Updated all existing `saved.fields` → `saved.config.fields` for the new return shape.
- `crmEnrichmentServiceV3.test.ts`: fan-out test for canonical→[user] writing to top-level + customFields, plus a 3-way alias case.
- Backend suite: 9,853 passed, 0 failed.

## Companion PR

Customer-portal changes (warning banner + conditional trash + saved-with-warnings UX) are in a separate PR on the customer-portal repo: same branch name.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open Enrichment Config on a list with `company` and `company_name` both present and saved → yellow banner appears with "Config saved — heads up, duplicate fields detected." Bullet lists the duplicate groups.
- [ ] Run an enrichment after saving with duplicates → both columns receive the same enriched value.
- [ ] Save with no duplicates → green toast (no banner).
- [ ] Backend: `npm test` in `backend/` stays green.

title: harshit/crm-enrichment-apollo-tech-stack-integration
body:
## Summary

Adds Apollo as an optional **Tier 1** source in the Discover Tech Stack enrichment waterfall, plus an associated DynamoDB nested-REMOVE bootstrap fix.

### Backend changes

**1. Apollo tech-stack tier (`crmEnrichmentService.ts`)**

- New `EnrichmentJobSpec.apolloTechStack?: boolean` flag on the job spec. When set, the enrichment waterfall extracts a domain from `lead.emailDomain` or `lead.website` (skipping personal-email domains), calls `apolloService.matchOrg(domain)`, and if the mapped Apollo organization returns a non-empty `techStack` array it builds a single LLM unit from that list — **bypassing the web-search tier entirely** for the lead.
- Falls back to web search transparently when Apollo is unavailable (`isApolloServiceReady() === false`), the lead has no resolvable domain, the domain is personal, or Apollo returns no tech data. No errors surfaced to the caller.
- Preview enrichment forcibly disables `apolloTechStack` — Apollo `matchOrg` calls burn real credits, and the preview UX is allowed to be less complete.
- Adds `isApolloServiceReady()` / `getApolloService()` imports from `apolloService`.

Note on field naming: Apollo's raw API field is `technology_names`; the code reads the mapped field `MappedOrganization.techStack` (mapping owned by `apolloFieldMapper.mapApolloOrganization`).

**2. Test coverage (`__tests__/crmEnrichmentService.test.ts`, +217 lines appended to existing file)**

New `describe('enrichLead — apolloTechStack waterfall', …)` block with 8 cases:
- Apollo hit → Apollo context used, web search skipped.
- Apollo returns no `techStack` → falls back to web search.
- Lead has no domain → Apollo not called, web search runs.
- Apollo service not ready → Apollo not called, web search runs.
- `apolloTechStack` flag absent → Apollo not called even if ready.
- Preview mode → Apollo not called regardless of flag (credit-conservation).
- Personal-email domain → Apollo not called, web search runs.
- `emailDomain` absent but `website` present → domain extracted from website (`https://www.beta.com` → `beta.com`).

**3. DynamoDB nested-REMOVE bootstrap fix (`db.ts`, commit `194f6976`, +4 / -2)**

In the nested-map update helper used by `crmDb` lead writes: the parent-map bootstrap previously only ran when there were `meta` / `customFields` keys to **SET**. REMOVE on a nested path (e.g. `customFields.<key>`) on a row whose parent map didn't exist throws `ValidationException`. Bootstrap now runs whenever **either** SET-keys OR REMOVE-keys are present for the `meta` / `customFields` maps.

### Why

- **Apollo Tier 1** — Apollo's mapped `techStack` is materially more reliable and far cheaper than the existing tier (LLM-over-Brave/Tavily over job postings + integration pages). Wiring it in as a precondition keeps the existing prompt path intact while letting us shed the bulk of the per-lead web-search spend on customers who have Apollo enabled.
- **Nested-REMOVE bootstrap** — surfaced while running the Apollo path end-to-end against real lead rows that lacked an empty `customFields` map. Decoupling it from the feature would just stall this PR.

### Customer-portal changes

A separate PR on `customer-portal` ([#786](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/pull/786)) tightens the **Discover Tech Stack dialog** layout (compact stat tiles, dedicated scrollable preview region).

### Status notes

- Branch is **3 commits behind `origin/main`** at PR-open time (main has `ec185bd4` auto-engagement comment-variety fix + 2 follow-ups touching `db.ts`, `cron/socialEngagementExecutor.ts`, and release notes). Reviewer can merge `main` in or wait for a rebase — no expected conflicts in `crmEnrichmentService.ts`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cd backend && npx tsc` clean.
- [ ] `cd backend && npm test -- crmEnrichmentService` — all 8 new `apolloTechStack` cases pass.
- [ ] On test env: enable `apolloTechStack: true` on a Discover Tech Stack job, run against a list with valid corporate domains, confirm `[CrmEnrichment][enrichLead] apollo tech stack HIT` log lines and that the per-lead web-search call is skipped.
- [ ] On test env: run with a mix of personal and corporate domains, confirm personal-domain rows fall back to web search without errors.
- [ ] On test env: clear a custom field on a lead whose `customFields` map is empty — confirm the update succeeds without `ValidationException` (covers the db.ts fix).
- [ ] Preview the same job from the customer portal — confirm no Apollo calls in the backend logs (preview-disable path).

title: feat(crm): per-category ICP matching with threshold scoring
body:
## Summary

Replaces the single-ICP LLM match with per-category evaluation. The LLM scores each lead against every ICP category in the market strategy; the highest-scoring category wins, and `isMatch` flips on at the `ICP_MATCH_THRESHOLD` (currently 70). Adds clamping, NaN coercion, and visibility logging so bad LLM responses don't silently corrupt the DB or look like "every lead is a bad fit".

## Why

The prior single-ICP prompt forced a binary "does this lead match the market strategy" judgment. When a strategy had multiple ICPs (e.g. "SaaS CTOs" + "Enterprise CFOs"), the user couldn't see which persona the lead actually resembled, and the score was untrustworthy because it summarized over multiple personas. Per-category scoring exposes that detail; a single hoisted threshold gives a defensible "is ICP" gate consistent with the LLM's per-category reason text.

## Changes

**`backend/src/routes/crm.ts`** — `/lists/:listId/leads/match-icps`

- LLM prompt rewritten to evaluate against EACH ICP category. Response shape is now `categoryMatches: { icpTitle, isMatch, score, reason }[]` per lead.
- Winner is the highest-scoring entry; persisted `isMatch = winner.score >= ICP_MATCH_THRESHOLD`.
- `matchedIcpTitle` is set only when the threshold is met (no stale title on a non-match).
- **Threshold hoisted to a module-level const** (`ICP_MATCH_THRESHOLD = 70`) and interpolated into the prompt template — prompt and code can't drift on what "match" means.
- **Score coercion**: non-finite values (string, NaN) are coerced to 0 before `Math.min/Math.max` clamping. `cat.score ?? 0` alone left NaN in flight, which DynamoDB rejects on write and breaks `cat.score > best.score` comparisons silently.
- **Empty-`categoryMatches` log**: emits `console.warn` when the LLM returns no entries, which almost always means it used the old top-level `{isMatch, score, reason}` schema. Without the log this manifests as "every lead is a bad fit" with no breadcrumb.
- Human-readable fallback reason ("Insufficient lead data to evaluate against ICP categories.") replaces the prior misleading "No ICP categories evaluated."
- Stores `categoryMatches` on the lead's `icpMatch` so the frontend can show the per-category breakdown.

**`backend/src/services/db.ts`** — adds `matchedIcpTitle` and `categoryMatches` to the `icpMatch` TypeScript type on `Lead`.

## Companion PR

Customer-portal: [AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#787](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/pull/787) — renders the new shape via a shared `<IcpCategoryBadge />` and renders the per-category list in `LeadDetailPanel` + `CRM.tsx`. Same branch name.

## Tests

`backend/src/__tests__/crm.routes.test.ts` — extended coverage:

- Per-category happy path (winner picks max-score category, persists `matchedIcpTitle` + `categoryMatches`).
- **Sub-threshold winner** (score 50) → `isMatch:false`, `matchedIcpTitle:undefined`. Closes the "no negative test" gap from the first round of review.
- Score clamping: input 150 → stored 100.
- **NaN coercion**: input `"high"` (string) → stored 0, asserted on both lead-level and stored `categoryMatches[0].score`.
- Empty-`categoryMatches` fallback path.

Backend suite: 90/90 in `crm.routes`. `npx tsc` clean.

## History note

The first push to this branch was based on a stale `origin/main` and the diff implicitly reverted the Slack `app_mention`/`message` double-reply fix and the social-engagement comment-variety feature. The branch has been **rebased onto current `origin/main`**, dropping those unrelated reverts. The current diff is scoped to backend ICP files only (3 files, ~150 lines).

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx tsc` + `npm test` in `backend/` — all green.
- [ ] On a list with a multi-ICP market strategy, click "Match ICPs". Each lead's `icpMatch` carries `categoryMatches` with one entry per ICP; `matchedIcpTitle` is set only when `winner.score >= 70`.
- [ ] Verify a lead the LLM scores below 70 still shows the winner's reason but `isMatch=false` and no `matchedIcpTitle`.
- [ ] Force a malformed LLM response (empty `categoryMatches`) → lead updates with `score: 0`, the human-readable fallback reason, AND a `[crm] match-icps: LLM returned empty categoryMatches…` warn in the backend log.
- [ ] If the LLM hallucinates a string score (`"high"`) → no DDB write failure; the entry is stored as `score: 0`.

title: fix(agent): exclude get_visual_context from Agent Mode tool list
body:
## Summary

- `get_visual_context` was leaking into Agent Mode sessions via the `__other_skills__` bucket (it wasn't assigned to any published skill, so `resolveSkillsToToolNames` included it as an unassociated tool)
- The LLM could then call it directly, and even hallucinate calls to it from conversation history
- The existing `excludeTools` filter correctly removed it from the tool definitions sent to the LLM, but couldn't block hallucinated calls since `allowedToolNames` still contained the tool name

## Root Cause

`getUnassociatedTools()` collects all registered tools not belonging to any skill, excluding only foundation tools and admin-only tools. `get_visual_context` fell into this bucket and surfaced to anyone with `__other_skills__` in their subscription.

## Fixes

1. **`agentModeService.getUnassociatedTools`** — add `get_visual_context` to the explicit exclusion set so it never appears in the `__other_skills__` bucket
2. **Tool call runtime guard** — before executing any tool call, check if the tool name is in `excludeTools`; if so, return an error response to the LLM instead of executing. This blocks hallucinated calls even when the tool definition wasn't provided.

## Test plan

- [ ] `agentModeService.skills.test.ts` — 2 new tests: `getUnassociatedTools` excludes `get_visual_context`, `getUnassociatedToolNames` excludes it too (56 total, all pass)

title: fix(crm): repair empty-string GSI key attributes on AW-Leads
body:
## Why

When the three sparse lookup GSIs (`EmailLookupIndex`, `LinkedinLookupIndex`, `NameCompanyLookupIndex`) were added to `AW-Leads`, the `backfillLeadsUserId` migration reported **`errored: 158,092`** — all with the same DynamoDB error:

> The AttributeValue for a key attribute cannot contain an empty string value.

Before the sparse-index guards landed in `createLead` / `updateLead`, some code paths (CSV imports, early enrichment writes) stored `""` for `email`, `linkedin`, and `nameCompanyKey`. DynamoDB now rejects **any** `UpdateItem` on a row carrying an empty string for a GSI hash key — even when the update doesn't touch that attribute. This silently blocks all enrichment writes and CRM field edits on ~77% of the table.

`updateLead` already self-heals rows it touches (added in a prior PR), but leads that are never explicitly edited, and code paths that bypass `updateLead` (e.g. `setLeadFields`), continue to fail without this repair.

## What

- **`backend/src/scripts/repairEmptyGsiKeys.ts`** — new one-shot repair script that:
  - Scans `AW-Leads` for rows with `email=""`, `linkedin=""`, or `nameCompanyKey=""`
  - `REMOVE`s the empty-string attributes (dropping the lead from those sparse GSIs, which is correct — no email means it shouldn't be indexed by email)
  - Re-attempts the `userId` + `nameCompanyKey` backfill for repaired leads in the same write (the original backfill skipped these due to the same error)
  - Idempotent, dry-run supported

- **`docs/aw-leads-gsi-migration-runbook.md`** — adds a "Repair: empty-string GSI key attributes" section with when/why to run it, dry-run instructions, expected output, and verification steps.

## No write-path code changes needed

`createLead`, `updateLead`, and the CSV import path already guard against writing `""` for GSI key fields. New leads are safe. This PR is purely the repair script + runbook for the existing bad data.

## Test plan

- [ ] Dry-run on prod: `NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/repairEmptyGsiKeys.ts --dry-run` — verify `repaired ≈ 158,092`, `errored: 0`
- [ ] Real run on prod — verify `errored: 0` in DONE output
- [ ] Re-run `SKIP_GSI=1 DRY_RUN=1` backfill — should now report `errored: 0`
- [ ] Spot-check a previously-failing lead: confirm `linkedin` attribute is absent (not `""`), and `userId` is set

## Summary

- Knowledge bases created via `create_knowledge_base` sometimes end up with `knowledgeBaseSize=0` in DynamoDB even though the GCS file is present and has valid content. This caused them to be completely invisible to the agent.
- **Root cause**: `knowledgeBaseSize` is stored as `0` (exact cause unclear — likely a DynamoDB update race in production) while the GCS content is correct. All affected logic uses `size > 0` as the gate.

**`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`**

- `createKnowledgeBase`, `updateKnowledgeBaseFile`, `attachKnowledgeBaseFiles`: use `Math.max(size, 1)` so newly-created KBs are never silently filtered out by `size > 0`.

**`backend/src/__tests__/knowledgeBase.fileVisibility.test.ts`**

title: harshit/crm-enrichment-apollo-tech-stack-integration
body:
> Re-opens #1543 — the original PR's branch was deleted by mistake and restored, but GitHub refused to reopen because the restored branch was rebased onto a newer `main` (head SHA no longer matches). Filing a fresh PR with the same scope. Branch merges cleanly into `main` (verified via `git merge-tree`).

## Summary

Adds Apollo as an optional **Tier 1** source in the Discover Tech Stack enrichment waterfall, plus an associated DynamoDB nested-REMOVE bootstrap fix.

### Backend changes

**1. Apollo tech-stack tier (`crmEnrichmentService.ts`)**

- New `EnrichmentJobSpec.apolloTechStack?: boolean` flag on the job spec. When set, the enrichment waterfall extracts a domain from `lead.emailDomain` or `lead.website` (skipping personal-email domains), calls `apolloService.matchOrg(domain)`, and if the mapped Apollo organization returns a non-empty `techStack` array it builds a single LLM unit from that list — **bypassing the web-search tier entirely** for the lead.
- Falls back to web search transparently when Apollo is unavailable (`isApolloServiceReady() === false`), the lead has no resolvable domain, the domain is personal, or Apollo returns no tech data. No errors surfaced to the caller.
- Preview enrichment forcibly disables `apolloTechStack` — Apollo `matchOrg` calls burn real credits, and the preview UX is allowed to be less complete.
- Adds `isApolloServiceReady()` / `getApolloService()` imports from `apolloService`.

Note on field naming: Apollo's raw API field is `technology_names`; the code reads the mapped field `MappedOrganization.techStack` (mapping owned by `apolloFieldMapper.mapApolloOrganization`).

**2. Test coverage (`__tests__/crmEnrichmentService.test.ts`, +217 lines appended to existing file)**

New `describe('enrichLead — apolloTechStack waterfall', …)` block with 8 cases:
- Apollo hit → Apollo context used, web search skipped.
- Apollo returns no `techStack` → falls back to web search.
- Lead has no domain → Apollo not called, web search runs.
- Apollo service not ready → Apollo not called, web search runs.
- `apolloTechStack` flag absent → Apollo not called even if ready.
- Preview mode → Apollo not called regardless of flag (credit-conservation).
- Personal-email domain → Apollo not called, web search runs.
- `emailDomain` absent but `website` present → domain extracted from website (`https://www.beta.com` → `beta.com`).

**3. DynamoDB nested-REMOVE bootstrap fix (`db.ts`)**

In the nested-map update helper used by `crmDb` lead writes: the parent-map bootstrap previously only ran when there were `meta` / `customFields` keys to **SET**. REMOVE on a nested path (e.g. `customFields.<key>`) on a row whose parent map didn't exist throws `ValidationException`. Bootstrap now runs whenever **either** SET-keys OR REMOVE-keys are present for the `meta` / `customFields` maps.

### Why

- **Apollo Tier 1** — Apollo's mapped `techStack` is materially more reliable and far cheaper than the existing tier (LLM-over-Brave/Tavily over job postings + integration pages). Wiring it in as a precondition keeps the existing prompt path intact while letting us shed the bulk of the per-lead web-search spend on customers who have Apollo enabled.
- **Nested-REMOVE bootstrap** — surfaced while running the Apollo path end-to-end against real lead rows that lacked an empty `customFields` map. Decoupling it from the feature would just stall this PR.

### Customer-portal changes

A separate PR on `customer-portal` ([#786](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/pull/786)) tightens the **Discover Tech Stack dialog** layout (compact stat tiles, dedicated scrollable preview region).

## Test plan

- [ ] `cd backend && npx tsc` clean.
- [ ] `cd backend && npm test -- crmEnrichmentService` — all 8 new `apolloTechStack` cases pass.
- [ ] On test env: enable `apolloTechStack: true` on a Discover Tech Stack job, run against a list with valid corporate domains, confirm `[CrmEnrichment][enrichLead] apollo tech stack HIT` log lines and that the per-lead web-search call is skipped.
- [ ] On test env: run with a mix of personal and corporate domains, confirm personal-domain rows fall back to web search without errors.
- [ ] On test env: clear a custom field on a lead whose `customFields` map is empty — confirm the update succeeds without `ValidationException` (covers the db.ts fix).
- [ ] Preview the same job from the customer portal — confirm no Apollo calls in the backend logs (preview-disable path).

title: fix(crm): prevent char-indexed customFields corruption
body:
## Summary
- Adds defensive `customFieldsGuard` utility (`backend/src/utils/customFieldsGuard.ts`) that prevents the char-indexed `customFields` corruption pattern (`{"0":"{","1":"\"","2":"f",…}`) observed on `list_1775001347573_e45x9md6x` ("Fangfang Tan outreach list", ~141 leads, 2026-04-10 → 2026-04-25).
- Replaces every inline `{ ...lead.customFields, ...patch }` spread with `mergeCustomFields(...)` at 7 call sites (the merge in `batchCreateLeads`, V3 tier0b enrichment, `crmAutoSync`, HubSpot legacy webhook, CRM webhook handler, `importLeadsFromSearch`, **and Emma's `update_lead` tool**).
- Sanitizes `customFields` at the DB write boundary in `createLead`, `batchCreateLeads` new-lead path, `updateLead`, and `setLeadFields` — belt-and-suspenders against any caller that bypasses the merge helper.
- On detection: silently coerces non-plain-object `customFields` to `{}` and logs `[customFieldsGuard]` with full caller stack to EB logs. Never throws.

## Root cause
`Lead.customFields` is typed `Record<string, any>` but nothing enforces it at runtime. Any path that did `{ ...stringValue, ...patch }` (because the stored value had drifted to a string) produced char-indexed keys directly, since `{...s}` on a string spreads it character-by-character. Once corrupted, subsequent merges preserved/extended the corruption. TypeScript couldn't catch this because all DDB reads come back as `any`.

The Emma `update_lead` tool path was discovered as an additional gap during testing — `agentModeService.ts:7857` was an unguarded spread that the original audit missed.

## Non-goals (explicit)
- No backfill/repair migration for the existing 141 corrupted leads (the user will fix the CSV manually).
- No read-time auto-heal — already-corrupted DDB rows continue to return what's stored.
- No throw-on-detect — silent sanitize + log only.

## Verification
- `npx tsc` — clean.
- Full test suite: 9988 passed, 0 failures (one pre-existing `xlsx`-module infra issue from `main`, unrelated).
- New utility: **100%** statements / branches / functions / lines (19 unit tests).
- New write-boundary tests: 12 tests across 4 new files (createLead, batchCreateLeads, updateLead, setLeadFields), all TDD red→green.
- New Emma `updateLead` regression test in `agentModeService.crmTools.test.ts`.

## Cloud test-env verification
Deployed to `vendor-argusoft-access-agentweb1` and exercised end-to-end against the running API:

| Test | Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|---|
| createLead with `customFields: "{json string}"` | `POST /api/crm/lists/:id/leads` | Stored as `{}` ✓ |
| createLead with plain-object customFields | `POST /api/crm/lists/:id/leads` | Stored unchanged ✓ |
| bulk-import with mixed corrupt + clean leads | `POST /api/crm/lists/:id/leads/bulk-import` | Corrupt → `{}`; clean → unchanged ✓ |
| Read leads back, scan for char-indexed keys | `GET /api/crm/lists/:id/leads` | Zero char-indexed keys ✓ |
| Backend logs `[customFieldsGuard]` with stack trace | Container logs | Triggers logged with `source`, `listId`, `leadId`, caller stack ✓ |

## Operational note
After merge, watch EB logs for `[customFieldsGuard] non-object customFields coerced to {}`. Each occurrence prints the upstream caller's stack trace, the `source` tag (e.g. `db.createLead`, `crmWebhook.hubspot`, `agentMode.updateLead`), and the `listId`/`leadId` — enough to triangulate the original bug source and fix it at the actual entry point.

## Design / plan documents
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-19-crm-customfields-guard-design.md`
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-19-crm-customfields-guard.md`

## Test plan
- [ ] CI passes (tsc + test suite + coverage ≥95%)
- [ ] Spot-check `[customFieldsGuard]` log entries on staging after deploy
- [ ] (Optional) Run the Fangfang Tan list import on the CSV the user is fixing manually; verify clean leads land with structured customFields and any remaining corrupt rows are coerced rather than re-corrupted

title: feat(org-sharing): org-wide sharing across KB, templates, LPs, work plans, skills
body:
## Summary

Introduces org-wide sharing across five user-owned entity types and three integrations, plus the admin controls to manage it.

**Model (strict, admin-controlled):**
- Per-feature `shareSettings.{feature}.enabled` toggle + `editors[]` list, managed by org owner.
- **Plain members:** see+use shared items when `enabled=true`; cannot create/edit.
- **Editors:** can always create/edit regardless of toggle (decoupled from `enabled`).
- **Org owner:** full admin override.
- **Delete:** owner-only or admin override; editors cannot delete.

**Features covered:**
- HTML Templates, Landing Pages, Knowledge Base, Work Plans, Skills (per-user items with member fanout)
- Brand Guidelines, Market Strategy (org-singleton, editor-gated PUT)
- ClickUp, Foreplay, Google Drive folders promoted to org-level (admin/editor connects; all members consume; platform fallback preserved)

**Other changes:**
- New `orgShareService` helpers: `canViewItem`, `canEditItem`, `canManageOrgFeature`, `isFeatureEffectivelyEnabled`, `listOrgVisibleItems` (generic fanout with truncation).
- `GET`/`PATCH /api/orgs/me/share-settings` admin endpoints.
- Member-removal flow: preview + per-feature transfer/delete/leave.
- Migration scripts: org share-settings defaults, ClickUp→org, Foreplay→org.
- New `OrgIdIndex` GSI on AW-Users (replaces scan in `getOrgMembers`).
- Emma `list_available_skills` honors `shareSettings.skills` toggle (closes cross-org-via-Emma leak).
- Updated agent-mode system prompt: "Org-Wide Sharing — Read This Before You Flag a 'Data Scoping Bug'".

## Migrations

Four scripts must run **in this exact order** on each environment (staging first, then prod). All scripts are idempotent — safe to re-run.

### 1. Create `OrgIdIndex` GSI on `AW-Users` (REQUIRED FIRST)

```bash
NODE_ENV=staging    npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/create-org-id-gsi.ts
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/create-org-id-gsi.ts
```

- **Why first:** `orgDb.getOrgMembers()` now `Query`s this GSI instead of scanning the table. Without the index, every member-list lookup returns an error → admin Org Sharing UI, share-settings PATCH editor validation, and member-fanout endpoints all fail.
- **Auto-detects** billing mode (on-demand vs provisioned) from `DescribeTable`; configures throughput accordingly.
- **Wait for the GSI to reach `ACTIVE` status** before proceeding to step 2. Backfill on a large table can take several minutes (DynamoDB does it asynchronously).
- Idempotent: re-running detects the existing index and exits cleanly.

### 2. Backfill `shareSettings` defaults on every Organization

```bash
NODE_ENV=staging    npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/migrate-org-share-settings.ts
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/migrate-org-share-settings.ts
```

- **Why:** `GET /api/orgs/me/share-settings` and every gating helper (`canManageOrgFeature`, `isFeatureEffectivelyEnabled`) assume `org.shareSettings` is present. Existing org rows predate the field and need it added before customer-portal admins open the new Org Sharing tab.
- **Defaults written:**
  - `knowledgeBase`, `htmlTemplates`, `landingPages`: `{ enabled: false, editors: [] }`
  - `workPlans`, `skills`: `{ enabled: true, editors: [] }` (always-on features)
  - `brandGuidelines`, `marketingStrategy`: `{ editors: [] }` (no toggle; org-singleton)
- Existing `shareSettings` are **preserved** — only missing fields get filled in.
- Pure additive write — no rollback needed.

### 3. Promote ClickUp tokens to org-level

```bash
NODE_ENV=staging    npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/migrate-clickup-to-org.ts --dry-run
NODE_ENV=staging    npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/migrate-clickup-to-org.ts
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/migrate-clickup-to-org.ts --dry-run
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/migrate-clickup-to-org.ts
```

- **Why:** ClickUp is now an org-level integration (admin/editor connects once; all members consume). Existing per-user tokens need to bubble up to the org record so members in the same org keep working.
- **Behavior per user with `secrets.clickup_access_token` + `orgId`:**
  - If org already has `secrets.clickup_access_token`: leave it (admin's connection wins).
  - Otherwise: copy the user's encrypted token to the org record.
- Per-user tokens are **intentionally left intact** — they serve as a fallback until an admin explicitly disconnects and reconnects at the org level.
- **`--dry-run`** prints the planned moves without writing.
- Idempotent: org-level tokens are never overwritten on re-run.

### 4. Promote Foreplay tokens to org-level

```bash
NODE_ENV=staging    npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/migrate-foreplay-to-org.ts --dry-run
NODE_ENV=staging    npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/migrate-foreplay-to-org.ts
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/migrate-foreplay-to-org.ts --dry-run
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/migrate-foreplay-to-org.ts
```

- Same shape as the ClickUp migration: per-user `secrets.foreplay_api_token` → org record. Org-level wins on conflict; per-user fallback retained.

### Migrations NOT needed

- **Google Drive folders** — already lived on `org.knowledgeBase` settings; only the UI/perm gating changed. No data move.
- **HtmlTemplates / LandingPages / WorkPlans / Skills / KnowledgeBase / BrandGuidelines / MarketStrategy** — sharing is driven entirely by `org.shareSettings` (covered by migration #2). Existing per-user items aren't rewritten; the fanout helper reads them from each member's bucket at request time.

### Rollback

- GSI: can be dropped via `aws dynamodb update-table --gsi-updates` if needed. Code falls back to error (not silent fail), so revert the backend deploy before dropping the GSI.
- Share-settings backfill: additive only — no rollback required.
- ClickUp / Foreplay token copies: revert by deleting `secrets.clickup_access_token` / `secrets.foreplay_api_token` from affected org rows. Per-user copies untouched.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc` — clean
- [x] All `__tests__/orgShared*.test.ts` suites pass (HtmlTemplates, KnowledgeBase, LandingPages, Skills, WorkPlans)
- [x] `orgShareService.test.ts`, `orgShareSettings.routes.test.ts`, `orgMemberRemoval.test.ts`, `orgPillarEditors.test.ts`, `orgClickupIntegration.test.ts`, `orgForeplayIntegration.test.ts`, `orgGoogleDriveFolders.test.ts` pass
- [x] `emma.listAvailableSkills.orgAware.test.ts` (7 cases) passes
- [x] Playwright manual verification: editor sees Create+Edit; plain member with toggle on sees read-only fanout; plain member with toggle off sees only own items
- [ ] **Staging:** run migrations 1 → 4 in order; verify GSI ACTIVE before #2
- [ ] **Production:** repeat migrations 1 → 4 in order **after** staging soak
- [ ] Pair with customer-portal PR: https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/pull/799

## Out of scope
- mcpFetch delegation elevation (separate cross-org concern, tracked separately)

title: fix: Stop button — cancel on client disconnect, discard ghost responses
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: Stop button worked on the client (aborted the fetch) but the backend kept running and saved the LLM response to DynamoDB, so it reappeared on reload.
- **Why**: The `/stop` HTTP call arrived too late — the worker had already finished and cleaned up the `sessionToRequestId` mapping, so the cancel IPC message was never sent to the worker.

## Fixes

**`backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts`**
- Added `req.on('close')` listener on `/generate` that fires the moment the client drops the connection (Stop button aborts the fetch). Immediately signals cancellation to the worker via IPC and emits SSE `complete` to clear "Thinking..." state.
- When `response.cancelled` is true, skip persisting `responseMessages` to DynamoDB entirely — cancelled turns leave no ghost response.

**`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`**
- Added a post-LLM `isCancelled()` check after each `callLLM()` await. The pre-iteration check fires before the LLM starts, so a Stop arriving mid-call was invisible to the cancellation logic.

**`customer-portal/src/hooks/useAgentModeChat.tsx`** (in customer-portal repo PR)
- Fixed a client-side race: when a response succeeded with a queued follow-up, the `finally` block dequeued the message and called `setTimeout(handleSend, 0)`. If Stop was clicked in that window, the timeout still fired. Now the timeout ID is stored in `pendingQueuedSendTimeoutRef` so `handleStop` can `clearTimeout` it.

## Test plan
- [ ] Send a message, click Stop mid-generation → no response appears on reload
- [ ] Send a message, let it complete → response appears normally
- [ ] Send two messages rapidly (queue) → second sends after first completes
- [ ] Send two messages rapidly, click Stop → neither queued message sends

title: fix(org-sharing): gate ClickUp/Foreplay/Drive integrations on Knowledge Bases sharing
body:
## Problem

When an org admin set the **Knowledge Bases** org-wide sharing toggle off ("Private"), plain org members could still see and access the org's connected **ClickUp**, **Foreplay**, and **Google Drive** integrations — on the Knowledge Base page and through Emma. Knowledge base *files* already honored the toggle, so the three integrations were inconsistent and exposed data the admin chose to keep private. This is an authorization defect: the admin's "Private" choice was not enforced for these integrations.

## Root cause

The token/folder resolution layer handed org-level resources to every org member unconditionally:

- `clickupService.getAccessToken()` / `foreplayService.getAccessToken()` returned the org-level token to any member.
- `agentModeService.getUserGoogleDriveFolders()` returned the org's `googleDriveFolders` to any member.

Connect/disconnect were already gated (`canEditItem`), but the *view/read* path was not.

## Fix

Gate all three at the resolution layer on `isFeatureEffectivelyEnabled(caller, org, 'knowledgeBase')` — the org resource is exposed only to the org owner, designated KB editors, or every member when sharing is on. Gated members fall through to their own personal token/folders. A single choke point per integration fixes both the page endpoints (`/api/oauth/clickup/status`, `/foreplay/status`, and downstream read endpoints) and Emma's `listKnowledgeBaseFiles` / `searchKnowledgeBase`.

This mirrors the already-correct pattern in the Google Drive *route* (`settings.ts` `/google-drive/folders/:id/files`, which already used `canViewItem`).

**No frontend change** — a gated member's `/status` now returns `connected:false`, so the existing "managed by your org admin" placeholder shows.

## Testing

- **Unit (TDD):** 7 new tests written failing-first; full backend suite **10,386 passing**, coverage Branches 95.17% / Statements 98.94% / Functions 97.89% / Lines 99.08%.
- **Cloud dev integration test** — real synced code against real Dev DynamoDB with controlled temp data: **10/10**. Owner & KB editors still get the org token; a plain member with sharing OFF is withheld it (ClickUp -> `null`, Foreplay -> falls through to the platform key not the org token, Drive -> `[]`); a member with sharing ON still gets it. Temp data cleaned up.

## Commits

- `fix(org-sharing): gate ClickUp/Foreplay/Drive integrations on knowledgeBase sharing`
- `test(org-sharing): cover knowledgeBase gating of ClickUp/Foreplay/Drive`
- `docs(release): note org integrations now respect Knowledge Bases sharing`

title: fix: retry Bedrock 400 no-body errors in scheduled chats
body:
## Summary
- Scheduled chats (e.g. "Social Listening Research") were failing intermittently with `I encountered an issue processing your request` when a Bedrock Converse API call returned `400 status code (no body)`
- This AWS SDK error occurs when Bedrock returns an HTTP 400 with no parseable response body — an intermittent infrastructure issue (API Gateway timeout, Bedrock cold-start), **not** a client validation error
- The error was incorrectly treated as permanent (400s are not in the transient retry list), causing the entire scheduled chat run to abort
- Fix: adds `/status code \(no body\)/i` to `TRANSIENT_MESSAGE_PATTERNS` in `agentModeErrors.ts` so these errors trigger the 3-attempt exponential backoff retry already in place for other transient errors

## Root Cause
The "Social Listening Research" schedule (ID `069cfe85-d8cd-472f-88d1-0ca0998c9847`) has failed 2/90 runs with identical symptoms: `bravesearch_brave_web_search` fails on one tool call, and the subsequent Bedrock LLM call returns `400 status code (no body)`. The pattern is intermittent (2.2% failure rate) and both failures follow the same pattern, pointing to a transient Bedrock infrastructure error rather than a structural bug in the request.

title: fix: LinkedIn drip campaign not-connected snooze and {{first name}} variable alias
body:
## Summary

- **Retry storm on not-connected leads**: When a lead in the LinkedIn Drip Campaign is not yet a 1st-degree connection, `sendLinkedInStep` throws and the enrollment stays stuck at `step=0` with `nextSendAt` in the past. The worker retried every 5 minutes indefinitely. Fix: catch the `"not a 1st-degree connection"` error and call the new `dripSequenceDb.snoozeEnrollment()` to push `nextSendAt` 6 hours out.
- **`{{first name}}` variable not substituted**: All 3 step templates use `{{first name}}` (space) but `substituteVariables` only handled camelCase `{{firstName}}`, so every sent message contained the literal `{{first name}}`. Fix: add a `VARIABLE_ALIASES` map in `emailVariables.ts` covering `first name`, `last name`, and their common case variants.

## Root cause discovered via

- Production DynamoDB query: `johnv.the.dev@gmail.com` enrollment `enr_1779300596886_816e4a43` stuck at `step=0` with `nextSendAt` = enrolled time
- Production logs (`web.stdout.log`): `[dripWorker] Error processing enrollment enr_1779300596886_816e4a43: Error: Cannot send message: target is not a 1st-degree connection (status: SECOND_DEGREE)` — repeating every 5 minutes
- Template inspection: `Hi {{first name}} — thanks for connecting!` → `substituteVariables` regex only matches `\{\{firstName\}\}`, not `\{\{first name\}\}`

title: feat(crm): organization-wide analytics & funnel sharing
body:
## Summary

Adds organization-wide analytics sharing and self-service analytics configuration. An organization's analytics (SEO domains, GA4 properties, Microsoft Clarity projects, product domain) live on the Organization record. Visibility and edit rights flow through a single `shareSettings.analytics` setting; funnel permissions are gated on the same setting.

## Data model

- `Organization` carries the analytics fields (`seoDomains`, `googleAnalyticsProperties`, `primaryAnalyticsPropertyId`, `gaFilteredDomains`, `productDomain`, `clarityProjects`) plus `analyticsConfigSource: "migrated" | "self"`.
- `OrgShareSettings.analytics: { enabled, editors }` controls plain-member visibility. Owners and listed editors always see and edit.
- Funnel permissions gate on `shareSettings.analytics`. A separate `OwnedFeature` type retains funnels so member-removal still iterates funnel data ownership.

## Resolver + storage

- `resolveAnalyticsConfig(user)` returns the effective analytics bundle for any caller: org users read the Organization record (with an owner-record fallback for orgs that have not yet been migrated); solo users read their own user record.
- `resolveConfigTarget(user)` returns `{ kind, id, canEdit, canView }` for write/read gating.
- `analyticsConfigStore` exposes `readAnalyticsConfig` / `writeAnalyticsConfig`. Reads of an un-migrated org transparently fall back to the owner's user record.

## API

- `GET /api/seo/config` — returns the caller's effective config + `canEdit` + `canView` + `scope` + service-account email. Plain members of an org with sharing off receive an empty bundle (no leak).
- `PUT /api/seo/config/ga`, `/config/seo-domains`, `/config/clarity` — editor-gated section saves, validated by `validateAnalyticsConfig`.
- `POST /api/seo/config/ga/test` — GA4 service-account connectivity check (rate-limited per user).
- `GET /api/auth/me` — exposes `effectiveAnalyticsConfig` and `canEditAnalyticsConfig`.

## Partner portal (admin)

- Configure SEO/AEO dialog reads from the org config and writes through the resolved target.
- `gaFilteredDomains` and product-domain admin paths are org-aware.

## Migration

One-shot script `backend/src/scripts/migrate-analytics-config.ts` scans `AW-Organizations`, copies each owner's analytics fields onto the org record (including legacy single-value `googleAnalyticsPropertyId` / `clarityProjectId` when the array form is empty), and sets `analyticsConfigSource: "migrated"`. Idempotent — re-running is a no-op.

### How to run

From `backend/`:

```bash
# Dry run — log what would change, write nothing
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node src/scripts/migrate-analytics-config.ts --dry-run

# Apply
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node src/scripts/migrate-analytics-config.ts
```

- `NODE_ENV` selects the DynamoDB table prefix: `production` (no prefix → `AW-Organizations`), anything else → `Dev-AW-Organizations`.
- Per-org log line lists the fields being written; final summary shows `scanned`, `changed`, `skipped` counts.
- Already-migrated orgs (those with `analyticsConfigSource` set) are skipped.
- Owner user records are not modified — the script only reads them.
- AWS credentials need DynamoDB read on `AW-Users` and read+update on `AW-Organizations`.

## Test plan

- [ ] **Migration:** un-migrated org with legacy single-value fields → run script → org has merged config with `analyticsConfigSource: "migrated"`, owner user-record untouched.
- [ ] **canView gate:** plain member of an org with sharing OFF → `GET /api/seo/config` returns empty arrays; flip sharing ON → returns the org config.
- [ ] **canEdit gate:** plain member tries `PUT /api/seo/config/ga` → 403; editor / org owner → 200.
- [ ] **Un-migrated fallback:** org with `analyticsConfigSource` absent → `readAnalyticsConfig` returns the owner's user-record analytics so dashboards aren't blank before the migration runs.

title: feat(emma): migrate CRM lead enrichment to the V3 engine
body:
## Summary

Migrates Emma's three CRM lead-enrichment tools from the legacy `CrmEnrichmentService` to the V3 `runEnrichment` engine — fixing the bug where Emma-driven enrichment reported success but left requested fields empty — plus a field-name normalization fix, and bundles the `crm-enrichment-v3-review-fixes` branch.

## Emma → V3 migration

- `enrich_leads_preview`, `enrich_leads_execute`, `enrich_lead_custom` now run the V3 engine instead of the legacy one (the legacy engine gated extended fields off, so they came back empty).
- Extracted `processEnrichmentConfig` from `setEnrichmentConfig` — Emma processes the config (alias resolution, smart-field classification, validation) in memory without persisting it, so the user's UI-saved config is never clobbered.
- New `enrichmentToolConfig.ts` (pure tool-args → V3 config mapper) and `enrichmentToolRunner.ts` (process config → run V3 → map result, with an engine-tagged observability log line).
- `EMMA_ENRICH_MAX_LEADS` batch cap (default 500, env-tunable) on `enrich_leads_execute`; representative 2-lead preview sampling.
- New `output_fields` schema with per-field `overwrite_policy`.

## Field-name normalization fix

Emma-requested field names that are synonyms of an existing column — `company_name`→`company`, `job_title`→`title`, `linkedin_url`→`linkedin`, or an existing custom field via canonical alias — are normalized before the config is built, so enrichment writes into the existing column instead of creating a duplicate custom field. Remaps are surfaced to Emma. Also adds `website` to V3's standard top-level columns.

## Merged: crm-enrichment-v3-review-fixes

Large-list `loadLeads` pagination (every lead processed, not just the first DynamoDB page), concurrent chunk writes, dead-code cleanup, single-source `STANDARD_ENRICHABLE_FIELDS`, shared Apollo helpers.

## Testing

- `npx tsc` clean; backend unit tests pass (≥95% coverage on new files).
- Cloud E2E on an ephemeral test environment: 14/16 matrix cases passed; Emma's 3 tools confirmed running V3, never the legacy engine.
- Field-normalization fix verified live — the remap is surfaced and no duplicate custom column is created.

title: fix: add sliding-window loop detector for alternating Playwright tool call patterns

## Summary
- Emma was getting stuck in a navigate→screenshot→navigate→screenshot loop when reading uploaded files (all navigating to the same S3 URL)
- The existing consecutive-repeat check (A→A→A) didn't catch this because the tool name alternates each step, so the signature never repeated consecutively

All 44 `playwright_browser_navigate` calls in the session navigated to the **identical S3 URL** — the same uploaded spreadsheet image. The alternating pattern (nav[144]→screenshot[146]→nav[148]→…) ran ~30 iterations before Emma tried something else. The window detector would have stopped it at iteration 10.

title: V3 enrichment: source attribution, critic view, phone validation & Tier 0.5 expansion
body:
## Summary

Hardens the V3 CRM-enrichment pipeline along three axes: every enriched field is now traceable and quality-labelled, phone numbers are validated before persistence, and Tier 0.5 web search reaches business-email leads with missing websites. Closes the source-attribution gaps from `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-22-v3-enrichment-source-attribution-design.md` (plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-22-v3-enrichment-source-attribution-fixes.md`).

### Source attribution & confidence
- **Fix 1 — web-tier per-field provenance:** `extractFieldsViaLLMReal` now returns `{value, sourceUrl?, sourceQuote?}` per field; web fills carry `provider:'llm_web_search'` + URL + quote, so the critic pass fact-checks against real evidence.
- **Fix 2 — pattern-guessed emails:** attributed to `provider:'pattern'` (was mislabelled `enrich.so`) with `confidence:'medium'` and the pattern recorded in `sourceQuote`.
- **Fix 3 — smart-field model:** `source:'llm'` fills record the producing model in `provider`.
- **Fix 5 — critic view:** the critic verdict is surfaced as a per-field `criticView` (`high`/`low`/`drop`) on `EnrichedFieldMeta`. Non-destructive — nothing is auto-deleted.
- **Fix 6 — confidence restoration:** the `getFieldConfidence()` registry is wired into V3 (`metaApollo`/`makeApiMeta`/`metaUnipile`); the Apollo table is extended with identity fields and the V3 waterfall's snake_case names so every enriched field carries a `confidence` label.
- **Fix 7 — job traceability:** the run id is stamped as `enrichedJobId` on every persisted fill.
- **Dropped on revalidation:** the planned Fix 4 (removing the `existing_data` bucketing branch) — that branch is a live guard for v2-enriched leads re-run through V3, not dead code.

### Phone validation
- Sanitize phone numbers from every enrichment source via `libphonenumber-js` before persisting. Three-tier strategy: E.164 → international, US national → E.164, digit-count fallback for local-format numbers.
- Drop invalid/vanity numbers instead of carrying them forward.
- Drive-by: fix `normalizeDate` UTC off-by-one for named-month formats in positive-offset timezones; restore missing jest mocks that were causing `agentModeService.llmTiming` test timeouts.

### Tier 0.5 web search reaches business-email leads
- Remove the `apolloPeopleMatch` bail-out for personal emails — Apollo now receives personal-email leads (email + name, no freemail domain).
- Strip freemail domains (`gmail.com`, `yahoo.com`, etc.) from `domainForApollo` so Apollo isn't misled by them as an org domain signal.
- Tier 0.5 now fires for business-email leads with a missing website, not only company-name-only leads — the LLM finds a website before Apollo runs so the domain signal improves org-match.
- Validate the LLM-returned website against the email domain (exact + subdomain) and the echoed `searchedDomain` to reject hallucinated / wrong-company results.

title: fix: align KB read bucket env vars with write to fix write-succeeds-but-read-not-found
body:
## Root Cause

`readSingleKnowledgeBaseFile` was using different environment variable names than all write operations:

| Operation | Env var used (public) | Env var used (private) |
|---|---|---|
| `createKnowledgeBase` | `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` | `PRIVATE_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` |
| `updateKnowledgeBaseFile` | `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` | `PRIVATE_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` |
| `attachKnowledgeBaseFiles` | `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` | `PRIVATE_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` |
| `readSingleKnowledgeBaseFile` (**before fix**) | `GCS_BUCKET_NAME` ❌ | `GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PRIVATE` ❌ |
| `readSingleKnowledgeBaseFile` (**after fix**) | `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` ✅ | `PRIVATE_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` ✅ |

In production, `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` / `PRIVATE_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` are set to the prod bucket names. `GCS_BUCKET_NAME` / `GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PRIVATE` are not set in prod, so reads fell back to the hardcoded default `agentweb-knowledge-base-dev`. Writes went to the correct prod bucket; reads looked in the wrong (dev) bucket → "not found in storage".

## Fix

One-line change in `readSingleKnowledgeBaseFile` (agentModeService.ts line 14751-14752): replace `GCS_BUCKET_NAME` → `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` and `GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PRIVATE` → `PRIVATE_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET`.

## Tests

- Updated `beforeEach` to set `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` / `PRIVATE_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_BUCKET` (matching the fix)
- Added explicit test asserting private bucket is used for private KBs on read
- All 39 KB tests pass

## Test plan

body:
## Summary

Implements the autonomous self-improving onboarding completion loop end-to-end. All changes are gated by \`ONBOARDING_LOOP_ENABLED=true\`.

### Phase 0 — AWS Infra
- S3 bucket \`agentweb-onboarding-loop\` (versioned), DynamoDB \`AW-OnboardingLoopRuns\`, IAM policy document
- Seed \`config.json\` in S3

### Phase 1 — Surface Audit
- \`onboarding-surface-audit.md\`: 16 screen types, ~66 hardcoded strings, terminal screen = \`closing\`

### Phase 2 — Variant Serving
- \`onboardingLoopConfig.ts\`: S3 read/write, 60s cache, djb2 deterministic A/B assignment; \`Variant.pending\` field — pending variants never served until approved
- \`onboardingVariants.ts\`: \`GET /api/onboarding/variants/:step\` — graceful degradation on S3 errors
- 26 tests (including pending-skip coverage)

### Phase 4 — Loop Pipeline + Crons
- \`onboardingLoopAgents.ts\`: sensorScan → diagnose → generateMutations → validateBusinessRules → critiqueMutations (Bedrock claude-sonnet-4-6; NO PII in prompts)
- \`onboardingLoopApproval.ts\`: daily Slack DM + reaction/reply polling; auto-ship at 6pm PT
- \`onboardingLoop.ts\`: daily 15:00 UTC — generates/critiques proposals, **stages them in S3 as \`pending=true\`** before posting Slack DM. Watchdog activates them after ✅
- \`onboardingLoopWatchdog.ts\`: hourly — polls Slack reactions on pending variants (✅→activate, ❌→remove, 🛑→hold), retires bad active variants, pauses loop on aggregate drop
- 97 tests across all pipeline functions, all pass

### High-Risk Items

## Root Cause

Schedule **Daily ICP Lead Finder — IncentivPay** (ID: `4cdb1134`) has `search_web` in `requiredFunctionCalls`. When BraveSearch MCP is available, the LLM prefers `bravesearch_brave_web_search` over the built-in `search_web`. The validation logic didn't recognize them as equivalent, so every run reported `search_web` as missing even though web searches were performed.

Evidence: run 1 (2026-05-23) called `search_web` 6× → **passed**. Run 2 (2026-05-24, 20 attempts) only called `bravesearch_brave_web_search` → **all 20 attempts failed**.

## Fix

Added a `FUNCTION_CALL_ALIASES` map in `runVerifiedChat` that normalizes MCP tool names to their built-in equivalents before validation counting:

```ts
const FUNCTION_CALL_ALIASES: Record<string, string> = {
  'bravesearch_brave_web_search': 'search_web',
  'bravesearch_brave_news_search': 'search_web',
};
```

Both the reporting array and key-value counter use normalized names, so `bravesearch_brave_web_search` calls now satisfy a `search_web` requirement.

title: fix(scheduled-chat): correct bravesearch alias to use satisfies-map instead of normalization
body:
## Problem with Previous Fix (PR #1626)

The first implementation normalized actual call names: `bravesearch_brave_web_search` → `search_web` before tracking. This broke 9 production schedules that explicitly require `bravesearch_brave_web_search` in their `requiredFunctionCalls` — those calls would be renamed to `search_web` and never satisfy the `bravesearch_brave_web_search` requirement.

## Correct Approach

Uses a `FUNCTION_CALL_SATISFIES` map and a `countCallsForRequirement` helper:

```ts
const FUNCTION_CALL_SATISFIES: Record<string, string[]> = {
  'search_web': ['bravesearch_brave_web_search', 'bravesearch_brave_news_search'],
};
const countCallsForRequirement = (functionName, calls) =>
  calls.filter(c => c === functionName || FUNCTION_CALL_SATISFIES[functionName]?.includes(c)).length;
```

- Actual call names are stored as-is (`bravesearch_brave_web_search` stays `bravesearch_brave_web_search`)
- When checking if `search_web` was satisfied, brave search calls also count
- Explicit `bravesearch_*` requirements in schedules remain specific and still work

Also removes the now-dead `allActualFunctionCalls` key-value tracker (all evaluation now uses `allActualFunctionCallsForReporting` + `countCallsForRequirement`).

## Test Plan

- [x] 381 agentModeController tests pass (includes 2 alias tests from PR #1626)
- [x] Verified 9 production schedules explicitly require `bravesearch_brave_web_search` — this fix doesn't break them
- [x] Dry-ran full test suite locally before pushing

title: Onboarding loop: heartbeat DM + 3 data-quality fixes
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)

The onboarding loop runs daily at 15:00 UTC but had been silent for at least 2 days. Investigation surfaced THREE distinct bugs:

1. **`logRun()` was writing the wrong key.** `AW-OnboardingLoopRuns` has composite key `(runId HASH, ts RANGE)` but `cron/onboardingLoop.ts:56` was setting `runAt` instead of `ts`. Every put threw `ValidationException: Missing the key ts in the item`, caught silently in a try/catch. Runs table sat at 0 items since creation, so we couldn't tell if the cron had fired at all.

2. **Google OAuth signups never set `signupSource`.** The `/register` (password) path at `controllers/auth.ts:150` sets `signupSource: "password"`, but both OAuth code paths (`auth.ts:326-330` and `:391-395`) omitted it. All 3 signups in the last 7d came via OAuth and showed `signupSource=null` in prod — making channel-source segmentation impossible.

3. **`isBotLikeEmail` was too loose.** Only caught Gmail 3-dot tricks + 2 hardcoded test domains. Real disposable-email signups (mailinator, guerrillamail, yopmail, etc.) were being counted as real users in the loop's denominator.

Plus a UX gap: when the loop had no mutations to propose (the common state today since only 1 variant per step exists), it returned silently. The approver couldn't distinguish "loop is healthy, nothing to ship" from "cron broken, no message." This is what masked bug #1 for 2 days.

## What this fixes (after)

- `logRun()` now writes `ts` instead of `runAt`, matching the table schema → runs table populates from this PR onward
- Both OAuth code paths now persist `signupSource: "oauth"`; `signupSource` is typed on the `User` interface
- `isBotLikeEmail` adds a disposable-domain blocklist, Gmail plus-addressing abuse pattern, and a heuristic for script-generated handles (≥16 chars with no vowel). All 3 real signups from the last 7d still classify as humans.
- New **daily heartbeat DM** when the loop has nothing to propose. Shows signups (24h/7d), completions (24h/7d), self-active users (24h/7d/30d using `lastActiveAt` which only ticks on non-delegated sessions), pilot ratio, and the full onboarding stage distribution.
- New `computeHeartbeatMetrics()` helper is pure + tested; new `postHeartbeatSlackDM()` uses `chat.postMessage` with user-id as channel (bot lacks `im:write` scope, so we avoid `conversations.open`).

## How to test

### Test 1 — Verify the heartbeat fires on the no-mutation path

1. SSH into prod-3 backend (or test env)
2. Set env vars: `ONBOARDING_LOOP_ENABLED=true`, `ONBOARDING_LOOP_APPROVER_SLACK_USER_ID=U08TM4QFQ1L`, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=<bot token>`
3. From `/var/app/current`: `node -e "require('./dist/cron/onboardingLoop').runOnboardingLoop()"`
4. **Expected:** Slack DM lands in `harsha-dm` with the heartbeat format (status, last 24h, last 7d, funnel, pilot ratio)
5. **Expected:** New entry in `AW-OnboardingLoopRuns` with `ts` populated

### Test 2 — Verify signupSource persists on Google OAuth signup

1. In an incognito browser, go through the Google OAuth signup flow on the customer portal
2. After signup, query DynamoDB: `aws dynamodb scan --table-name AW-Users --filter-expression "email = :e" --expression-attribute-values '{":e":{"S":"<your-test-email>"}}'`
3. **Expected:** Item has `signupSource: "oauth"`

### Test 3 — Verify the bot filter still admits real humans

1. Run the new unit tests: `npm test -- --testPathPattern "(isBotLikeEmail|onboardingHeartbeat)"`
2. **Expected:** 45 tests pass

### Test 4 — Verify the runs table starts populating

1. After the cron fires (or you manually fire it per Test 1), query the table
2. **Expected:** Each run produces an item with `runId`, `ts`, `status`, and details

## Edge cases to check

- Heartbeat DM gracefully degrades if Slack scope is missing (logs warning, doesn't crash loop)
- `lastActiveAt` being absent on a user → user excluded from self-active count, not crash
- New users from disposable domains hitting `/register` → they'll be created (we can't block at signup easily without breaking some legit cases), but they'll be filtered out of loop denominators

## Test Evidence

- New tests: 45 passed, 0 failed
- Full backend suite: 10,637 passed, 3 skipped, 1 pre-existing failure (`readFileContent.test.ts` — unrelated xlsx module resolution issue on `harsha/dev` baseline, not caused by this PR)
- `npx tsc` clean

Tested as: my own laptop with prod IAM creds + prod S3/DDB/Slack tokens. Manual fire confirmed:
- Heartbeat lands in Slack (`channel=U08TM4QFQ1L ts=1779726314.412049`)
- Funnel data accurate against prod (3 last-7d signups visible, 1 user in `active` stage, 14 self-DAU)

## Files changed

- `backend/src/cron/onboardingLoop.ts` — logRun ts fix, heartbeat wiring on no-mutation branch, computeHeartbeatMetrics helper
- `backend/src/services/onboardingLoopApproval.ts` — postHeartbeatSlackDM + formatHeartbeat
- `backend/src/services/db.ts` — UserDB class export, signupSource type, isBotLikeEmail tightening
- `backend/src/controllers/auth.ts` — signupSource on both OAuth code paths
- `backend/src/__tests__/onboardingHeartbeat.test.ts` — new
- `backend/src/__tests__/isBotLikeEmail.test.ts` — new

## What was NOT tested

- The setTimeout-based scheduling in `server.ts:533-555` is still fragile (every EB restart resets the timer to next 15:00 UTC). This PR does NOT fix that — separate Notion task filed for EventBridge migration. Tomorrow's auto-fire is still not guaranteed without that work.
- UTMs through Google OAuth still don't persist to user record — separate Notion task filed.
- Did NOT add a Slack `im:write` scope; instead worked around with user-id-as-channel. Works only because Harsha has DM'd the bot before. If we ever want to DM new approvers, scope expansion needed.

## Related PRs

- Backend-only. No customer-portal or landing-page changes.

title: Onboarding loop: admin HTTP trigger endpoint
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)

The onboarding loop is scheduled via in-process `setTimeout` in `server.ts:533-555`. Every EB restart (deploy, env var change, health-driven instance replacement) wipes the timer and reschedules from "now". If a restart lands after 15:00 UTC, today's fire is skipped silently. There's no way to re-fire without SSH access.

This fragility is what masked the `logRun` bug for 2 days in PR #1631 — the cron looked like it had never run, but I couldn't tell from the application side whether the timer was firing at all.

## What this fixes (after)

Adds `POST /api/admin/onboarding-loop/trigger`:

- Standard admin auth: `authenticateToken + isAdmin` middleware (mounted in `app.ts:288`)
- Fire-and-forget: returns `202 Accepted` immediately with `triggeredAt` + `triggeredBy` for audit
- Run continues in background; the loop's own `try/catch` + `logRun` capture results into `AW-OnboardingLoopRuns`
- No 500 on background failure; rejection is caught and logged

This sets up the surface for the planned EventBridge migration (Notion task #33): a scheduled rule → Lambda → IAM-signed POST to this endpoint gives a durable cron that survives any EB restart.

## How to test

### Test 1 — Smoke test the endpoint

1. Get an admin JWT for an admin user (e.g., `harsha@agentweb.pro`)
2. `curl -X POST https://api.agentweb.pro/api/admin/onboarding-loop/trigger -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT"`
3. **Expected:** Returns `202 Accepted` within ~100ms with body:
   ```json
   {
     "accepted": true,
     "triggeredAt": "2026-05-25T...",
     "triggeredBy": { "userId": "...", "email": "harsha@agentweb.pro" },
     "note": "Loop is running in the background. Poll AW-OnboardingLoopRuns for completion."
   }
   ```

### Test 2 — Verify the loop actually runs

1. Right after the curl above, watch CloudWatch logs for `[OnboardingLoop] Starting run loop-<ts>`
2. Wait 60-90 seconds for the LLM calls to complete
3. **Expected:** New entry in `AW-OnboardingLoopRuns` table with `status: 'completed'` and a fresh `ts`
4. **Expected:** Slack heartbeat DM lands in `harsha-dm` (assuming PR #1631 is merged first — the heartbeat code lives in that PR)

### Test 3 — Non-admin gets 403

1. Get a non-admin JWT (e.g., a regular customer user)
2. `curl -X POST https://api.agentweb.pro/api/admin/onboarding-loop/trigger -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT"`
3. **Expected:** `403 Forbidden` from the `isAdmin` middleware

### Test 4 — No JWT gets 401

1. `curl -X POST https://api.agentweb.pro/api/admin/onboarding-loop/trigger`
2. **Expected:** `401 Unauthorized` from `authenticateToken`

## Edge cases to check

- Concurrent triggers (two admins click within seconds): each invocation runs the loop fully. The loop is idempotent on the data (sensorScan → diagnoseUnderperforming is deterministic for a given dataset), but two concurrent runs would each generate their own runId + write to the runs table. Worth noting but not urgent.
- If `runOnboardingLoop()` throws synchronously (rare), the `.catch()` chain still catches it.

## Test Evidence

- Unit tests: 7 passed, 0 failed (`onboardingLoopAdminRoute.test.ts`)
- `npx tsc` clean
- Did NOT integration-test against prod yet (depends on PR #1631 merge)

Tested as: unit tests with stubbed `runOnboardingLoop` + stubbed auth middleware.

## Files changed

- `backend/src/routes/onboardingLoopAdmin.ts` — new, 57 lines
- `backend/src/app.ts` — 2-line mount with auth middleware
- `backend/src/__tests__/onboardingLoopAdminRoute.test.ts` — new, 118 lines

## What was NOT tested

- Production smoke test (waiting on PR #1631 merge first, since the heartbeat path is what makes the trigger immediately useful)
- Concurrent-trigger behavior in prod (the worst case is two runs table entries, not a corruption)

## Related PRs

- Depends on / pairs with #1631 (heartbeat + 3 data-quality fixes). Order: merge #1631 first, then this. They can also merge independently — no shared file edits.
- Backend-only. No customer-portal or landing-page changes.

## Notion task

Will be filed alongside the EventBridge migration task (#33).

title: feat(loops): closed-loop framework skeleton (Phase 1a)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The onboarding completion loop is a working implementation of a closed-loop AI system but its 5 layers (sensor → policy → tools → quality gate → learning) are tangled into a monolithic implementation tied to "onboarding" — bucket name, runs table, env vars, function names, and prompts all hardcoded. Adding a second loop (e.g. for `/ai-eval`) means duplicating that code, not configuring it.

## What this fixes (after)
This PR is **Phase 1a of the templatize-loop-apparatus task** — pure new files that establish the 5-layer framework's type interfaces, injected ports, and central registry. **No behavior change to the existing onboarding loop.** Subsequent phases port the onboarding implementation into the framework (Phase 2) and instance the framework for `/ai-eval` (Phase 3).

What this PR ships:

- `backend/src/loops/core/types.ts` — the 5 layer interfaces (`EventSource`, `RuleSet`, `MutationTools`, `ApprovalGate`, `LearningStore`) + `LoopManifest` + `LoopRunResult` + branded ID types
- `backend/src/loops/core/ports.ts` — injected dependencies (`S3Port`, `DynamoPort`, `BedrockPort`, `SlackPort`, `ClockPort`, `LoggerPort`)
- `backend/src/loops/index.ts` — `LOOP_REGISTRY` with `register*` / `get*` for each layer + loop manifests
- `backend/src/loops/MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md` — authoritative schema reference
- `backend/src/loops/README.md` — entry point with "add a loop in 4 steps" recipe
- `backend/src/__tests__/loops.registry.test.ts` — 17 cases covering register/get round-trips, duplicate detection, missing-impl error paths, reset helper

**Package boundary**: `loops/core/` has zero imports from elsewhere in agentweb — verified via `grep -rE "^import.*from '" backend/src/loops/core/` returning empty. This is the constraint that makes the package open-source-ready.

## How to test
1. Pull this branch locally: `git checkout harsha/loops-framework`
2. Run `cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit`
3. **Expected**: exit 0, no output
4. Run `npx jest src/__tests__/loops.registry.test.ts --no-coverage`
5. **Expected**: `Test Suites: 1 passed, 1 total. Tests: 17 passed, 17 total.`
6. Visit `backend/src/loops/README.md` and `backend/src/loops/MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md` — confirm they read as a usable reference
7. Grep for boundary violation: `grep -rE "^import.*from '" backend/src/loops/core/`
8. **Expected**: empty output

## Edge cases to check
- The branded ID types (`LoopId`, `RunId`, etc.) — confirm TypeScript prevents passing a `RunId` where a `LoopId` is expected. Try editing one of the tests to swap and `npx tsc` should error.
- The `_resetRegistryForTesting()` helper — confirm it's only callable from `loops/index.ts`'s own export, so production code can't accidentally wipe the registry.

## Test Evidence
- TypeScript: `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (zero errors)
- Unit tests: 17 passed, 0 failed (`loops.registry.test.ts`)
- Package boundary: zero imports from outside `loops/core/`
- Tested as: branched from `origin/harsha/dev` (commit 359f9384)

## Files changed
**New (all under `backend/src/loops/`):**
- `core/types.ts` — 5 layer interfaces + manifest + run result (310 LOC)
- `core/ports.ts` — injected ports (238 LOC)
- `index.ts` — LOOP_REGISTRY (174 LOC)
- `MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md` — docs
- `README.md` — docs

**New (under `backend/src/__tests__/`):**
- `loops.registry.test.ts` — 17 test cases (197 LOC)

## What was NOT tested
- Real S3 / DynamoDB / Bedrock / Slack calls — the ports are interface-only in Phase 1a. Concrete implementations land in Phase 2 (when the onboarding loop ports in) and Phase 3 (for the lander instance). The ports here have no runtime code yet, so there's nothing to integration-test.
- The policy DSL evaluator — defined as a type (`Condition = string`) here, but the parser/evaluator implementation lands in Phase 1b along with `loops/core/orchestrator.ts` and the smoke harness.

Maps to acceptance criteria 1, 5 (Phase 1a portions only — full criteria proven in later phases):
