title: feat(loops): wire daily cron + Slack digest DM + Notion task creation (Phase 4)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The closed-loop framework's ingestion side shipped + deployed in PR #1634 (events land in Dev-AW-LoopEvents), but the **decision side was disconnected**:

- The lander loop was registered with `InMemoryEventSource` (couldn't see real DDB writes)
- No cron was scheduled, so the orchestrator never ran on its own
- The quality gate was `CaptureGate` (collected mutations in memory, never posted Slack DM)
- Tools layer was `SpecOutputTool` (produced JSON only, never created real Notion tasks)

Net effect: events were flowing INTO production DDB but nothing was reading them or producing decisions. Loop ran end-to-end only via manual `liveSmokeTest.ts`.

## What this fixes (after)
End-to-end production wiring — daily cron fires, real Slack DM lands, real Notion tasks get created.

1. **`loops/adapters/awsAdapters.ts`** — binds framework ports (S3, DynamoDB, Slack, Bedrock, Clock, Logger) to aws-sdk v2 + @slack/web-api the backend already uses. Lives outside `loops/core/` to preserve the package boundary.

2. **`loops/instances/ai-eval-funnel/notionDigestTool.ts`** — real `MutationTools<AiEvalProposalPayload>` impl. POSTs to Notion pages API for each proposal, creates a task in the Sprint Tasks DB tagged "Landing Site" with triggering data + proposed change spec inline as code blocks.

3. **`loops/instances/ai-eval-funnel/cron.ts`** — `registerAiEvalFunnelForProduction()` + `runAiEvalLoopOnce()`. Wires real DDB sensor, NotionDigestTool, CaptureGate, InMemoryLearningStore. After orchestrator runs, drains the gate and posts a single Slack digest DM to Harsha with all proposed fixes inline as Notion-task links.

4. **`app.ts`** — swaps `registerAiEvalFunnel()` → `registerAiEvalFunnelForProduction()` at boot.

5. **`server.ts`** — adds daily cron at 16:00 UTC (8am PT, one hour offset from onboarding loop). Gated by `AI_EVAL_LOOP_ENABLED=true` env var so it doesn't fire on first deploy until IAM is verified.

## How to test
1. Pull this branch + run `cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit` — expect clean.
2. Set `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, `NOTION_API_KEY`, and `AI_EVAL_LOOP_ENABLED=true` env vars.
3. Run the existing live smoke test against real DDB: `npx ts-node src/loops/scripts/liveSmokeTest.ts --seed-fake-events`.
4. **Expected**: 3 rules fire as before. Now with the cron wired, restart the backend and the daily cron registers at boot — verify via logs: `[AiEvalLoop] Initialized — first run at 16:00 UTC (in N min)`.
5. To trigger the cron immediately (test path), import `runAiEvalLoopOnce` and call it from a one-shot script.

## Edge cases to check
- `AI_EVAL_LOOP_ENABLED` unset → cron silently skipped, route still works for ingestion.
- `NOTION_API_KEY` missing → NotionDigestTool returns mutation with `error` set; daily DM surfaces "⚠️ NOTION_API_KEY env var missing" inline; orchestrator continues.
- `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` missing → cron logs error but doesn't crash; DM not posted (events still flow into DDB on next tick).
- Multiple EB instances → all of them schedule the cron; each fires at 16:00 UTC. Mitigated by NotionDigestTool's idempotency (creating duplicate Notion tasks is annoying but not destructive). Future: gate cron to single leader via DDB lock.

## Test Evidence
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- 50 existing framework tests still pass (`loops.registry.test.ts` + `loops.policyDsl.test.ts`)
- No new tests in this PR for the cron wrapper — the wrapper is integration-shaped (real Notion + Slack + DDB). Real verification will be the first cron firing on production.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/loops/adapters/awsAdapters.ts` (new, 191 LOC)
- `backend/src/loops/instances/ai-eval-funnel/notionDigestTool.ts` (new, 201 LOC)
- `backend/src/loops/instances/ai-eval-funnel/cron.ts` (new, ~145 LOC)
- `backend/src/app.ts` — swap register fn
- `backend/src/server.ts` — add cron block (~30 LOC)

## What was NOT tested
- The daily cron actually firing on production — requires deploy + waiting for 16:00 UTC.
- Real Notion task creation via NotionDigestTool — depends on NOTION_API_KEY being set in EB env + valid Notion permissions. Verify via the next cron run's Slack DM.
- IAM permissions for the backend EB role on Dev-AW-LoopEvents — empirical: writes succeeded earlier this session via the POST route, so role has it. Reads should too.

## Related PRs
- Phase 1+3 framework: agentweb #1634 (already merged + deployed)
- Lander telemetry: agentweb-landing-page #36 + #38 (already merged + deployed)
- This PR: Phase 4 — turns the framework from "ingestion only" to "ingestion + daily decisions"

## Pre-deploy checklist
- [ ] Set `AI_EVAL_LOOP_ENABLED=true` on Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3 EB env
- [ ] Verify `NOTION_API_KEY` is set on the same env (existing usage by other features)
- [ ] Verify `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` is set (existing usage)
- [ ] Verify IAM role has dynamodb:PutItem + dynamodb:Query on Dev-AW-LoopEvents

title: fix: default to Free tier instead of Basic for users with null subscriptionType
body:
## Summary

- `getUserSubscriptionType()` was returning `"Basic"` as a fallback when a user had no `subscriptionType` set in the DB — this gave them full all-access tier unintentionally
- The `/me` endpoint error handler was also hardcoding `'Basic'` as the fallback on any subscription lookup error

## Root cause

New users get `subscriptionType: "Free"` set via a separate `updateUser()` call after `createUser()`. If that write failed (or for any legacy user with a null field), `getUserSubscriptionType()` hit the `|| "Basic"` fallback — displaying them as "Basic" in the admin panel and granting full page/skill access.

title: fix(agent-mode): instrument first-attempt failures even when retry rescues
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The lander loop's "loop ran against REAL data" finding from 2026-05-25 surfaced this:

> ⚠️ CRITICAL: instrumentation gap (loop is blind to its most important signal)
> You said "the LLM shat itself" is a known real failure mode, but ZERO sessions in 30 days have `metadata.isErrorMessage = true`.

Root cause found today by reading the catch block at `agentModeController.ts:5411-5469`:
1. The fire-and-forget agent run catches the first-attempt failure
2. Restarts the worker, retries
3. **If the retry succeeds, NO `isErrorMessage` marker is ever persisted**
4. Sessions appear "successful" — masking the first-attempt failure that the user actually experienced (longer wait, possibly different output)

Result: out of 95 production eval sessions in 30 days, the existing both-attempts-failed path produced **0** `isErrorMessage` markers (the data the loop's sensor queries). The retry path was rescuing essentially all failures, but the data showed perfect health.

## What this fixes
1. **First-attempt failure ALWAYS persists a tagged marker** (system-role message with `metadata.isErrorMessage = true`). System-role messages are stripped by `filterMessagesForClient` so the user doesn't see them in their chat UI, but the sensor's raw scan path sees them. Debug context (error name/code/httpStatus) is packed into the content field as JSON.
2. **If retry also fails, additionally fires `loopEventsEmitter.fireEvalFailed`** to `Dev-AW-LoopEvents`. This means the loop's anon-event sensor gets the signal too — defense in depth against the session-scan path missing it.

Net effect on the loop's data:
- **Retry-rescued sessions** → 1 `isErrorMessage` marker (was 0)
- **Terminal-failed sessions** → 2 markers + 1 `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` row (was 1 marker)
- **eval-failing rule** can now fire on real production data instead of staying blind

## How to test
1. Pull this branch + start backend locally OR wait for deploy
2. Force a first-attempt failure by mocking `generateSessionResponse` to throw once, then succeed
3. Check session messages → expect a system-role message with `[telemetry] First-attempt agent failure (retry will follow): ...` and `metadata.isErrorMessage = true`
4. Verify the user-facing chat UI does NOT show this message (filterMessagesForClient strips system role)
5. After both attempts fail, also verify a row appears in `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` with `eventType = 'eval_failed'`

## Edge cases to check
- The retry-on-restart-worker path: the `restartWorker()` call at line 5416 might itself throw. The catch around it is preserved.
- `planTitle === 'AI_GTM_Position_Eval'` check on the `fireEvalFailed` call — non-eval plans don't fire to `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` (correct — that table is loop-scoped).
- The `firstErr?.message` slicing at 200 chars per side — covers most error messages, drops the long Bedrock validation errors. Slicing limit is intentional (DDB item size).

title: fix(crm): prevent duplicate LinkedIn connection accepted notifications
body:
## Root cause

Two bugs in PR #1643 caused the notification to fire on every 10-minute cron run instead of once.

**Bug 1 — broken watermark in `getLatestConnectedAt`**

`AW-UnipileConnections` has `accountId` as PK and `memberId` (a string like `"ACoABC..."`) as SK. `getLatestConnectedAt` did a DynamoDB `query` with `ScanIndexForward: false, Limit: 1` — which returns the item whose SK sorts _last_ alphabetically, not the one with the highest `connectedAt` timestamp. So the watermark was always garbage, and `syncConnectionsForAccount` treated all 150 fetched connections (3 pages × 50) as "new" on every run.

**Fix:** `upsertConnections` now also writes a sentinel row with `SK='__latest__'` (via a conditional update — only advances forward). `getLatestConnectedAt` reads it directly via `GetItem` instead of a query.

**Bug 2 — no dedup guard in `notifyNewConnections`**

Even if the watermark was fixed, `notifyNewConnections` had no check to see if a notification was already sent for a given lead's connection event. If the same lead matched, it would re-send.

**Fix:** Before notifying, check `lead.system.linkedInConnectionNotifiedAt`. If set, skip. Otherwise mark it (via `updateLead` with `skipFieldNamesUpdate: true`) _before_ sending the email, so race conditions from parallel cron runs are also blocked.

## Test plan
- [ ] All 9 tests in `linkedInConnectionSync.notifyNewConnections.test.ts` pass (includes 2 new dedup tests)
- [ ] TypeScript compiles cleanly
- [ ] Verify in prod: connection accepted notification fires exactly once per lead

title: fix(coding-agent): fail fast with clear message on 403 authorization errors
body:
## Root Cause

When an org member without edit permissions (e.g. `harsha@agentweb.pro`) tried to edit a landing page owned by `founders@agentweb.pro` via the `coding_agent` tool:

1. The pre-flight `list_files` call **succeeds** (view access is allowed for org members when `enabled: true`)
2. The LLM starts iterating and calls `edit_file`
3. The `PUT /github-edit` call returns **403** "Not authorized to edit this landing page"
4. Previously: the 403 error was fed back into the LLM as a tool error, wasting iterations before eventually failing
5. Now: the 403 is detected immediately and the agent returns a clear, actionable error message

The authorization model is correct — `harsha` needs to be added to `shareSettings.landingPages.editors` in the org settings (Settings → Org Sharing → Landing Pages) by the org owner (`founders@agentweb.pro`) to gain edit access.

## Changes

- **`codingAgentService.ts`**: Added `is403Error()` helper. Two fail-fast paths:
  1. Pre-flight `list_files` 403 → re-throw (caught at `runCodingAgent` level)
  2. Tool execution 403 → re-throw from inner catch (propagates to outer catch)
  - Outer catch and `runCodingAgent` `.catch()` both convert 403 to a clear user-facing message with actionable guidance

- **`codingAgentService.test.ts`**: Added 2 failing tests (written before implementation):
  1. 403 on `edit_file` write → fail fast, no second LLM iteration
  2. 403 on pre-flight `list_files` → fail fast, no LLM call at all

title: feat(slack): wire ✅ on ai-eval-funnel daily DM to dispatch cloud-dev runs
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The daily ai-eval-funnel Slack DM told Harsha to "React: ✅ ship all" but **nothing on the backend listened for the reaction**. Notion tasks tagged `Landing Site` piled up and never got picked up by cloud-dev. The checkmark was a lie.

## What this fixes (after)
- `POST /api/slack/events` now handles `reaction_added` events.
- When Harsha (U08TM4QFQ1L) reacts ✅ on an Emma-bot DM containing `AI Eval Funnel — daily run`, the handler parses every Notion page URL out of the message, fetches each task's title + content, and calls `launchEnvironment(pageId, title, content, '2bf09247-c951-812a-bd0a-000bd4c05bbf')` for each. Status updates are posted as thread replies.
- New in-memory `loopDispatchTracker` (`backend/src/services/loopDispatchTracker.ts`) dedupes by `messageTs` so a second ✅ on the same DM is a no-op.
- Daily DM template in `cron.ts` updated to reflect the new behavior: `React ✅ to dispatch all to cloud-dev | ❌ to skip | 🛑 to pause loop`.

## Slack scope status
- **`reactions:read`**: required for Slack to deliver `reaction_added` events. The bot already calls `slackClient.reactions.get(...)` in `backend/src/services/onboardingLoopApproval.ts:218` in production, so the scope itself is granted.
- **What may still need to be enabled**: the `reaction_added` event subscription in the Slack app's Event Subscriptions config at https://api.slack.com/apps/<appId>/event-subscriptions. If this PR ships and the handler isn't firing in prod, that's the first place to check. The handler degrades gracefully (loud console.error pointing at the Slack admin URL) if scope/subscription is missing.

## Behavioral assertions verified
Mapped to the 7 human-written acceptance criteria from the Notion spec:

| # | Acceptance criterion | Test / verification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | POST `/api/slack/events` handles `reaction_added` | `slack.aiEvalReaction.test.ts` — all 9 tests POST a `reaction_added` payload to the live router |
| 2 | Dispatches only when ALL guard conditions are true | Tests: dispatches happy path; ignores non-Harsha user; ignores non-✅ reaction; ignores non-DM channel; ignores message without `AI Eval Funnel — daily run` marker; ignores message not from Emma bot; ignores already-dispatched ts |
| 3 | Parses every Notion page URL, calls `launchEnvironment` per id with Sprint Tasks DSID | Test "dispatches cloud-dev runs when Harsha reacts ✅ on the daily Emma DM" asserts both page IDs from a 2-URL fixture are dispatched with the canonical data-source ID |
| 4 | Thread reply: `Dispatching N…` then completion summary; `⚠️ Failed: <error>` on failure | Tests: happy path asserts both replies; partial-success test ("reports partial-success when one launchEnvironment throws") asserts `Launched 1/2` summary + per-task failure note |
| 5 | Idempotency: second ✅ on same `event.item.ts` is a no-op | Tests: "skips dispatch on duplicate ✅ for the same messageTs" + 10 unit tests on `loopDispatchTracker` (100% coverage) |
| 6 | Missing `reactions:read` scope → clear console.error, no silent fail | Test: "logs a clear error and returns 200 when Slack returns missing_scope" asserts the error message includes `reactions:read` and `api.slack.com/apps` |
| 7 | DM template in `cron.ts` updated | `cron.ts:143` now reads `React ✅ to dispatch all to cloud-dev  \|  ❌ to skip  \|  🛑 to pause loop` (commit `fd91d3ad`) |

## How to test
1. Wait for backend deploy to dev or merge to `harsha/dev` and stage.
2. Trigger a fresh daily DM by running `runAiEvalLoopOnce()` from a Node REPL on the deployed backend (or wait until the next 8am PT cron). Confirm the DM body reads `React ✅ to dispatch all to cloud-dev …`.
3. From the @harshmoney Slack account, react ✅ on the DM message in Emma's DM channel.
4. **Expected**: Within ~5 seconds, a thread reply appears: `🚀 Dispatching N cloud-dev runs…`. Within ~30 seconds, a second thread reply appears: `✅ Launched X/N cloud-dev runs:` with one bullet per task.
5. **Expected**: AWS Console → EC2 shows N new t3.xlarge instances spinning up tagged `agentweb-test-env-notion-<pageId>`.
6. **Expected**: Each linked Notion task gets its `Instance ID` / `Public IP` / `SG ID` populated by `launchEnvironment` once the instance is reachable.
7. Re-react ✅ on the same DM. **Expected**: no new thread reply, no new EC2 instances (idempotency).

## Edge cases to check
- React ❌ — no-op (only `white_check_mark` triggers).
- A non-Harsha user reacts ✅ — no-op.
- React ✅ on a non-daily-digest DM Emma sent — no-op (marker check).
- React ✅ on the daily DM, then trigger backend redeploy, then re-react — **may re-dispatch once** (in-memory tracker reset). Documented v1 trade-off.

## Test Evidence
- New tests:
  - `backend/src/__tests__/loopDispatchTracker.test.ts` — 10 tests, 100% coverage on `loopDispatchTracker.ts`
  - `backend/src/__tests__/slack.aiEvalReaction.test.ts` — 9 tests covering all 7 acceptance criteria

title: feat(ai-eval-funnel): enrich daily DM + Notion tasks with LLM root-cause analysis + ranked fixes
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The daily ai-eval-funnel cron's Slack DM and the Notion tasks it creates report **what** went wrong (the rule's static `hypothesis`) but offer no investigation into **why** and no ranked candidate fixes. Harsha re-derives root cause every morning. Example from 2026-05-27: `capture-broken` fired with "Lots of landings but very few form submits" — but the real root cause is that `<LandedTracker />` fires on every site pathname while `form_submitted` only fires from `/ai-eval`. The loop currently has no way to surface that.

## What this fixes (after)
A new `rcaEnricher.ts` module calls claude-sonnet-4-6 via Bedrock (with prompt caching on the cacheable system prompt) for each fired rule. body:
## Sprint Review: 2026-05-27 — 2 PRs

**How to review**: Go through the testing plan below. Comment on this PR with fix/revert notes. Anything you don't mention = approved to ship.

**Comment format**:
- `fix #NNN: what's wrong` — swarm will fix it
- `revert #NNN` — will be removed before shipping

Both PRs are focused on the ai-eval-funnel closed loop. They solve a related pair of problems: the daily DM/Notion output is now decision-ready (RCA + ranked fixes), and the ✅ reaction on the DM now actually dispatches cloud-dev runs instead of falling into the void.

---

### PR #1663: feat(slack): wire ✅ on ai-eval-funnel daily DM to dispatch cloud-dev runs
**Risk**: Medium | **Type**: feat | **Files**: 4 (1 new module, 2 modified, 2 new test files)

**What was wrong (before)**: The daily 9 AM Slack DM said "React: ✅ ship all" but nothing on the backend listened for the reaction. `routes/slack.ts:/api/slack/events` only handled `app_mention`. Cron created Notion tasks tagged `Landing Site` then exited — no dispatcher picked them up.

**What this fixes (after)**: Adds a `reaction_added` handler to the existing Slack events endpoint. Gated on (a) reaction = ✅, (b) reactor = Harsha (U08TM4QFQ1L), (c) DM channel, (d) message authored by Emma bot, (e) text contains `AI Eval Funnel — daily run`, (f) not already dispatched. On match: parses Notion page URLs from the message, dispatches each via `launchEnvironment(pageId, title, content, SPRINT_TASKS_DATA_SOURCE)` from `services/devEnvService.ts`, posts thread confirmation. In-memory idempotency tracker prevents double-dispatch.

**How to test**:
1. Wait for tomorrow's 9 AM PT daily DM from Emma (channel `D095JNTNNPM`), OR trigger ad-hoc via `runAiEvalLoopOnce()`.
2. React ✅ on the DM.
3. **Expected**: Within ~2s, a thread reply appears: `🚀 Dispatching N cloud-dev runs...`
4. Within ~30s, a follow-up thread reply: `✅ Launched N/N cloud-dev runs:` followed by a bulleted list of Notion task titles.
5. Open AWS EC2 console (us-west-2).
6. **Expected**: N new EC2 instances spinning up, tagged `agentweb-test-env-notion-<pageId>`.
7. React ✅ on the **same** DM a second time.
8. **Expected**: Nothing happens. No new thread reply, no new EC2 instances. Tracker dedupes by `messageTs`.

**Edge case to check**: If the Emma Slack app doesn't have the `reaction_added` event subscription enabled at api.slack.com/apps, the handler never fires. The `reactions:read` scope is already granted (used by onboardingLoopApproval). The event subscription is a separate toggle — verify before relying on this in prod.

---

### PR #1664: feat(ai-eval-funnel): enrich daily DM + Notion tasks with LLM root-cause analysis + ranked fixes
**Risk**: Low | **Type**: feat | **Files**: 6 (1 new module, 2 modified, 3 new test files)

**What was wrong (before)**: The daily DM and the Notion tasks it spawned reported the rule's static `hypothesis` string — what went wrong, but not why or how to fix. Harsha re-derived root cause every morning. Example: `capture-broken` hypothesis was generic copy advice when the real root cause was a measurement bug (`<LandedTracker />` over-counting denominator).

**What this fixes (after)**: New `rcaEnricher.ts` module calls Bedrock (claude-sonnet-4-6 + prompt caching) per fired rule with the rule id + triggering stats + mutation surface. Returns `{topHypotheses[], rankedFixes[]}` — each fix has `{title, impact, confidence, cost_sp, why_this_rank}`. Top fix appears in the Slack DM as a one-liner; full ranked list goes into the Notion task body under new `## Root cause hypotheses` and `## Ranked fixes` sections. Graceful fallback if Bedrock errors/times out (falls back to existing `rule.hypothesis`, marks `error` in the Notion body).

**How to test**:
1. Wait for tomorrow's 9 AM PT daily DM.
2. **Expected**: For each fired rule, a new indented line under the rule: `   ↳ Top fix: <truncated title>`.
3. Click any `fix(ai-eval-funnel): ...` link in the DM to open the corresponding Notion task.
4. **Expected**: Task body now has two new sections between Summary and Triggering data: `## Root cause hypotheses` (3–5 bullets) and `## Ranked fixes` (≥3 paragraphs with impact/confidence/cost).
5. **Quality check**: confirm the hypotheses reference specific components/events/files (e.g., `<LandedTracker />` over-counts denominator), not generic copy advice.

**Edge case to check**: First production run will surface real latency. Typical Sonnet 4.6 + 2K-token completions run 2-4s. Spec accepts +30s in the typical case; worst case (25s timeout × 7 fired rules serially) is 175s — if that bites, a follow-up should parallelize per-proposal calls.

---

### High-Risk Items — CTO: start here
- **#1663 (Medium risk)**: New public-facing Slack event handler. Guard chain is tight (5 conditions + idempotency) so the dispatch path is narrow. Bedrock-side risk is bounded by the per-call 25s timeout and the existing manifest budget cap. Rollback: `git revert <merge-commit>` for #1663 on harsha/dev, then push.
- **#1664 (Low risk)**: Adds an LLM call inside the daily cron. Worst case is a slower DM, not a broken one — fallback path is exercised by tests.

- Each sub-PR: CI green (10,845 backend tests, 0 failures on #1664; 10,843 on #1663).

- Real Bedrock latency under realistic stats payloads.
- Whether `reaction_added` event subscription is currently enabled in the Emma Slack app config (one-click admin step at api.slack.com/apps).

- Everything: `git revert -m 1 <mega-merge>` on main once this lands.

body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The frontend `OutreachCrmSave` component (sub-task 7, already merged to customer-portal `harsha/dev`) POSTs to `/api/onboarding/outreach/save` with `{ icpId, prospects, drafts }` and expects `{ leadListId }` back. That endpoint did not exist, so the FE rendered a 404 in its error state.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds `POST /api/onboarding/outreach/save`. It creates a new CRM Lead List named after the ICP (`Outreach — {icpLabel || icpId}`) and persists each kept prospect as a lead with its Emma-drafted message attached, owned by the authenticated user. Reuses the exact same crmDb lead-import path Emma's `import_leads_from_search` tool uses (`crmDb.createLeadList` + `crmDb.batchCreateLeads`), so dedup, atomic lead counting, and field-name merging behave identically. The drafted message rides on the lead `notes` field; ICP attribution goes in the `system.icpSource` sidecar (same as the import tool). **Pure CRM scope — does not touch agent-mode / Emma core internals.**

## How to test
1. Log in as a normal user (`test@example.com` / `Test123!`).
2. Go through outreach onboarding to the prospect-reveal screen, keep a few prospects, let Emma draft messages, and hit Save.
3. **Expected**: the request returns `200 { leadListId: "list_..." }` and the FE advances past the save step (no 404).
4. Go to `/crm` and open the lead lists.
5. **Expected**: a new list named `Outreach — {your ICP}` exists, containing one lead per kept prospect, each with the drafted message visible in its `notes`.

API-level check (curl):
```
# 401 — no auth
curl -i -X POST <env>/api/onboarding/outreach/save -d '{"icpId":"x","prospects":[{"id":"a","name":"A","linkedin_url":""}],"drafts":{}}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
# 400 — empty prospects
curl -i -X POST <env>/api/onboarding/outreach/save -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"icpId":"x","prospects":[],"drafts":{}}'
# 200 — happy path returns {leadListId}
curl -i -X POST <env>/api/onboarding/outreach/save -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"icpId":"x","icpLabel":"Founders","prospects":[{"id":"a","name":"Jane Doe","linkedin_url":"https://www.linkedin.com/in/janedoe","headline":"Director of Growth","company":"Acme"}],"drafts":{"a":"Hi Jane"}}'
```

## Edge cases to check
- A prospect id with no entry in `drafts` is saved with no note (not a crash).

title: chore(security): stop tracking .notion-token + .notion-page-id, add to .gitignore
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High (security hygiene)

## What was wrong (before)
The repo root tracked two files that were never gitignored:
- **`.notion-token`** — a real Notion integration token (`ntn_` prefix, 51 chars). Leaked credential.
- **`.notion-page-id`** — Notion page id (config, not secret, but shouldn't be tracked).

Surfaced during the 2026-05-27 dev↔main sync.

## What this fixes (after)
- `git rm --cached` both files (stops tracking, keeps local copies on disk)
- Adds both to `.gitignore` with a comment pointing at the real source of truth

## Why this is safe (no runtime regression)
The token's source of truth is already **AWS Secrets Manager** (`agentweb/test-env/notion-token`). The committed repo-root file was redundant:
- `test-env/user-data-dev-auto.sh:283,396-397` — cloud-dev EC2 instances fetch the token from Secrets Manager at boot and **write** `.notion-token` to the instance's app dir themselves. So `.claude-run.sh`'s `cat .notion-token` still works on the instance.
- `backend/src/services/devEnvService.ts:28` reads from `getSecret("agentweb/test-env/notion-token")`.
- `test-env-access/server.js:298` reads from Secrets Manager (line 369 file-read is a fallback the boot script satisfies).

Nothing reads the *committed* repo-root copy as a source of truth.

## ⚠️ REQUIRED follow-up (cannot be done in this PR)
**Rotate the Notion token.** `git rm --cached` does NOT purge it from git history — the old token remains in past commits and on the remote, so it's compromised regardless. Steps:
1. In Notion → Settings → Integrations, regenerate the integration token.
2. Update the AWS secret: `aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id agentweb/test-env/notion-token --secret-string '<new-token>'`
3. (Optional, heavier) Purge from history with `git filter-repo` if the repo's history is considered sensitive — coordinate since it rewrites shared history.

## How to test
1. `git check-ignore .notion-token .notion-page-id` → both echoed (ignored). ✓ verified
2. Confirm a fresh clone of this branch has neither file tracked: `git ls-files | grep notion` → empty.
3. Spin a cloud-dev test env → confirm the instance still gets a working `.notion-token` (written at boot from Secrets Manager) and `.claude-run.sh` posts its Notion status update.

## Files changed
- `.gitignore` (+6)
- `.notion-token` (removed from tracking)
- `.notion-page-id` (removed from tracking)

## What was NOT tested
- A live cloud-dev boot cycle (the boot-time write path is unchanged, but worth a smoke on the next test-env spin).

- **Root cause:** When a draft branch diverges from main (e.g. after a previous conflict was resolved directly on main with "ours" strategy), GitHub's `/merges` API returns 409. The original handler surfaced this as an unrecoverable error to the user.
- **Fix:** On 409, fetch the draft branch tip SHA and force-update `main` to point at it (`PATCH /git/refs/heads/main` with `force: true`). This is safe because landing page repos are exclusively managed by our system — there are no external contributors whose work could be clobbered.
- **Test:** Updated the "merge conflict → 409" test to verify the fallback path returns 200 with the draft tip SHA as `merge_commit_sha`.

## Immediate unblock
Vivian Health's page `3f200cb9-5bfa-467c-83c4-eb9be1275420` is stuck — its draft branch `draft/f3e9af36-7f3f-46` has diverged from main after an earlier conflict-resolution commit. After this fix deploys, Emma can retry `publish_landing_page_changes` and it will succeed.

## Summary

- Fixes relay (`test-env-access/server.js`) which was hardcoding `--model us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` (Bedrock) for all follow-up prompts, ignoring the Vertex AI setup from `claude-run.sh`

The `runClaude()` function spread `process.env` (which includes `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` from `.bashrc`) into child process env and hardcoded the Sonnet model — so after any restart the relay ignored the Vertex setup done by `claude-run.sh`.

## Summary
Adds the ability for admins to choose which LLM model evaluates sessions, per scoring judge, in the **Admin → Scoring Judges** tab. Both custom judges and the **Default** judge now have an **LLM Model** dropdown. Judges without an explicit model continue to use the standard fast scorer (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`).

## Changes
**Backend**
- `routes/settings.ts`
  - `GET /scoring-judges` now returns `availableModels` (live/streaming models filtered out).
  - `POST`/`PUT /scoring-judges` persist (and clear) a per-judge `llmModel`.
  - `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /scoring-judges/default-prompt` now read/write/reset a `default-scoring-model` setting for the Default judge.
- `services/sessionScoringService.ts`
  - `scoreSessionWithJudge` uses `judge.llmModel` (falls back to default for unset/empty).
  - `scoreSession` (default scorer) honors the configured `default-scoring-model` via new `getDefaultScoringModel()`.
  - Raised the JSON scoring budget to **2000** tokens (`SCORING_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS`). Reasoning models like `gemini-3.5-flash` consume the completion budget while "thinking"; at the old 300-token cap they returned truncated/empty JSON. Non-thinking models still stop after ~80 tokens, so there is no added cost for them.

**Frontend (`partner-portal`)**
- `ScoringJudgesTab.tsx`: moved the **LLM Model** dropdown above the System Prompt (it was previously below the fold and not visible), added a **Model** column to the table, and wired model selection for the Default judge.

## Why a model picker
Empirical comparison on 24 real dev sessions (default prompt, identical inputs):
| | gemini-3.1-flash-lite | gemini-3.5-flash |
|---|---|---|
| Latency (mean) | ~1.0s | ~3.1s |
| Score distribution | 19/23 scored "5" (grade inflation) | spread across 3/4/5 |
| Agreement | 96% within ±1, agree on low scores | |

`gemini-3.1-flash-lite` stays the default (fast/cheap, reliably flags bad sessions); `gemini-3.5-flash` is now selectable for stricter, more discriminating evaluation.

## Tests
- New: `sessionScoring.modelSelection.test.ts` (10), `settings.scoringJudges.test.ts` (12).
- Updated `sessionScoring.contentFormatting.test.ts` for the new token budget.

title: fix(cloud-dev): re-assert Vertex env in relay follow-up runs
body:
## Summary
- Follow-up Notion comments on cloud-dev boxes were failing: `claude-opus-4-8` got routed to **Bedrock** (where the id is invalid) → `400 The provided model identifier is invalid`. On other boxes the same root cause silently fell back to Bedrock sonnet (wrong model + leaked context).
- **Root cause:** `runClaude` in `test-env-access/server.js` spawns claude via `bash -lc` — a **login shell** that re-sources `~/.bashrc`. `user-data-dev-auto.sh` writes `export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` + `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` into `~/.bashrc`, so those re-export **after** the `childEnv` overrides are applied, defeating them. The JS-level `delete childEnv.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` is useless against the shell re-adding it.
- **Fix:** when using Vertex, prepend an inline `unset CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK; export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1 ...` to the command string so it runs *after* `~/.bashrc` is sourced and takes final precedence.

## Verification (live box i-0b957658e7f5d0e08)
Before — child shell ends up with both flags set:
```
BEDROCK=1 VERTEX=1 BEARER=SET
```
After inline fix:
```
BEDROCK=unset VERTEX=1 BEARER=
```

## Test plan
- [ ] New cloud-dev box: post a follow-up Notion comment → confirm it runs on Vertex `claude-opus-4-8` (no 400, model label shows Opus 4.8 (Google Vertex))
- [ ] Bedrock-only fallback path unchanged when no Vertex SA is configured

title: fix(coding-agent): route claude-opus-4-8 to Vertex (fixes '400 invalid model identifier')
body:
## Problem

The `coding_agent` tool returned **`400 The provided model identifier is invalid`** on every call (iterations=1, no edits), starting when the coding-agent default model was switched to **`claude-opus-4-8`**.

Reported by matthew@agentweb.pro for Lyndi Thompson (lyndi@every.io) during a landing-page editing session.

## Root cause

The coding agent runs its agentic loop through a **Bedrock-only** client (`getBedrockClient()` → `AnthropicBedrock`). `claude-opus-4-8` is a **Google Vertex AI** model — addressed by a bare `claude-*` id with no `anthropic.` prefix and not available on this Bedrock account. The loop handed that id straight to Bedrock, which rejected it on the first iteration before any file edit. The main `agentModeService` already routes `claude-*` → Vertex; the coding agent was never taught that routing.

## Fix

`backend/src/services/codingAgentService.ts`:
- Add a native-Anthropic-format **Vertex client** (raw `rawPredict` HTTP — Vertex speaks the same Messages format the coding agent already builds, so no request/response conversion is needed).
- Add `getClientForModel(model)`: `claude-*` → Vertex, `anthropic.*` → Bedrock.
- Route the loop through `getClientForModel(model)` instead of the hardcoded Bedrock client.
- `callWithRetry` now retries transient 429/5xx from either provider and uses the injectable sleep fn.
- Export `_setVertexClientForTest` for testability.

## Tests

`backend/src/__tests__/codingAgentService.test.ts` — 3 new tests (52 total pass):
- `claude-opus-4-8` routes to the Vertex client (not Bedrock), id passed through unchanged
- `anthropic.*` models route to the Bedrock client (not Vertex)
- transient 5xx from the Vertex client is retried, then succeeds

## Verification

- `npx tsc` clean; `npm test` for the suite: **52/52 pass**.
- **Live probe** against the real dev Vertex endpoint with `claude-opus-4-8` returned `"OK"` — confirming the model id is valid there (vs. the 400 Bedrock threw), so routing to Vertex resolves the error.
- Backend restarted in the cloud dev env, health endpoint returns 200 with the fix live.

title: fix(agent-mode): describe_image works with Vertex Claude Opus 4.8
body:
## Problem
`describe_image` started failing with `400 ... Input tag 'image_url' ... does not match expected tags (image, document, ...)` for all users once **Claude Opus 4.8 (Vertex AI)** became the default agent-mode model.

`describe_image` does **not** use the chat's selected model — it always uses the configured `agent_mode_default_model` (the model arg was never populated). When that default was switched to `claude-opus-4-8` (Vertex), every call routed to the Vertex path, which:

1. **`getVertexClient`** forwarded OpenAI-style `{type:'image_url'}` content blocks verbatim — Anthropic-on-Vertex only accepts native `{type:'image', source:{...}}` blocks (Bedrock has `convertContentToBedrockBlocks`; Vertex had no equivalent).
2. **`describeImage`** only base64-downloaded images for `anthropic.*` (Bedrock), not `claude-*` (Vertex), so it sent a bare private-S3 URL Anthropic's fetcher can't reach.

## Fix
- New `convertContentToAnthropicBlocks` helper converts `image_url` blocks to Anthropic-native `image` blocks (base64 data URIs → base64 source; public URLs → url source; passthrough for native blocks). Used by the Vertex client's user-message path.
- `describeImage` now downloads + base64-encodes for `claude-*` (Vertex) as well as `anthropic.*` (Bedrock).
- Removed the dead `args.llmModel` in the `describe_image` tool handler and documented that it intentionally uses the configured default model (**Option A**).

## Tests
- `agentModeService.anthropicImageBlocks.test.ts` — converter (base64/url/native/malformed/edge).
- `emma.describeImageTool.test.ts` — tool wiring calls `describeImage` with `undefined` model (uses default, not chat model).
- `agentModeService.describeImageVertex.test.ts` — `describeImage` downloads + base64-encodes for `claude-*`.

Verified end-to-end through the cloud-dev customer portal with Opus 4.8: tool call succeeds, no Vertex 400, accurate image description.

title: fix(landing-pages): auto-add 'use client' for all JSX event handlers (onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave hover bug)
body:
## Problem

Every `generate_landing_page` call produced components with `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` event handlers on Server Components, causing a **100%-reproducible** Next.js prerender failure:

> Event handlers cannot be passed to Client Component props.

This required a manual `coding_agent` fix after **every single** landing page generation.

## Root cause

`autoFixV0Files` in `backend/src/services/v0Service.ts` is the deterministic safety-net that injects `'use client'` into components that need it (runs on every v0 download, all generation paths). But its event-handler detection only checked three hardcoded handlers:

```js
/\bonClick\b/ || /\bonChange\b/ || /\bonSubmit\b/
```

`onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` (and `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onMouseOver`, `onKeyDown`, …) were never detected, so hover-driven components never got `'use client'`. The v0 prompt already asks v0 to avoid this, but v0 ignores it — so the deterministic auto-fix is the correct place to fix it.

## Fix

Replace the three hardcoded checks with one general JSX-event-handler regex:

```js
/\bon[A-Z][a-zA-Z]*\s*=\s*\{/.test(content)
```

- Catches **every** event handler (`onClick`, `onMouseEnter`, `onMouseLeave`, `onFocus`, `onKeyDown`, …).
- The `=\{` guard matches only JSX usage, so it also fixes a **pre-existing false positive**: the old `\bonClick\b` matched TypeScript type annotations like `onClick?: () => void`.

## Tests

7 new tests in `services.v0Service.test.ts` (TDD — confirmed failing before the fix):
- `onMouseEnter` / `onMouseLeave` / `onFocus` / `onKeyDown` / `onMouseOver` / `onBlur` → add `'use client'`
- `onClick` → still works (no regression)
- Pure Server Component (incl. Tailwind `hover:` classes) → untouched
- File already `'use client'` → not double-added
- TS prop type annotation (`onClick?:`) → no longer misfires

## Verification
- New tests: 7/7 pass · full v0Service suite: 81/81 pass
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- Coverage gate (≥95%) verified locally

title: fix(crm): stop syncing unrelated LinkedIn messages onto non-connected leads
body:
## Summary

Investigation + fix for two CRM bugs reported against list `list_1770238037853_wh6sswaay` ("LinkedIn Connections - Rui").

### Bug A — non-connected leads show hundreds of unrelated LinkedIn messages ✅ Fixed

**Symptom:** "first lead not even connected but many messages are synced."

**Confirmed from production data:** the list had **1,021** LinkedIn message events; one non-connected lead (`karthy-chandra`) held **996** of them — the user's entire 2022–2024 sent history to many *different* people (e.g. *"Hey Kevin…"*). All events came from the **live Unipile sync** (`linkedin_msg_*` event ids), which is auto-fired on every lead-detail panel open.

**Root cause:** `POST /sync-linkedin-messages` synced for any lead with a LinkedIn URL, with **no connection check**. For a non-connected attendee, `getMessagesWithContact` → `getAllChatsFromAttendee` resolves to an unrelated chat and `getAllMessagesFromChat` dumps up to ~1000 messages onto that lead. Cross-checking `AW-UnipileConnections` (69 real connections for the account), **every** lead that received messages is `connected=false`.

**Fix:**
- Gate the sync on connection status — resolve the account as `list.linkedInAccountId || resolveAccountId(userId)`, look up `getConnectionByProfileUrlAndAccount`, and skip (`synced:0, connected:false`, stamping `syncAt`) for non-connections. No events written.
- Defense-in-depth in `getMessagesWithContact`: return `[]` when the resolved chat has no `id` (an empty `chat_id` makes Unipile return account-wide messages).
- Tests added to `crm.syncLinkedInMessages.test.ts` (16 pass; 1148 CRM/outreach tests green).
- Cleanup script `backend/src/scripts/cleanup-misattributed-linkedin-messages.ts` (dry-run by default) to purge existing bad events. **Not yet applied to prod** — destructive, awaiting approval. Dry run flags all 1,021 events on this list.

### Bug B — "Lead list not found" on clicking some leads ⏳ Needs repro

Could not deterministically reproduce from static analysis: a normal row click uses the valid `selectedList.listId`, so `getLeadListById` would not 404. The error is a backend 404 surfaced by panel-action toasts; the panel passes `listId={selectedList?.listId ?? ''}`, so an empty/stale selected list (e.g. deep-link race or a list deleted in another tab) is the likely trigger. Holding off on a speculative change — see `dev.md` for the full analysis. **Need the exact view + action that produced the error.**

## Test plan
- `npx tsc` clean
- `npx jest crm linkedInOutreach` → 1148 passed
- Dry-run cleanup script against prod list confirms correct identification of bad events

## Follow-ups
- Confirm Bug B repro so it can be fixed in the same branch (customer-portal change likely).
- Approve running the cleanup script with `--apply` to remove the 1,021 mis-attributed events.

title: feat(onboarding-loop): propose a daily improvement idea instead of only reporting data
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The onboarding loop DM'd funnel **data** every day but never proposed an actual improvement. Root cause: `diagnoseUnderperforming` only flagged a step when a non-control variant was measurably **losing** to control (`lift_pct < 0 AND n >= promote_min_n`). Every step is control-only, so `lift_pct` is always `null` → it always returned `[]` → the loop fell into the heartbeat / `no_mutations` branch **every single day**. The generate→DM→ship machinery was fully built and wired, just never triggered. The heartbeat copy even framed this as intended ("Need a challenger variant per step").

## What this fixes (after)
Added a **Tier 2** fallback to `diagnoseUnderperforming`:
- **Tier 1** (unchanged): a challenger confirmed losing to control with enough traffic.
- **Tier 2** (new): when no confirmed loser exists, bootstrap a first challenger for the **weakest-converting eligible step**. Eligible = has a control to mutate from AND (when an allowlist is set) is in `ONBOARDING_LOOP_ALLOWLIST`. No traffic gate — at pilot scale `n` is tiny and a proposal is cheap because you approve/deny it in Slack. With zero funnel data it still surfaces a configured step so ideas flow on day one.

The existing `generateMutations → validateBusinessRules → critiqueMutations → postDailySlackDM → watchdog ship` pipeline is **reused unchanged** — only the trigger changed (~50 lines in one function + a 1-arg call-site change). Also fixed the misleading heartbeat reason copy; the heartbeat is now the exception (a draft that failed quality review), not the daily rule.

## How to test
This is a backend cron. To verify the behavior:
1. **Unit/integration (fastest):** `cd backend && npx jest onboardingLoop onboardingHeartbeat` → 104 pass. The integration test `proposes a challenger for the weakest allowlisted step even with no losing variant` proves the loop now logs `status=completed, proposedSteps=['brand_voice']` (pre-fix: `no_mutations`).
2. **Live (prod):** the daily 7am-PT DM should now contain a concrete copy proposal for the weakest allowlisted step (`icp_setup`/`brand_voice`) with a ✅/❌ approve prompt — instead of a heartbeat. Reacting ✅ stages + ships it (note: the ✅ dispatch for the *other* (ai-eval) loop is blocked on a separate Slack subscription toggle — see related task; this onboarding loop's own watchdog handles its approvals).

## Edge cases to check
- If the S3 config's step keys don't match the allowlist (`icp_setup`/`brand_voice`), Tier 2 finds nothing eligible and heartbeats — **no regression**, just no improvement until the config/allowlist align. Worth confirming the live config uses those exact step keys.
- Un-approved pending challengers accumulate on a step (capped by `max_active_arms_per_step`); the DM still sends each day even once staging is capped. Pre-existing behavior, not introduced here.

## Test Evidence
- `npx jest onboardingLoop onboardingHeartbeat`: **104 passed, 0 failed**
- `npx tsc`: clean (one unrelated pre-existing error in `phoneValidation.ts` re: `libphonenumber-js`, not touched here)
- Added 9 Tier-2 unit assertions (human-written acceptance criteria) + 1 integration test.

## Behavioral assertions verified
| Assertion | Test |
|---|---|
| Control-only step is proposed (core fix) | `Tier 2 bootstrap › control-only step is proposed` |
| All-positive-lift still proposes weakest step | `…› all-positive-lift still proposes the weakest step` |
| Sub-threshold negative lift still proposed | `…› a negative-lift signal too small for Tier 1` |
| Tier 1 precedence over Tier 2 | `…› Tier 1 takes precedence` |
| Ranks lowest completion rate; maxSteps N worst | `…› picks the lowest-completion-rate step`, `…› maxSteps returns the N worst` |
| Allowlist restricts Tier 2 | `…› allowlist restricts Tier 2` |
| Zero data → day-one idea | `…› zero funnel data still proposes` |
| [] only when nothing eligible | `…› returns [] only when no step is eligible` |
| Loop DMs a proposal (not heartbeat) | `runOnboardingLoop › proposes a challenger…` |

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/onboardingLoopAgents.ts` — Tier 2 fallback in `diagnoseUnderperforming`
- `backend/src/cron/onboardingLoop.ts` — pass `{maxSteps, allowlist}`; fix heartbeat reason copy
- `backend/src/__tests__/onboardingLoop.test.ts` — Tier 2 + integration tests
- `backend/src/__tests__/onboardingHeartbeat.test.ts` — updated reason assertion

## What was NOT tested
- No live prod run of the cron against the real S3 config (can't from here) — the step-key/allowlist alignment caveat above is the one thing to confirm live.
- Whether the LLM's *generated copy quality* is good day-to-day (subjective; you'll see it in the daily DM and approve/deny).

## Related
- Sibling issue: the **ai-eval-funnel** ✅→cloud-dev dispatch is dead because the Emma Slack app lacks the `reaction_added` event subscription (manual Slack-admin toggle). Tracked separately.

title: fix(ai-eval-loop): scope landed metric to /ai-eval so capture-broken stops false-alarming
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The `ai-eval-funnel` loop fired `capture-broken` (352 landings → 2 submits → "capture is broken") **every day** and filed a duplicate cloud-dev task each time. It was a **false alarm caused by a unit mismatch**, confirmed in the code:

- `<LandedTracker/>` is mounted in `app/(frontend)/layout.tsx:56` — the shared layout — so `landed` fires on **every** frontend page (`/`, `/blog`, …), each tagged with `dimensions.landerPath`. `form_submitted`/`eval_started` only fire on `/ai-eval`.
- The rule was `form_submitted_count / landed_count < 0.1` and the DSL's `countByType` (`dsl.ts`) matches on event *type only* — it ignored `landerPath` entirely. So it divided `/ai-eval` submits by **site-wide** landings. Structurally guaranteed to look catastrophic.
- Secondary: the numerator `form_submitted` is a *client* event that under-fires (data showed `eval_started=6 > form_submitted=2` — the server saw 6 submissions, the client beacon only reported 2).

Strip the noise and the real `/ai-eval` funnel was tiny but healthy (~6 engaged, 5/6 completed the eval). **The real bottleneck is top-of-funnel volume, not capture.**

## What this fixes (after)
- **DSL**: added an optional `[dimensionKey=dimensionValue]` filter to count terms — e.g. `landed_count[landerPath=/ai-eval]`. The dimension was always on the event; the DSL just didn't use it. `countByType` now filters by it.
- **capture-broken** → `eval_started_count / landed_count[landerPath=/ai-eval] < 0.1`. Denominator scoped to `/ai-eval`; numerator switched to server-confirmed `eval_started`.
- **top-of-funnel-cold** → `landed_count[landerPath=/ai-eval] < 100`.
- The tracker is untouched — its broad coverage is intentional (it tags `landerPath` precisely so the loop can segment per-lander). The bug was the rule not using the dimension, not the tracker. (This is why I did **not** take the loop's own auto-suggested fix of neutering `<LandedTracker/>`.)

Knock-on: capture-broken stops firing on noise → the daily duplicate-task spam for that rule stops at the source. (A separate PR adds search-before-create dedup as defense-in-depth.)

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest loops.policyDsl` → 37 pass. Key case `capture-broken: scoping the denominator to /ai-eval flips a false alarm to healthy` asserts `eval_started/landed` unscoped (2/30) fires but scoped (2/3) does not.
2. `npx jest loops aiEvalFunnel` → 84 pass (persona fixtures now tag `landed` with `landerPath=/ai-eval`; capture-broken still fires on the smoke scenario at 11/111=0.099, so cron/digest behavior is unchanged).

## Edge cases to check
- Filter value containing `/` (a pathname) parses correctly — covered.
- Events missing the dimension are excluded from a scoped count (not counted as a match) — covered.
- No-filter conditions parse identically to before (no `filter` key) — existing `toEqual` tests still pass.

## Behavioral assertions verified
| Assertion | Test |
|---|---|
| `_count[key=value]` parses (value may contain `/`) | `dimension filters › parses a count with a dimension filter` |
| Ratio with denominator-only filter parses | `…› parses a ratio with a denominator filter only` |
| Scoped count only counts matching events | `…› count filter only counts events whose dimension matches` |
| Scoping flips the false alarm to healthy | `…› capture-broken: scoping the denominator … flips a false alarm` |

## Test Evidence
- `npx tsc`: clean (one unrelated pre-existing `libphonenumber-js` error, untouched)
- `npx jest loops aiEvalFunnel slack.aiEvalReaction`: **84 passed, 0 failed**

## Files changed
- `backend/src/loops/core/policy/dsl.ts` — dimension-filter grammar + `countByType` filtering
- `backend/src/loops/instances/ai-eval-funnel/rules.ts` — scope capture-broken + top-of-funnel-cold
- `backend/src/loops/instances/ai-eval-funnel/personas.ts` — tag fixture `landed` events with landerPath
- `backend/src/__tests__/loops.policyDsl.test.ts` — dimension-filter tests

## What was NOT tested
- No live prod replay against the real `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` data (can't from here). The fix is verified by unit logic; the prod effect is "capture-broken stops firing daily" which you'll see in the absence of new capture-broken tasks/DMs.
- The `eval_started > form_submitted` client-beacon under-firing is mitigated (numerator now uses the server event) but the client `form_submitted` gap itself is left as-is (out of scope).

## Related
- Follow-up PR: search-before-create dedup in `NotionDigestTool` so the loop never files the same rule's task twice while one is open.

title: fix(ai-eval-loop): dedup cloud-dev tasks — search before create
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
The ai-eval-funnel loop fires the same rule on every cron tick, and `NotionDigestTool.apply()` created a Notion task unconditionally — so it filed a **duplicate every day**: `capture-broken` was filed 4× (5/26–5/29), `no-signup` 2×, etc. This violates the search-before-create rule in `notion-tracking.md` and buries the board in noise.

## What this fixes (after)
`apply()` now searches the Sprint Tasks data source for an **open** task matching the rule's stable title prefix `fix(ai-eval-funnel): <ruleId> ` before creating. If an open one exists, it returns a pointer to it (`artifact.deduped = true`) and creates nothing. Done **before** RCA enrichment, so a dedup hit also skips the Bedrock call.

- A previously-**Done** task does NOT block creation — if the issue recurs after being fixed, a fresh task is wanted.
- **Best-effort**: any search error falls through to create (better a rare duplicate than a dropped task).

## How to test
`cd backend && npx jest aiEvalFunnel.notionDigest` → 8 pass. The dedup suite mocks axios to cover all four branches:
- open dup found → skips create (1 axios call, no enrichment), returns `deduped:true`
- none found → creates (search `/query` then create `/pages`), enrichment runs
- only a Done task → creates a fresh one
- search throws → creates anyway

## Edge cases to check
- Title-prefix match uses `fix(ai-eval-funnel): <ruleId> ` (trailing space) so rule ids can't prefix-collide.
- Dedup spans days because it queries Notion live (not in-memory) — survives cron restarts.

## Behavioral assertions verified
| Assertion | Test |
|---|---|
| Open dup → skip creation, point at existing | `…dedup › skips creation when an OPEN task already exists` |
| No dup → create | `…› creates a task when no existing task is found` |
| Only Done dup → create (recurrence) | `…› creates a fresh task when only a Done task exists` |
| Search failure → create anyway | `…› creates anyway when the dedup search fails` |

## Test Evidence
- `npx tsc`: clean (unrelated pre-existing `libphonenumber-js` error only)
- `npx jest aiEvalFunnel.notionDigest`: **8 passed, 0 failed**

## Files changed
- `backend/src/loops/instances/ai-eval-funnel/notionDigestTool.ts` — `findOpenDuplicate` + dedup guard in `apply()`
- `backend/src/__tests__/aiEvalFunnel.notionDigest.dedup.test.ts` — new (axios-mocked)

## What was NOT tested
- No live Notion query against the real data source (mocked). The query endpoint (`POST /v1/data_sources/{id}/query`) mirrors the existing create call's data-source usage; if Notion rejects the filter shape, the try/catch degrades to "create anyway" — so worst case is the pre-existing behavior, never a crash.

## Related
- Pairs with #1708 (scoping the capture metric). #1708 stops capture-broken from firing on noise; this stops any rule from filing duplicates while one is open. Together they end the daily task spam. I'm also closing the already-filed duplicate tasks by hand.

title: docs(loops): design guardrails — avoid local maxima (3 rules)
body:
Captures the three guardrails that keep every loop instance trending toward a global maximum instead of polishing a local one, in the loop framework README so every future loop inherits them.

## The 3 guardrails
1. **Don't lock the loop into micro-edits** — keep `mutationSurface` able to express structural change (flow/steps/first-value moment), not just copy. A copy-only loop is architecturally trapped in one basin.
2. **Keep a human + users as the basin-jumper** — the loop does exploitation (hill-climb the current basin); exploration (a fundamentally different approach) comes from founder insight + user convos, not the loop. At scale, add explicit exploration into the loop (parallel distinct approaches = random restarts; radical variants = annealing temperature).
3. **Climb the right hill** — point `targetMetric` at the true downstream outcome (activation/retention/revenue), not a proxy (clicks, "completed onboarding"). Wrong hill → wrong summit.

Doc-only. No code change.

title: feat(loops): LLM-analyst policy — reason over telemetry instead of threshold rules
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The loop's policy layer (Layer 2) is the DSL RuleSet — hand-written threshold rules. At low volume they never fire, and they can only catch failures you *predicted a rule for*. That's why the onboarding loop just reports "N people tried" and never tells you when something's broken.

## What this adds (after)
`LlmAnalystRuleSet` — a drop-in Layer-2 (`RuleSet`) implementation that hands the event window to an LLM with a description of what the flow should do, and asks it to **reason**: *"what looks broken or where are users struggling, and what would you do about it?"* Each issue becomes a `MutationProposal` → the gate (your Slack DM ✅/❌) → on approval the tools layer ships it. The loop becomes:

`raw events → LLM reasons → suggestion → you approve → it builds → measure`

Everything downstream already exists (gate, cloud-dev dispatch, attribution). **This is the keystone — the one missing piece** that turns the loop from a counter into something that tells you what's wrong and offers to fix it.

## Design choices that matter
- **Summary, not firehose:** feeds the LLM per-type + per-step counts, error samples, and a few representative journeys — sprawl-free, cheap at low volume. At scale, gate it behind a structural pre-filter so it only reasons over flagged slices.
- **Pluggable:** a loop opts in via `rulesetImpl: 'llmAnalyst'` + supplies its `flowDescription` in instance wiring. Same analyst for onboarding, lander, any surface.
- **Safe by construction:** `code_change` proposals are never auto-ship-safe; a bedrock failure or malformed LLM output degrades to **zero** proposals (never crashes the loop). LLM noise is contained by the human gate + outcome attribution.

## How to test
`cd backend && npx jest loops.llmAnalyst` → 9 pass. Covers: no events → no LLM call; reasoned issues → proposals; code_change never auto-ships; healthy verdict → none; malformed/throwing LLM → none (no crash); maxProposals respected; the prompt includes the event summary.

## Behavioral assertions verified
| Assertion | Test |
|---|---|
| No events → no LLM call, no proposals | `makes no LLM call … when there are no events` |
| LLM issues → correctly-shaped proposals | `turns the LLM's reasoned issues into proposals` |
| code_change never auto-ship-safe | `…only for low-risk copy fixes` + code_change assertion |
| Healthy/empty verdict → none | `returns no proposals on a healthy verdict` |
| Malformed / thrown → none, no crash | `malformed LLM output`, `when bedrock throws` |
| maxProposals respected | `respects maxProposals` |
| LLM sees the event summary | `feeds the LLM a summary…` |

## Test Evidence
- `npx tsc`: clean (unrelated pre-existing libphonenumber error only)
- `npx jest loops.llmAnalyst`: 9 passed, 0 failed

## Files changed
- `backend/src/loops/core/policy/llmAnalystRuleSet.ts` — the analyst (new)
- `backend/src/__tests__/loops.llmAnalyst.test.ts` — tests (new)

## What was NOT tested / NOT done (this is the engine, not the live wiring)
This PR is the reusable **component**. It is NOT yet wired into a running loop. To go live it needs: (1) a loop instance to register it (`rulesetImpl: 'llmAnalyst'`) with a real `flowDescription`, (2) that loop's events flowing to it, (3) a prod deploy. The onboarding loop specifically is on a **separate pre-framework codepath**, so it needs a port or a bolt-in first; the lander (ai-eval) loop is framework-native and is the fastest place to activate this. Prompt quality + real-LLM output quality are unverified until it runs against live data.

## Related
- Pairs with the layer-5 attribution engine (separate branch) and the design guardrails (#1711).

title: feat(loops): layer-5 attribution engine — measure whether a shipped fix moved the metric
body:
The reusable engine that closes layer 5: measures the target metric before vs after a shipped fix, assigns a verdict (improved/no_change/regressed/inconclusive), records it, and exposes `lastOutcomeForRule` for a failure-driven policy cooldown. Pure + tested (13 tests); manifest-driven so it works for any loop. This PR is the engine; durable DynamoDB store + cron wiring + policy read-back is the activation follow-up.

See commit messages for detail. `npx jest loops.learning` → all pass.

title: fix(crm): org-aware access on LinkedIn invite/message/connection endpoints

## Summary
Follow-up to the CRM lead-list/message-sync fixes. An org member opening a lead on a **teammate-owned** list saw **"Lead list not found"** when:
- the LinkedIn invite note auto-drafts on panel open (`draft-invite-note`), and
- clicking **Send LinkedIn Invite** (`send-linkedin-invite`).

### Root cause
Five CRM LinkedIn endpoints used a strict owner check `list.userId !== userId` and returned 404, instead of the org-aware `canAccessCrmList` used by the sync endpoints:
- `check-linkedin-connections`
- `sync-linkedin-connections`
- `send-linkedin-message`
- `send-linkedin-invite`
- `draft-invite-note`

Confirmed against prod: the list is owned by `founders@agentweb.pro` (org `dabd0425-…`); the reporting user is a same-org member, so the strict check rejected them.

### Fix
Switch all five to `canAccessCrmList(userId, list)` (owner OR same-org), matching `sync-linkedin-messages` / `sync-linkedin-connection`. Truly cross-org users are still rejected (IDOR test still passes).

## Test plan
- `npx tsc` clean

- `jest crm.sendLinkedInMessage crm.sync.idor crm.routes` → all pass

## Note
The agent-mode CRM tools in `agentModeService.ts` use the same strict pattern in ~10 places (a broader, separate surface whose failures are silent). Not changed here to keep this hotfix focused; flagged as a follow-up.

title: fix(crm): fully backfill LinkedIn connections (existing connections shown as not-connected)
body:
## Summary
Reported: clicking **Send LinkedIn Invite** on a lead you're already connected to fails with "already connected", and the CRM treats most already-connected leads as not connected.

### Root cause
The `AW-UnipileConnections` cache was **incomplete**. The 10-min `linkedInConnectionSyncCron` only pulls 3 pages (~150 connections) and early-stops at the latest known timestamp. An account that already had more than ~150 connections when caching began never had its **older** connections backfilled. So genuinely-connected leads looked "not connected" → the UI offered "Send Invite" (which Unipile then rejects as already-connected) and message sync was skipped for them.

Verified against prod (account `LIBGE2pYS1eckwgo7wUIGQ`): cache had only **70** connections; the account actually has **3,400+**. After a full sync, **all 37 leads** in the reported list are correctly detected as connected (incl. Ji Fang).

### Fix
- `linkedInConnectionSyncCron.syncConnectionsForAccount`: treat an **empty cache** (`getLatestConnectedAt === null`) as a full sync, so a new account paginates through ALL connections on first sync instead of capping at 3 pages. (The per-list "Sync connections" endpoint already does a full sync for on-demand refresh.)
- `scripts/backfill-unipile-connections.ts`: one-off/on-demand full backfill for accounts whose cache predates this fix.

### Prod repair (already run)
Ran the backfill for `LIBGE2pYS1eckwgo7wUIGQ` → cache 70 → 3,439; the affected list's leads now resolve as connected. This is shared data, so the CRM already reflects it without a deploy.

## Test plan
- `npx tsc` clean
- Added `linkedInConnectionSync.initialFullSync.test.ts` (full-syncs empty cache; caps incremental at 3 pages)
- `jest linkedInConnectionSync` → all pass

## Heads-up (related, not in this PR)
Now that these leads resolve as **connected**, the lead-panel auto message-sync will run for them again. The earlier mis-attribution (PR #1706) was mitigated by the empty-`chatId` guard, but if any lead still shows messages that aren't theirs, that points to `getMessagesWithContact` chat resolution and I'll harden it (verify the resolved chat's attendee). Worth a quick check after this ships.

title: Retrieval upgrades: relevance-based memory + KB search fixes
body:
## Summary
Adopts two pieces of the retrieval/memory proposal, both with **no new database and no new API key** (reuses the existing Azure `text-embedding-3-large` deployment):

### 1. Relevance-based memory (proposal Upgrade B)
Emma injected only the **20 most recent** account/org memories every turn, so a relevant older fact was never placed in front of the model. Now memories are ranked by **semantic relevance** to the user's message (with a small recency tie-breaker).
- Accounts at/below the limit keep the exact prior recency behavior (no embedding cost).
- Embeddings computed at write time; legacy memories lazily embedded + backfilled once on read.
- New: `utils/memoryRanking.ts` (pure, 100% covered), `utils/embeddings.ts`.

### 2. Knowledge base search fixes
Found while testing the live KB on `test@example.com` (24 KBs / 94 files):
- **Bug 1 — `max_results` didn't bound results.** It was passed to Vertex as per-document segment count with no `pageSize`; `max_results=10` returned 19 (and up to ~40 across sources). Fixed by adding `pageSize` and slicing the merged results to the requested max.
- **Bug 2 — empty query returned the whole KB** (~59 chunks). Fixed by short-circuiting blank/whitespace queries.

## Verification
- **All 11,333 backend unit tests pass**; `npx tsc` clean.
- New util files: **100%** statements/branches/functions/lines.
- Live before/after (API on `test@example.com`):
  - `max_results` 1/3/10 → **1/3/10** results (was 3/9/19).

title: fix(agent-mode): return Meta Ads insights inline instead of unreadable S3 URL
body:
## Problem

`call_meta_ads_insights_api` always returned its results as an S3 JSON URL (`insights_*.json`) instead of inline data, and **none** of the agent's file-reading tools could open that URL — blocking the founders' daily Meta Ads digest.

Reported failures:
1. `read_file_content` → `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading startsWith)`
2. `perform_data_analysis` → `file URLs not accessible` (HTTP 400)
3. `read_tool_response` → `s3_key is required` (insights returned `s3_url`, not `s3_key`)

Repro: account `1842363582956923` (Haven AI), campaign `120244135557390173`, `object_type=campaign`, `date_preset='yesterday'`, fields incl. `spend`/`actions`/`cost_per_action_type` → `totalRows:1`, unreadable `s3_url`.

## Root cause

The wrapper (`agentModeService.ts:callMetaAdsInsightsApiWrapper`) did its **own** S3 upload of the JSON envelope and returned `{ success, s3_url, totalRows }` with no data. That `s3_url` was unreadable everywhere:

- **`read_tool_response`** requires `s3_key`; it got `s3_url`.
- **`read_file_content`** expects param `file_url`; the LLM passed `s3_url`, so `fileUrl` was `undefined` → `undefined.startsWith` crash.
- **`perform_data_analysis`** downloaded the URL and base64-inlined it to Gemini's code-execution sandbox, which rejected the part → generic HTTP 400.

The "CSVs in the same bucket are readable" clue was a red herring — it's **not** a bucket-permission difference. `get_meta_ads_metrics` returns its data inline as `formattedContent`; its CSVs are only supplementary, so the agent never needs to open them.

Crucially, agent-mode **already** has a generic large-response overflow mechanism: any oversized tool response is auto-offloaded to a readable `tool-responses/<sessionId>` S3 **key** (retrievable via `read_tool_response`/`search_tool_response`), and small responses stay inline. The insights wrapper was bypassing this with its bespoke upload.

## Fix

Return the insights rows **inline** as `{ success, totalRows, metadata, data }` and let the existing pipeline handle sizing:
- Small results (the repro: a single yesterday-only campaign row) → inline, read immediately. This gives the agent yesterday-only metrics **and** the full `actions` array (so `complete_registration`/`lead` counts are available, per the digest spec).
- Large results → auto-offloaded to a readable `s3_key` the agent can page through.

This matches the task's stated EXPECTED outcome and removes the unreadable `s3_url` dead-end.

## Changes
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` — return inline `{ totalRows, metadata, data }`; drop the bespoke `uploadFileToS3` call.
- `backend/src/emma/tools.ts` — update the tool description (inline shape + S3 offload fallback).
- `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.insights.test.ts` — assert inline return and `uploadFileToS3` not called (single-page + paginated).

## Testing
- `npx tsc` ✅ (clean)
- `npx jest agentModeService.insights.test.ts agentModeService.metaCredentialsFallback.test.ts` ✅ 17/17
- Full `agentModeService` suite glob ✅ exit 0
- Backend reloaded cleanly (worker ready, no compile errors)

title: fix(crm): de-duplicate LinkedIn sent messages in activity timeline + counts
body:
## Summary
A LinkedIn message sent from the CRM showed up **twice** in a lead's activity (and counted twice). Confirmed on prod for lead **Kfir Levari** — "Thanks for connecting. would love to learn more about your work." was sent once on LinkedIn but appeared as two events.

### Root cause (data-confirmed)
The same outbound message is written under two different eventId schemes:
1. **Send time** — `send-linkedin-message` writes a synthetic event `linkedin_sent_<ts>_<leadId>` (senderId = accountId) for instant UI feedback.
2. **Sync time** — the periodic message sync re-imports the same message from Unipile keyed on its stable provider_id: `linkedin_msg_<provider_id>`.

Different eventIds → no dedup → the message renders and counts twice.

### Fix
Added `dedupeLinkedInMessageEvents` in `db.ts`: when a synced `linkedin_msg_*` SENT event with the same normalized text exists for the lead, drop the synthetic `linkedin_sent_*` SENT event (prefer the synced one — it has the real provider id). Applied in both:
- `getLeadEngagements` (activity timeline)
- `getLeadEngagementCount` (sent / total counts)

This is a **read-time** fix, so it also corrects already-duplicated rows in prod with **no data migration**, and self-corrects going forward.

## Test plan
- `npx tsc` clean
- `crm.engagementCount.test.ts`: +3 tests (no double-count; timeline drops synthetic dup; keeps un-synced send). 10 pass.
- `jest crm.engagementCount crm.syncLinkedInMessages crm.sendLinkedInMessage linkedInSentInvitationsSync` → 43 pass.

## Note
Matching is on normalized message text (send-time and sync-time timestamps differ, so text is the reliable key). Received messages and distinct sent messages are unaffected.

title: fix(images): return final render (not interim draft) for Gemini 3 image edits
body:
## Problem

Reported by Dyllan Liu (dyllan@rankai.ai), session `b7ab3bb5-54ce-4574-a42c-29f824467520`, priority High.

When revising an existing image via `generate_image` with `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` and an `inputImages` array (e.g. requesting text-overlay changes), the returned image came back **nearly identical to the input**, ignoring the prompt instructions.

## Root cause

`gemini-3-pro-image-preview` and `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` are Gemini 3 **"thinking" image models**. Per [Google's docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation), they stream up to two **interim draft images** before the final rendered image ("the last image within Thinking is also the final rendered image"), and flag drafts with `part.thought`.

`generateWithGoogleGemini3Pro` (in `backend/src/services/imageGeneration.ts`) broke out of the stream loop on the **first** `inlineData` part — so it saved an early draft. On an *edit*, that first draft closely resembles the input image, which is exactly why the requested changes appeared to be ignored.

## Fix

Iterate the **entire** stream, skip parts flagged `part.thought`, and keep the **last** image part (the final render). This also handles multiple image parts arriving within a single chunk.

This affects both Gemini 3 image models, which share this code path. `gemini-2.5-flash-image` is unaffected (separate method, not a thinking model).

## Tests

Added a `Gemini 3 Thinking Image Part Selection` suite (4 cases): last-part-across-chunks, last-part-within-one-chunk, skip `thought`-flagged drafts, and single-part still works. All new tests fail against the old code and pass with the fix.

- `npx tsc` ✅ (clean)
- `imageGeneration.test.ts`, `imageGeneration.likeness-fixes.test.ts`, `agentModeService.generateImage.test.ts` → **73 passed** ✅

title: feat(html-email): generate one-off newsletter emails + fix create_html_file vs create_html_template routing
body:
## Problem

A user asked Emma to *"build this into a branded HTML email"* — expecting a one-off newsletter email rendered in HTML. Instead, `create_html_template` was invoked and it persisted a saved, parameterized **template** (26 variables) into the user's Templates library.

Two root causes:
1. **Tool-selection ambiguity.** Emma has `create_html_file` (one-off standalone HTML document, saves nothing) and `create_html_template` (reusable `{{variable}}` template, **saved** to the Templates library). `create_html_file`'s description never mentioned "email"/"newsletter", while `create_html_template` was the only HTML tool that did — so one-off email requests were routed to the template tool.
2. **No way to make a one-off email from scratch.** `create_html_file` only produced general web-page HTML (embedded/external CSS, scripts, charts) that breaks in email clients. The only working newsletter path was `create_html_from_template`, which **requires a pre-existing saved template**.

Plus a secondary crash: `create_html_template` threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')` when `html_source` was undefined.

Reported by matthew@agentweb.pro (session `4dad9500-ef75-49da-815e-9044cacf9f6e`).

## Changes

**1. New: one-off newsletter emails via `create_html_file`**
- Added an optional `document_type` param (`'document'` default | `'email'`). In `'email'` mode it uses an email-client-safe generation prompt: table-based layout, inline CSS, 600px centered container, web-safe fonts, bulletproof CTA buttons, unsubscribe footer, and **no** `<script>`/`<link>`/charts. It fills in real content (no `{{variable}}` placeholders) — a finished one-off email, not a reusable template.
- Threaded through the tool schema/description, the `executeTool` mock path, the result extractor, and `POST /api/emma/create-html`.

**2. Fix: tool-selection disambiguation**

- `create_html_template` is now reserved for explicit "create/save a reusable template" requests and redirects one-off email drafting to `create_html_file`.

**3. Fix: `html_source` guard** — missing/empty value returns a clean validation error instead of crashing on `.startsWith`.

title: fix(pdf): stop sections/tables overwriting each other in HTML-to-PDF export
body:
## Summary

Fixes a layout bug where exporting a rich HTML report (section cards + tables) to PDF caused **sections to overlap / overwrite each other**.

Reported by yuan@carley.ai (High priority), session `dc1b45fb-1039-4b29-b2a2-3ddf13ca0942`.

## Root cause

Generated report HTML applies `page-break-inside: avoid` to large containers (`.section-block`, cards). When such a container is **taller than a single printable A4 page** (~971px with the 20mm/20mm margins used), Chrome's print engine cannot satisfy "never break inside this block" — it overflows the block past the page boundary and paints the next section on top of it.

Confirmed empirically against the reported session's report: 7 `.section-block` elements measured **1140–2295px tall** vs. a **971px** printable page, all carrying `page-break-inside: avoid`.

## The fix

New utility `backend/src/utils/pdfPrintLayout.ts`, wired into **both** Puppeteer conversion paths right before `page.pdf()`:
- `controllers/filesController.ts` — `exportHtmlToPdf` (`/api/files/export-pdf`)
- `services/agentModeService.ts` — `convertToPdf` (the agent-mode `convert_to_pdf` tool the user actually used)

In the print-media context (never affects on-screen rendering) it:
1. Injects print-safety CSS — large tables/wrappers may break across pages, while rows, images, and headers stay intact and attached to following content.
2. Relaxes `break-inside: avoid → auto` on any element taller than the printable page, so Chrome inserts **clean page breaks** instead of overflowing.

This is a pipeline-level fix, so it protects any generated report, not just this template.

## Verification

Ran the **actual `convertToPdf` tool** end-to-end on the reported session's report:
- **Before:** 22 pages, broken page-breaks (large blank gaps where oversized blocks were shoved; sections overlapping).
- **After:** 19 pages, content flows continuously across pages, no overlap, multi-table checklist breaks cleanly with rows intact.

## Tests & checks

- `npx tsc` clean.
- New `pdfPrintLayout.ts` at **100% coverage** (statements/branches/functions/lines).
- Full backend suite: **11,446 passing**. Global branch coverage **94.72%** (improved from 93.88% on main; the residual <95% is pre-existing in other `utils` files). CI runs coverage with `--coverageThreshold='{}'`, so it reports but does not gate on this.

## Summary

The coding agent (the sub-agent Emma delegates to for landing-page edits) could call `take_screenshot`, but **the model never saw the captured image** — so it was editing visually blind. This makes the screenshot actually useful.

### The bug
- `take_screenshot` returned only the string `"Screenshot taken successfully."`, discarding the base64 image the Playwright MCP returns in `result.raw.content` (`codingAgentService.ts`).
- The agent loop pushed every tool result as truncated **text**, with no path to attach an image block.

### The fix — `backend/src/services/codingAgentService.ts`
- New `ToolImageResult` type + `isToolImageResult` guard.
- `executeTool` return type widened to `string | ToolImageResult`.
- `take_screenshot` extracts the image from `result.raw.content` and returns it structured; falls back to text when no image is returned; the no-browser error path is unchanged.
- The agent loop renders a `ToolImageResult` as an Anthropic image content block (`{type:'image', source:{type:'base64', media_type, data}}`) with an "Analyze the image below" prefix — mirroring the proven main agent-mode loop (`agentModeService.ts:2705`).
- Tool description updated to tell the model to actually look at the image.

## Testing
- **3 new unit tests** in `codingAgentService.test.ts`: image fed back as a vision block; text-error fallback when browser tools are unavailable; text fallback when MCP returns no image data.

The agent reported pixel-level visual detail (gradient hex colors `#e6518d → #3f3fa6`, white text contrast, button fill/shape) that exists only in the rendered image, not in the accessibility tree — confirming the model now genuinely sees the screenshot.
