title: fix(agentmode): MCP session terminal-400 self-heals via 404 — ENG-97
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

Single-bug PR for ENG-97. One concern, one commit. Behavior-preserving for healthy sessions; only the failure-recovery path changes.

## What was wrong (before) — per bug

### ENG-97 — MCP server returns terminal `-32000` and strands the session
The MCP server's `POST /mcp` handler (`backend/src/mcp/server/mcpServer.ts`) had four branches: (1) known `mcp-session-id` → reuse transport; (2) no id + initialize → create session; (3) id present but unknown → `404 / -32001 "Session not found"` (already correct, set in commit `9799b23b`); and (4) the final `else` — no session id AND not an initialize request → `400 / -32000 "Bad Request: No valid session ID provided"`.

Sessions live only in an in-memory per-process `Map`, evicted by `cleanupStaleSessions` (1h timeout) or wiped on restart/redeploy, with no shared store and no sticky routing across instances/worker. When a client's session is gone and its transport has dropped/never re-set the `mcp-session-id` header, the next non-initialize call lands in that final `else` and gets the **terminal** `400`. The MCP TypeScript SDK's `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` treats `400` as terminal (no recovery) but treats `404` as "session expired → re-run initialize". So `emma_create_session` and every subsequent tool call permanently failed with `-32000` until a manual reconnect.

## Investigation — is the 404 fix the real fix, or a symptom patch? (resolves the central OPEN QUESTION)

The reviewer's concern was whether org accounts fail at **(1)** the bare non-init branch (which 404 self-heals) or **(2)** the `initialize` handshake itself (in which case a 404→reinit would just loop a failing init). Traced read-only through `validateMcpAccessToken`, `agentApiKeyService.validateKey`, `mcpServerCore.createMcpServer`, and the session-store / transport lifecycle:

- **The reported error is the smoking gun.** ENG-97's actual payload is byte-for-byte `{"code":-32000,"message":"Bad Request: No valid session ID provided"}`. That exact string is produced by **one and only one** place in the codebase — the old branch-(4) bare-non-init `else`. It is case **(1)**.
- **It is not the auth/account layer.** `validateMcpAccessToken` → `agentApiKeyService.validateKey` resolves an `aw_*` key to a `userId` purely by `keyHash` (status/expiry checks only); there is **zero** org-specific branching, and an auth failure returns `401`, never `-32000`. The org-aware skill-discovery in `apiTools.ts` runs *inside* tool execution, long after the session handshake — it can't produce this error.
- **It is not a failing `initialize`.** The initialize branch (`!sessionId && isInitializeRequest`) and `createMcpServer` have no account-state checks that could throw for an org account; `effectiveUserId` resolution is account-agnostic. So once a 404 prompts the SDK to re-run `initialize`, that handshake **succeeds** and registers a fresh session — recovery closes, it does not loop.

**Conclusion: the 404 conversion IS the correct fix, applied at the correct layer (MCP session handshake, not auth/account state).** Org accounts are not gated in code; they just hit the bare-non-init path more often (long-lived shared `aw_*` keys + higher concurrency → sessions evicted/restarted more frequently, and the in-memory Map is not shared across instances/worker). Status: **done**.

> Residual (already flagged out-of-scope, unchanged): under a genuine multi-instance/worker deploy with no shared session store and no sticky routing, a fresh initialize can land on instance A while the retried call lands on instance B → another 404 → another reinit. Each reinit still *succeeds* (it is not a failing-init loop), and stateless request/response tools complete on any single same-instance round trip, so 404 is strictly better than the old terminal 400. The durable fix (stateless transport `sessionIdGenerator: undefined`, or a shared session store) is a larger, riskier change tracked separately.

## What this fixes (after) — per bug

### ENG-97
Changed the final `else` branch (`mcpServer.ts`, the bare-non-init path) from `400 / -32000 "Bad Request: No valid session ID provided"` to `404 / -32001 "Session not found. Please reinitialize."` — byte-for-byte the same JSON-RPC envelope the unknown-session branch already returns. The SDK now treats this as a recoverable "session expired" signal, transparently re-runs the initialize handshake, and retries the call with a fresh, valid session. `emma_create_session` and all subsequent tool calls self-heal for **any** account (org or personal) whose session was evicted/lost. The healthy initialize and known-session paths are unchanged.

## How to test — concrete steps/assertions per bug

### ENG-97
```
cd backend && npx tsc            # clean (exit 0)
npx jest src/__tests__/mcp.mcpServer.test.ts --runInBand   # 24/24 green
```
- Status-code assertion: `POST /mcp` with a non-initialize body and **no** `mcp-session-id` header → `status 404`, `error.code -32001`, message contains `Session not found`.
- **New end-to-end recovery test** (`recovers a stranded session end-to-end …`): drives the full client-recovery sequence against the server with the SDK transport mocked — (1) bare `emma_create_session` (no session header) → `404 / -32001`; (2) the SDK re-runs `initialize` → a fresh session is created (`StreamableHTTPServerTransport` constructed, `onsessioninitialized` registers the id); (3) the retried tool call **with** the new `mcp-session-id` header reuses the transport and returns `200`. This proves the previously-terminal failure now closes the loop instead of stranding the session.
- Existing initialize and unknown-session tests still green.
- Manual: against a running server, send a `tools/list` POST with no session header → observe `404` (was `400`). An SDK client whose session expired now auto-reinitializes instead of erroring out.

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines:** `mcpServer.ts`: +~14 (status/code change + rationale comment + one debug log line). Test file: +~50 (the new end-to-end recovery test + comments; the prior lock-in test's assertions swapped 1:1). No new source files.
- **Moving parts:** none added — no new table, flag, branch, dependency, or abstraction. The `else` branch now returns the *same* response shape as the sibling unknown-session branch, consolidating two failure paths onto one recovery contract (one fewer distinct error contract).
- **Behavior:** behavior-preserving except the intended reliability delta (a previously-terminal failure becomes self-healing). No chat output / tool-selection / prompt / model change.

## Behavior-preserving proof
- Only the bare-non-init failure branch changed; the initialize branch, the known-session reuse branch, and the unknown-session branch are untouched. Verified by the full `mcp.mcpServer.test.ts` suite (24/24 green) covering all those paths plus the new end-to-end recovery walk.
- No change to any tool handler, tool schema, prompt, model default, or `agentModeService` — Emma chat's observable outputs and tool-selection are unchanged. The only user-visible effect is a previously-stuck session now recovers automatically (fewer errors), which is the allowed reliability-only delta.
- `mcpClientService.ts` (the client) was deliberately not touched.
- **Prior art:** mirrors the MCP spec + SDK status-code semantics (404 = recoverable session-expired; 400 = terminal) — the same recovery contract this repo already established in commit `9799b23b` for the unknown-session path.

## Behavioral assertions verified
ENG-97 acceptance criteria → verifying test/code path:
- *"emma_create_session for an org account returns a valid session ID; subsequent tool calls succeed"* → proven as far as is mockable by the new end-to-end test `recovers a stranded session end-to-end …`: the bare call that used to strand the session now returns the recoverable `404 / -32001`, the SDK's reinitialize creates a session, and the retried tool call succeeds (`200`) on that session. (The client-side 404→reinit hop is the SDK's documented behavior, relied upon, not re-implemented; no live multi-instance run — see "What was NOT tested".)
- *"determine whether org-account-specific or all accounts"* → confirmed **all accounts**, not org-gated. The error string is uniquely the bare-non-init branch; `validateMcpAccessToken` / `agentApiKeyService.validateKey` / `apiTools.ts` skill discovery are account-agnostic (auth failures return `401`, not `-32000`). See "Investigation" above.
- *"fix at the correct layer (MCP protocol session handshake vs Emma backend auth/account state)"* → fixed at the **MCP-protocol-session layer** (`mcpServer.ts` POST handler), confirmed by tracing that `initialize` and `createMcpServer` have no org-specific failure path, so reinit recovers rather than loops.

## What was NOT tested
- No live end-to-end run against a deployed multi-instance server with real SDK clients (the unit test mocks the SDK transport, per the planned mockable scope). The SDK's actual 404→reinitialize behavior is relied upon from spec/SDK semantics and the precedent unknown-session branch.
- The out-of-scope durable fix (stateless transport / shared session store) is not implemented or tested; the residual multi-instance reinit-churn described above is not exercised.
- Full backend suite not run (per instructions — only the targeted test file).

## Files changed
- `backend/src/mcp/server/mcpServer.ts` — final `else` branch: `400/-32000` → `404/-32001`, with rationale comment + debug log.
- `backend/src/__tests__/mcp.mcpServer.test.ts` — corrected the lock-in test (`400` → `404/-32001`) and added the end-to-end stranded-session recovery test.

## Linear issues
- ENG-97: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-97

title: fix(agentmode): structured MCP tool telemetry — ENG-107
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before) — per bug

### ENG-107 — MCP tool telemetry is unstructured text
MCP tool calls run inside two nearly-identical `execute` closures in `mcpClientService.ts` (the main connect/discovery path and the per-user secret-placeholder discovery path). Both emitted ONLY unstructured `console.log/warn/error` strings:
- `[MCP-DEBUG] Calling tool <name> on server <srv>, MCP session: ..., chat sessionId: ...`
- `[MCP-RETRY] Browser tool "<name>" failed on attempt N/M, retrying ...`
- `[MCP Tool Execution Error (<name>): <error>`

None of the reliability dimensions were captured as structured/queryable fields: server name, MCP session id, transport type, retry count, or a **normalized error class**. The repo already has `classifyToolErrorClass` (the runtime-spine error taxonomy) but it was never imported into `mcpClientService` (grep count 0), so every MCP failure was invisible to the failure-clustering policy. Browser retry vs final failure was distinguishable only by log level/prefix text, and raw error messages (which can contain bearer tokens / api keys) were logged unredacted.

## What this fixes (after) — per bug

### ENG-107
New pure helper `backend/src/mcp/client/mcpToolTelemetry.ts`:
- `buildMcpToolTelemetry(input)` → normalized JSON-serializable payload: `event:'mcp_tool_call'`, `serverName`, `toolName`, `transport`, `chatSessionId` (truncated 8 chars), `mcpSessionId` (truncated 8 chars, else `NO_SESSION_ID`), `retryCount` (= attempt-1), `maxAttempts`, `phase` (`call`|`retry`|`final_failure`), and on failures `errorClass` (from the existing `classifyToolErrorClass`) + `errorMessage` (redacted).
- `redactSensitive(msg)` masks bearer tokens, `access_token`/`refresh_token`/`api_key`/`password`/`secret`/`authorization` values, and long opaque hex/base64/JWT blobs.

Both `execute` closures now emit `console.log/warn/error(JSON.stringify(buildMcpToolTelemetry(...)))` at the three log sites. `phase:'retry'` on `attempt < maxAttempts`, `phase:'final_failure'` on the last attempt — making retry vs terminal failure a structured discriminator. The dedupe (two copies of ad-hoc logging → one tested unit) is subtraction-biased.

Prior art: Claude Code's `src/tools` boundary — one coarse, stable error taxonomy + structured telemetry at the tool dispatch edge rather than ad-hoc strings. We reuse the existing `classifyToolErrorClass` taxonomy rather than inventing a parallel one.

## How to test — concrete steps/assertions per bug

### ENG-107
```
cd backend
npx jest src/__tests__/mcpToolTelemetry.test.ts --runInBand        # 12 pass
npx jest src/__tests__/mcpClientService.browserRetry.test.ts --runInBand  # 6 pass (behavior preserved)
npx tsc --noEmit                                                    # clean
```
Assertions:
- call payload includes serverName, transport, truncated chat/MCP session ids, `retryCount=0`, `phase='call'`.
- timeout error → `errorClass='timeout'`, `phase='retry'` when attempt < maxAttempts.
- auth (`unauthorized`) → `errorClass='auth'`, `phase='final_failure'` on last attempt.
- rate-limit (`429`) → `rate_limit`; network (`ECONNRESET`) → `network`.
- `retryCount` increments across attempts; `final_failure` distinguishable from `retry`.
- a message with `Bearer eyJ...`, `access_token=...`, `api_key=...` is masked; session ids truncated; payload round-trips through `JSON.stringify`/`parse`.

## Complexity ledger
- Net lines: +374 (new pure module ~133 + focused test ~179; service wiring net ~+62). The new lines are a tested pure unit + its tests; the ad-hoc 3-line log statements in two closures were consolidated to call one shared helper (dedupe of the two near-identical logging copies).
- Moving parts: +1 small pure module (`mcpToolTelemetry.ts`), 0 new tables/flags/deps. Reuses the existing `classifyToolErrorClass` taxonomy instead of adding a new one.
- Behavior: behavior-preserving — only the log payload shape changes; retry/throw control flow and tool outputs are unchanged.

## Behavior-preserving proof
- The retry loop, `result.isError` handling, client eviction, `sleep`, and `throw lastError` paths were not touched — only the three `console.*` argument expressions changed (string → `JSON.stringify(buildMcpToolTelemetry(...))`).
- `classifyToolErrorClass` and `redactSensitive` operate on the error/strings AFTER control-flow decisions; classification reads the raw error, redaction only affects the logged message.
- Characterization: the existing `mcpClientService.browserRetry.test.ts` (asserts retry counts, success-on-Nth-attempt, fail-fast for non-browser tools, throw on exhaustion) passes unchanged (6/6) — proving tool-call sequence + throw behavior are identical. Observed in the run: structured JSON lines now appear where the old text lines were, with no change in `callTool` call counts.
- No change to chat outputs, prompts, model defaults, or tool selection.

## Behavioral assertions verified
ENG-107 acceptance criteria → verification:
- "telemetry includes server name/id, session id where safe, transport type, retry count, normalized error class" → `buildMcpToolTelemetry` success/call test + failure tests (`mcpToolTelemetry.test.ts`: "success/call payload includes...", "timeout error →...", "auth error →...").
- "browser retry attempts and final failure are distinguishable" → test "retryCount increments across attempts and final_failure is distinguishable from retry" (`phase` field + `retryCount`).
- "sensitive values redacted" → tests "redacts secrets in the emitted error message" + `redactSensitive` describe block (bearer/access_token/api_key/password masked); session ids truncated asserted in the call-payload test.
- "tests cover normalized telemetry payloads for representative MCP failure modes" → timeout / auth / rate_limit / network cases + JSON-serializable round-trip test.
- Behavior preservation (charter hard invariant) → existing `mcpClientService.browserRetry.test.ts` green.

## What was NOT tested
- No live MCP server / SDK round-trip — the wiring into the two closures is exercised indirectly via the existing browser-retry suite (mocked SDK), not a new end-to-end test against a real transport.
- Full backend suite not run (per swarm rules: only the focused new + behavior-preservation tests). `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean across the backend.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/mcp/client/mcpToolTelemetry.ts` (new — pure helper)
- `backend/src/mcp/client/mcpClientService.ts` (import + 6 log sites across 2 closures)
- `backend/src/__tests__/mcpToolTelemetry.test.ts` (new — 12 focused unit tests)

## Linear issues
- ENG-107: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-107

title: fix(agentmode): gateway breaker counts structured failures + Emma tool schema/impl alignment — ENG-101, ENG-106
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

Two reliability fixes at the Emma agent-tool gateway boundary. Both are internal/correctness-only — Emma chat outputs, tool-selection, prompts, and model defaults are unchanged.

## What was wrong (before) — per bug

**ENG-101 (High/High) — structured tool failures never tripped the circuit breaker.**
`executeAgentToolThroughGateway` treated ANY resolved `input.execute()` as a success: it unconditionally cleared the run's failure counts and returned `status:'success'`. `recordToolFailure` was only reached in the `catch` path, i.e. only for *thrown* errors. Tools that signal failure by *resolving* with a structured payload (`{success:false}` / `{isError:true}`) — `performDataAnalysis`, `getMetaAdsMetrics`, `fathom_get_meetings`, `coding_agent` — were (a) never counted toward the repeated-failure / media-budget breaker and, worse, (b) actively *cleared* any prior thrown-error counts for that tool. A tool returning `success:false` could retry-spiral indefinitely; the breaker never tripped.

**ENG-106 (Medium/Medium) — two schema/impl contract mismatches.**
- `send_email_from_sender` required only `to`+`subject`; nothing enforced a non-empty body, even though the impl soft-fails at execution when `html`/`text`/`body` are all empty. A body-less call passed validation and wasted a round-trip.
- `get_meta_ads_metrics` declared `campaign_ids` as a required `array` (minItems 1), but `execute()` deliberately normalizes legacy scalar `campaign_id` and string `campaign_ids` for back-compat. The gateway's `validateAndRepairToolArgs` rejected both legacy shapes first (missing_required / type_mismatch), so the impl's normalization was dead and schema/impl disagreed.

## What this fixes (after) — per bug

**ENG-101.** In the gateway's try-block, after `await input.execute()`, the result is run through `toolResultError` (the repo's canonical structured-failure detector — the SAME function the dispatcher uses to downgrade encoded errors at `toolDispatch.ts:495-509`, so accounting and classification stay in lockstep). A structured failure is now accounted exactly like the catch path (`recordToolFailure` for `runId`, and the media-budget-gated `recordToolFailure` for `budgetScopeId`), and prior counts are NOT cleared. The genuine-success path (clear + success return) is untouched; the thrown-error catch path is untouched. The gateway still returns `status:'success'` with the result for structured failures so the dispatcher's downgrade carries the structured payload to the model — flipping to `status:'error'` would strip `result`. The only observable change is internal accounting: counts increment instead of being cleared, so repeated identical structured failures collide on the same `errorHead` key and trip `findTrippedFailure` / `findTrippedBudget` on the next call — the identical protection thrown errors get.

**ENG-106.**
- `get_meta_ads_metrics` schema (`emma/tools.ts`): `campaign_ids` broadened to `type:['array','string']` (union types already supported by the hand-rolled type validator; `minItems` only fires for arrays), added an optional legacy `campaign_id` string property, and dropped the hard `required:['campaign_ids']`. The static schema now accepts exactly the shapes `execute()` normalizes.
- `validateSemanticToolContract` (`agentToolGatewayService.ts`) gains two branches alongside the existing `linkedin_outreach` rule (the established seam — no new abstraction): (i) `send_email_from_sender` → `invalid_args` with "Provide a non-empty email body via html, text, or body." when none of html/text/body is a non-empty string; (ii) `get_meta_ads_metrics` → `invalid_args` with an actionable campaign-id message unless at least one usable id is present (non-empty array `campaign_ids`, non-empty string `campaign_ids`, or non-empty `campaign_id`). This restores the "at least one campaign id" guarantee that dropping `required` would otherwise lose, while accepting every impl-normalized shape.

**Prior art:** uniform tool-failure normalization regardless of throw-vs-return, and schema/semantic validation at the tool boundary, mirror the Claude Code / OpenAI agent-loop tool layer (one error channel + boundary-validated typed tool registry). MCP-spec alignment (e.g. unknown-session→404) was reviewed and is unaffected here.

## How to test — concrete steps/assertions per bug

Run: `cd backend && npx tsc && npx jest src/__tests__/agentToolGatewayService.test.ts --runInBand`

**ENG-101** (in the `repeated-failure circuit breaker` describe):
- `trips the breaker when a tool repeatedly RESOLVES with success:false` — 3× resolved `{success:false}` each return `status:'success'`; the 4th (a `jest.fn`) returns `status:'error'` / `AgentToolRepeatedFailureError` and `execute` is NOT called.
- `does NOT clear prior thrown-error counts when a structured failure resolves` — 2 thrown + 1 resolved (same message) → next call trips.
- `trips the breaker on repeated isError:true structured failures` — mirrors case 1 for the `isError:true` shape.
- `still clears the count on a genuine success after structured failures` — no-regression guard on the clear path.
- Existing thrown-error tests (`blocks the next call after three identical failures`, `resets the failure count when the tool succeeds`) still pass → parity.

**ENG-106** (in the `semantic tool contract (ENG-106)` describe):
- send_email: `{to,subject}` only → `invalid` at `$.body`; whitespace-only `html` → `invalid`; `html`/`text`/`body` non-empty → `valid`/`repaired`.
- meta: `{campaign_ids:['123']}`, `{campaign_ids:'123'}`, `{campaign_id:'123'}` → `valid`; `{timeframe:'7d'}` (no ids) → `invalid` with campaign-id message; `{campaign_ids:[]}` → `invalid`.

Fail-before/pass-after was verified by stashing each source change and re-running: 3 ENG-101 tests and 3 ENG-106 rejection tests fail on current code and pass after.

## Complexity ledger

- **Net lines:** source `+~55` (gateway structured-failure branch `+~25`; two semantic branches `+~30`); schema edit is roughly flat (broadened one property, added one optional property, removed one `required` line). Tests `+~200`.
- **Moving parts:** no new tables, flags, dependencies, or abstractions. ENG-101 reuses the existing `recordToolFailure`/`mediaFailureBudget` accounting and the existing `toolResultError` detector (single source of truth — removes the divergence where the gateway and dispatcher disagreed on what counts as a failure). ENG-106 reuses the existing `validateSemanticToolContract` seam.
- **Behavior:** behavior-preserving for chat; the only deltas are internal failure accounting (ENG-101) and earlier, clearer validation rejection of inputs that previously soft-failed or were wrongly rejected (ENG-106).

## Behavior-preserving proof

- **ENG-101:** structured-failure results still return `status:'success'` carrying `result`, exactly as before, so the dispatcher's `status==='success'` downgrade at `toolDispatch.ts:495-509` runs identically and the model sees the same payload. The genuine-success and thrown-error paths are byte-for-byte unchanged. The sole difference is that internal `runFailureCounts` now increments (and stops clearing) for structured failures — invisible to chat output until the breaker legitimately trips, which is the intended protection.
- **ENG-106:** valid array/body calls validate exactly as before. Legacy meta scalar/string calls that the impl already normalized now reach the impl instead of being rejected (matches impl intent). Body-less emails now fail at validation with an actionable `modelMessage` instead of an opaque execution soft-fail — same end (no email sent), faster and clearer. No prompt, tool-selection, or model-default change.

## Behavioral assertions verified

**ENG-101**
- "Structured failure results are counted as failures by gateway failure accounting" → `trips the breaker when a tool repeatedly RESOLVES with success:false` + `trips the breaker on repeated isError:true structured failures`.
- "Prior failure counts NOT cleared for such results" → `does NOT clear prior thrown-error counts when a structured failure resolves`.
- "Thrown-error behavior unchanged" → existing `blocks the next call after three identical failures` / `resets the failure count when the tool succeeds` still green.
- "Unit tests prove both thrown AND structured failures trip the same protection path" → thrown tests + new structured tests both assert `AgentToolRepeatedFailureError`.

**ENG-106**
- "Schemas enforce required semantic fields (email body)" → `rejects {to, subject} with no body` + `rejects a whitespace-only body`.
- "Schema and impl agree on accepted Meta campaign-id shapes" → `accepts a non-empty array campaign_ids` / `accepts a legacy string campaign_ids` / `accepts a legacy scalar campaign_id`.
- "Invalid semantic inputs fail at validation with clear messages" → `rejects a call with no campaign id at all` (asserts `modelMessage` contains "campaign id") + send_email body message assertion.
- "Tests cover send_email_from_sender and get_meta_ads_metrics legacy/current argument shapes" → the two ENG-106 describe blocks.

## What was NOT tested

- The `emma/tools.ts` `get_meta_ads_metrics` schema change is verified via an inlined post-fix copy in the gateway unit tests (to avoid booting the `agentModeService` monolith); the live registry schema itself is covered only by `npx tsc`, not a dedicated runtime test.
- No end-to-end Emma chat run was executed (no test env in this PR); the dispatcher-downgrade parity is argued from `toolDispatch.ts:495-509` reading, not a live trace.
- The `execute()` normalization of `getMetaAdsMetrics` (already present) was not re-tested; only the gateway-side acceptance of its input shapes.

## Files changed

- `backend/src/services/agentToolGatewayService.ts` — ENG-101 structured-failure accounting in the gateway try-block; ENG-106 semantic-contract branches.
- `backend/src/emma/tools.ts` — ENG-106 `get_meta_ads_metrics` schema (union `campaign_ids`, optional `campaign_id`, dropped hard `required`).
- `backend/src/__tests__/agentToolGatewayService.test.ts` — ENG-101 + ENG-106 unit tests.

## Linear issues
- ENG-101: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-101
- ENG-106: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-106

title: fix(agentmode): telemetry serialization + deferred/partial/invalid-output + same-turn dedupe — ENG-102, ENG-103, ENG-104, ENG-105, ENG-108
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

Five related AgentMode (Emma) backend reliability/telemetry/correctness fixes. Prompts, model defaults, tool selection, and streaming are unchanged. The chat surface is behavior-preserving **except in two defined edge cases** that this PR deliberately corrects: ENG-105 turns an empty/undefined tool "success" into a structured tool failure (so the model stops getting garbage fed back as a result), and ENG-108 makes two identical same-turn tool calls execute once instead of twice. Everything else is reliability/telemetry/correctness with no user-visible delta. The runtime-spine telemetry path stays gated behind `AGENT_RUNTIME_SPINE_ENABLED` (off in prod).

## What was wrong (before) — per bug

- **ENG-102 (telemetry races + loss):** Per-tool telemetry was wrapped in a detached `void (async)()`; the terminal `run_completed`/`run_failed` records were independent detached promises. So `run_completed` could persist before `tool_failed` for the same run, and unflushed writes were lost when the worker exited. Dynamo write failures were console-only.
- **ENG-103 (deferred recorded as nothing):** Media-gen calls deferred by the per-run time budget were filtered out of telemetry entirely — recorded as neither success, failure, nor skipped.
- **ENG-104 (silent partial Meta failures):** `getMetaAdsMetrics` fetched 3 breakdown endpoints (demographics/placement/device) concurrently; a breakdown error was `console.error`'d and skipped, so a failed section was indistinguishable from an empty one and the tool always returned `success:true` with no indication of which sections came back.
- **ENG-105 (no output contract):** `extractToolContent` had a loose `JSON.stringify` fallback with no schema check, so a tool returning `undefined`/`{}`/`{content:[]}` without throwing was treated as a success, fed to the model as garbage (`JSON.stringify(undefined)` → `'undefined'`), and counted as success.
- **ENG-108 (no same-turn dedupe):** Loop detection was cross-iteration only; identical (name+args) tool calls emitted in ONE turn both executed and could double-bill.

## What this fixes (after) — per bug

- **ENG-102:** `AgentRunRecorder` routes every emit through a monotonic write chain (call-order == write-order), adds `flush()` to drain before teardown, and surfaces write failures as a structured logger signal + `writeFailures` counter. `agentModeService` enqueues per-tool records synchronously (drops the detached IIFE) and drains (bounded by a 5s race, mirroring the existing suggested-replies guard) before the worker returns/throws. Net: tool records always serialize before the terminal record, and the terminal flush implies all tool records are durably written before exit.
- **ENG-103:** New `EVT_TOOL_DEFERRED` + `recorder.toolDeferred` (tool name, reason/category, run id, budget/defer context). Deferred is no longer filtered out of telemetry, but routes to `toolDeferred` — NOT `toolInvoked` (denominator stays clean) or `toolFailed`. Inspector adds `deferredToolCalls`, counted separately from `toolCalls`/`failedToolCalls`.
- **ENG-104:** New pure `summarizeBreakdownSections` → per-section `ok|unavailable` + `unavailableSections` + `partialFailure` + captured errors; attached to the tool result and noted in `message`; 3 scattered `console.error`s replaced with one structured `console.warn`. Fatal core-endpoint throws untouched (fatal ⇒ `success:false`; partial ⇒ `success:true` + `partialFailure:true`). **Follow-up:** the partial result now also emits a STRUCTURED loop-event (`agent_tool_partial_failure` via `recorder.toolPartialFailure`) through the same agent-mode telemetry path ENG-102/103 use — its own class, NOT `toolFailed` (the call succeeded) and NOT `toolDeferred` (it executed) — so a section silently going dark is queryable in `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` instead of living only in a `console.warn`. Emitted only when `partialFailure:true`; the all-success path stays byte-identical and `getMetaAdsMetrics` itself is untouched.
- **ENG-105:** New pure `validateToolOutputContract` + `ToolOutputContractError`. The existing success→error downgrade pass also runs the output-contract check via a new optional `validateToolOutput` port, so invalid/empty output becomes a structured tool failure (`errorClass: invalid_output`, distinct from execution failures) routed through `formatToolError` + the failed counter. **Follow-up (review gaps closed):** (a) **false-positive fix** — the empty-content check no longer downgrades a legitimate non-text result: a content array with an image/audio/file/resource part (e.g. `content:[{type:'image',...}]`) is now treated as usable payload; only a genuinely empty array, or one whose every part is blank text, counts as empty. (b) **real-port wiring test** — `extractToolContent` is extracted to a pure monolith-free util (`utils/extractToolContent`, re-exported from `agentModeService`) so the isolated `core/toolDispatch` suite wires the ACTUAL production composition `validateToolOutputContract(result, extractToolContent)` through `executePreparedTools` (no hand-copied mirror) and proves the empty→failure + `invalid_output` path end-to-end.
- **ENG-108:** Phase-1 same-turn dedupe on a stable (name + key-sorted args) signature; a duplicate is skipped from execution but still answered with its own `tool_call_id` (tool-role message + ledger entry referencing the handled call). `NON_DEDUPABLE_TOOLS` (e.g. `wait_seconds`) are exempt. Suppression is neither success nor failure — recorded via a new `recordDuplicateSuppression` port, NOT through `recordToolTelemetry`.

## How to test

Run the focused suites (all green):

```
cd backend
npx tsc
npx jest src/__tests__/loops.agentRunRecorder.test.ts \
  src/__tests__/agentRunInspectorService.test.ts \
  src/services/agentMode/core/__tests__/toolDispatch.test.ts \
  src/__tests__/agentMode.metaBreakdownStatus.test.ts \
  src/__tests__/toolOutputContract.test.ts \
  src/__tests__/toolErrorClassifier.test.ts \
  src/__tests__/agentModeService.metaMetrics.test.ts \
  src/__tests__/agentMode/characterization/ --runInBand
```

- **ENG-102:** recorder ordering test fires `toolFailed` then `runCompleted` fire-and-forget with delayed tool puts → asserts `agent_tool_failed` is written before `agent_run_completed`; flush test asserts all 7 puts land; write-failure test asserts a rejecting `putItem` → structured `agent_recorder_write_failed` log + `writeFailures===1`, no throw.
- **ENG-103:** `toolDeferred` emits `EVT_TOOL_DEFERRED` with reason+context; toolDispatch forwards the deferred result to telemetry; inspector reports `deferredToolCalls===2`, `failedToolCalls===0`, no `failed_tool_calls` flag.
- **ENG-104:** pure helper covers all-ok / empty-ok / one-fail / two-fail / null; integration test mocks a demographics breakdown error → `success:true`, `partialFailure:true`, `sections.demographics==='unavailable'`; all-success path is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **ENG-105:** pure validator flags undefined/null/`{}`/empty-content/`'undefined'`, passes string/`formattedContent`/`content[0].text`/data-object; classifier maps `ToolOutputContractError` → `invalid_output`.
- **ENG-108:** identical calls execute once + answer both ids; arg-order insensitive; distinct args both run; `wait_seconds` exempt; suppression recorded separately and absent from `recordToolTelemetry`.

## Complexity ledger

- Net lines: positive, but the additions are mostly two small pure modules (`metaBreakdownStatus`, `toolOutputContract`) + focused tests; production logic deltas are small and additive.
- Moving parts added: 2 event types (`agent_tool_deferred`, `agent_tool_partial_failure`), 3 pure util modules (`metaBreakdownStatus`, `toolOutputContract`, `extractToolContent`), 2 optional dispatch ports (`validateToolOutput`, `recordDuplicateSuppression`), 1 errorClass (`invalid_output`). Each earns its place by closing a named correctness/observability gap.
- Moving parts removed/consolidated: removed the detached fire-and-forget telemetry IIFE + the 3 scattered Meta `console.error`s (consolidated into one structured warn); the output-contract check extends the EXISTING downgrade pass rather than adding a parallel path; the follow-up **shrinks the monolith** by lifting `extractToolContent` into a pure util (re-exported, zero importer churn), letting the isolated dispatch suite stay monolith-free.
- Behavior: behavior-preserving for chat EXCEPT the two intended ENG-105/ENG-108 edge-case corrections called out in the Behavior-preserving proof scope caveat. The follow-up image-only narrowing strictly reduces the ENG-105 edge-case surface. Verified by the unchanged characterization suite + the new wiring/false-positive tests.

## Behavior-preserving proof

> **Scope caveat (be precise):** this PR is NOT 100% behavior-preserving. **ENG-105** and **ENG-108** change prod tool behavior in two narrow, intended edge cases: (1) a tool that returns an empty/undefined/`'undefined'`/empty-content "success" is now downgraded to a structured tool failure (`invalid_output`) instead of feeding garbage back to the model; (2) two identical (name+key-sorted-args) tool calls emitted in the SAME turn now execute once (both `tool_call_id`s still answered) instead of twice. Both are deliberate correctness fixes, each gated to its exact trigger and covered by tests. The ENG-105 follow-up image-only narrowing strictly *shrinks* edge case (1) — it never downgrades a legitimate non-text result. Everything below is genuinely behavior-preserving.

- `npx tsc` clean; the AgentMode characterization suite (`src/__tests__/agentMode/characterization/`, 8 tests) passes unchanged — it pins the tool-call sequence, final content, responseMessages shape, and LLM turns consumed through `executePreparedTools`.
- ENG-102/103: telemetry path is gated behind `AGENT_RUNTIME_SPINE_ENABLED` (off in prod) and is observability-only; recorder methods still return promptly and swallow errors.
- ENG-104: the all-success Meta path returns the same `message` and adds only additive fields; fatal throws are untouched. The new `agent_tool_partial_failure` loop-event is additive observability only (emitted off the chat hot path, swallowing its own write errors) and fires only on `partialFailure:true`, so the all-success path is byte-identical.
- ENG-105: `validateToolOutput` is an optional port; existing **valid** outputs (string/formattedContent/content[0].text/data objects, AND image-only/non-text content arrays after the follow-up narrowing) return null (unchanged). The ONLY observable behavior change is the intended one in the scope caveat above — a genuinely empty/undefined output becomes a structured failure. New `validateToolOutputContract` unit + the real-port dispatch wiring test assert valid outputs stay valid and only empty outputs downgrade.
- ENG-108: dedupe only collapses identical (name+args) repeats in one turn and still answers every `tool_call_id`; distinct calls and exempt tools are unaffected (proved by tests + characterization).

Prior art (idea adopted, not pasted): ENG-102 — Vercel `waitUntil` / "drain background work before teardown"; ENG-105 & ENG-108 — Claude Code / OpenAI agent-loop "validate tool results at the boundary, return a structured tool error" and "collapse identical in-turn tool calls but still emit a result for every tool_call_id"; MCP `isError` convention; ENG-104 — the repo's own structured error taxonomy (`toolErrorClassifier`/`toolFailureType`).

## Behavioral assertions verified

**ENG-102**
- Per-tool telemetry awaited/durably queued before terminal run telemetry is complete → recorder write chain + `flush()` drained at run end (`flush() drains all enqueued writes`).
- Terminal record cannot race ahead of tool-result records for the same run → `serializes a terminal record AFTER per-tool records even when tool puts are slow`.
- Persistence failures surfaced as structured errors/metrics → `surfaces a write failure as a structured logger signal + writeFailures counter`.
- Tests cover ordering + write-failure → both above.

**ENG-103**
- Deferred emits a structured event w/ tool name, reason/category, run id, budget/defer context → `records a deferred tool call as its own event class with reason + budget context`.
- Daily summaries account deferred/skipped separately from success/failure → inspector `accounts deferred tool calls separately from success and failure`.
- Tests cover deferred recorded → recorder test + `forwards a deferred call to telemetry as a deferred result`.

**ENG-104**
- Partial endpoint failures represented in result AND telemetry → metaMetrics `returns success:true with partialFailure metadata...` + structured `console.warn`.
- Successful result indicates complete vs unavailable sections → `sections` field + pure-helper tests.
- Fatal vs partial distinguished consistently → fatal throws untouched (success:false) vs partial (success:true + partialFailure); pure-helper tests + integration.
- Tests cover partial breakdown failure + telemetry-visible metadata → integration test asserts `result.partialFailure`/`result.sections`.
- **Follow-up — partial failure emits a STRUCTURED loop-event (not just `console.warn`)** → recorder test `records a partial-failure tool call as its own event class with the unavailable sections (ENG-104)` asserts `agent_tool_partial_failure` fires with `unavailableSections`/`unavailableCount` metadata; pure-helper tests `buildToolPartialFailureTelemetry (ENG-104 — telemetry routing)` assert a flagged success → payload with the unavailable sections and an all-success/other-tool result → `null` (so the all-success path emits no event).

**ENG-105**
- Tool outputs validated against a minimum contract before treated as success → toolDispatch downgrade pass + `validateToolOutputContract`.
- Invalid/empty/undefined extracted content → structured tool failure → downgrade to status `error` + `formatToolError` (toolDispatch) ; classifier → `invalid_output`.
- Telemetry captures invalid-output distinctly from execution failures → `classifies a ToolOutputContractError as invalid_output`.
- Tests cover undefined / malformed object / empty content array / valid formatted content → `toolOutputContract.test.ts`.
- **Follow-up — the REAL `validateToolOutput` port is wired through dispatch and tested end-to-end** → `core/toolDispatch.test.ts` describe `ENG-105: real validateToolOutput port wiring` composes the actual `validateToolOutputContract(result, extractToolContent)` (not a mirror) into `executePreparedTools` and asserts that a result extracting to undefined / `''` / `'undefined'` / empty content is downgraded to a failure (failed counter incremented, no pending counter) with `classifyToolErrorClass(error) === 'invalid_output'`, while a valid string passes through as success.
- **Follow-up — false-positive fix: legitimate non-text content is preserved** → `toolOutputContract.test.ts` `accepts an image-only content array …` + `accepts a content array mixing a blank text part with a non-text part`, and the dispatch wiring test `passes an image-only content array through unchanged` assert an image-only `content:[{type:'image',...}]` success is NOT downgraded.

**ENG-108**
- Identical same-turn calls collapsed before execution unless non-dedupable → `collapses two identical calls...` + `does NOT collapse... wait_seconds`.
- Deduping preserves tool_call_id handling (valid response per emitted call) → `answers BOTH tool_call_ids`.
- Telemetry records duplicate suppression separately from success/failure → `records suppression separately and keeps duplicates OUT of success/failure telemetry`.
- Tests cover duplicate same-turn + distinct args → `does NOT collapse distinct args` + arg-order test.

- No live worker/IPC integration test for ENG-102 drain-before-exit (the unit proves serialization + flush; the worker wiring is exercised only via the bounded `flushAgentRunRecorderSafe` call site).

title: fix(backend): resolve file upload CORS errors, S3 fetching, and parser timeouts
body:
### Description
This PR resolves critical Backend failures in the attachment pipeline, PDF parsing hangs, and Notion bug reporting.

### Key Changes
1. **CORS Rejection Diagnostics (app.ts):** 
   - Appends the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header on CORS 403 Forbidden responses. This allows client browsers to read the response payload instead of raising a generic `TypeError: Failed to fetch` block.
2. **Private S3 Fetching (agentModeService.ts):**
   - Automatically detects private S3 bucket attachment URLs and fetches them directly using the AWS SDK stream, resolving 403 Forbidden failures on plain Axios GET requests.
3. **PDF Parser Timeout (agentModeService.ts):**
   - Implements a `Promise.race` timeout for the CPU-heavy `pdf-parse` operations, raised to 60 seconds to support large documents without risk of blocking the Event Loop indefinitely.
4. **Google Drive Link Guard (agentModeService.ts):**
   - Rejects unauthenticated Google Drive/Docs links with a clean, user-friendly message advising manual upload instead of failing silently on Axios.
5. **Issue Reporting Resilience (tools.ts):**
   - Increases Notion intake timeout to 30s to prevent false-negative timeouts during latency spikes.
   - Makes internal Resend notification emails non-blocking (fire-and-forget) to isolate SMTP failures from the primary tracker creation.
6. **Unit Tests (readFileContent.test.ts):**
   - Added full mock configurations for `@slack/web-api` to resolve axios mock conflicts during test setup.
   - Added unit test cases covering private S3 SDK streams, Google Docs link blocks, and PDF timeout boundaries.

title: feat: zero-downtime deploys with graceful drain on Elastic Beanstalk
body:
## Problem

Every deploy caused user-visible downtime:
- AWS Elastic Beanstalk (All-at-Once policy) took the instance out of service, deployed, then brought it back — causing 502 errors for the duration
- On SIGTERM, the Node.js process force-exited after 5 seconds, killing every in-flight scheduled chat, EMMA run, and agent-mode execution mid-flight with a "Worker shutdown" error
- Deploys ran on a daily cron schedule, not on every merge

## Solution

**Immutable deployment** — EB provisions a new EC2 instance with the new code, health-checks it, registers it with the ALB, then deregisters and drains the old one. Users are never served by an unhealthy instance.

**Graceful drain** — on SIGTERM the old instance:
1. Sets `isCronEnabled = false` immediately → `/run-scheduled-chats` returns 503, agent-engine reroutes to the new instance within one 5-second poll cycle
2. Stops accepting new HTTP/socket connections (`server.close()` + `io.close()`)
3. Waits up to 10 minutes for all in-flight scheduled chats and EMMA runs to complete naturally before killing the worker process
4. Guards all 13 background worker loops with `isCronEnabled()` so no new background work starts on a draining instance

**Timeout alignment**: drain ceiling (10 min) = ALB deregistration delay (10 min) < force-exit (13 min) < EB Timeout (15 min)

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `backend/src/utils/instanceState.ts` | New — in-memory `isCronEnabled` flag + `disableCron()` |
| `backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts` | 503 guard at top of `runScheduledChats` |
| `backend/src/server.ts` | Reordered graceful shutdown, 13-min force-exit, `isCronEnabled` guards on all 13 workers |
| `backend/src/services/generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.ts` | Drain-aware shutdown — polls `pendingRequests.size` every 2s, 10-min ceiling |

title: Fix Meta COPY_AD adcreative create failure (subcode 1487390)
body:
## What was wrong

`MetaService.getAdCreative()` requested the bare `object_story_spec` field from the Meta Graph API. Meta only returns `image_hash` for `link_data` / `video_data` / carousel `child_attachments` when that subfield is explicitly named via field-expansion syntax (`object_story_spec{link_data{image_hash,...}}`); requesting the bare field silently omits `image_hash` and returns only the hosted, low-resolution `picture` preview URL instead.

`copyMetaAdsAd` (the `COPY_AD` action of `call_meta_marketing_api`) reads that image_hash back so it can attach the *same* account-scoped hash to the new creative. Since the hash was never actually returned, every copy fell back to downloading Meta's `picture` preview URL and re-uploading it as a brand-new image — which Meta's `AdCreative` create endpoint rejects, producing error code 100, subcode 1487390 ("Adcreative Create Failed for the following reason: Something went wrong") on every attempt, regardless of source ad.

This matches the reported symptoms: 100% failure rate across all copied ads, and reproduces even for a manual `AD_CREATIVE` create call using `image_hash` sourced this way.

## Fix

Expand the `object_story_spec` field requested in `getAdCreative` to explicitly include `image_hash` (and `picture`) for `link_data`, `video_data`, and carousel `child_attachments`, so the original hash is returned and reused directly instead of triggering an unnecessary/broken re-upload.

## Verification

- Added unit tests in `backend/src/__tests__/metaService.test.ts` asserting `getAdCreative` requests `image_hash` as an explicit subfield for `link_data`, `video_data`, and carousel `child_attachments`. Confirmed these fail against the old bare-field request and pass after the fix.
- `npx tsc` passes.
- `npx jest src/__tests__/metaService.test.ts` — 60/60 passing.
- `npx jest src/__tests__/agentModeService.metaAdsCRUD.test.ts -t copyMetaAdsAd` — passing, no regression.

Note: live reproduction against the actual Meta ad account (26242538088719416) was not possible in this environment; this fix is based on static analysis of the code path plus Meta's documented Graph API field-expansion behavior for `object_story_spec`.

Fixes ENG-50 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-50/meta-copy-ad-fails-with-subcode-1487390-adcreative-create-failed

title: Fix video pipeline: voiceover, black-screen, timeout & closing-slate (ENG-123)
body:
## ENG-123 — Video generation pipeline: voiceover, black-screen, timeout, and closing-slate fixes

Resolves the four defects from the xCures CTV/OTT spot session (silent video, ~4s black screen, timeout on revision with no delivered asset, unacceptable closing slate).

### Fixes

1. **Silent video (primary defect).** `agentModeService.composeVideo()` enumerated only brand fields when calling `remotionService.compose` and dropped `audioUrl`/`audioVolume` — so a voiceover attached during composition was silently discarded. Now forwarded end-to-end.

2. **Black screen ("black hole").** `remotionService.compose` set the composition to `targetDurationSeconds` even when it exceeded the actual clip footage, rendering the bare black background as a multi-second tail. Duration is now **clamped to available footage** (`resolveCompositionDuration`) — a target can only trim, never pad with black — and the shortfall is surfaced to the user as a warning (not just a server log).

3. **Timeout on revision (no asset delivered).** `compose` blocked synchronously polling Remotion for up to 5 min; stacked on clip regeneration it blew past the run's 10-min wall-clock and was killed mid-compose. `compose` now bounds its poll to the run's remaining media-gen budget and, when it can't finish in time, **hands off the deterministic S3 output URL** with a "still finalizing" message — the detached Lambda completes on its own and the link resolves. No new tool/subsystem.

4. **Unacceptable closing slate.** `OutroOverlay` reworked to the Video Production skill's Layer 8: an opaque brand-gradient end card with the (previously missing) brand mark/logo, offer line, and URL button, with a staggered reveal. Button text and a light scrim keep it legible across arbitrary brand palettes.

5. **Voiceover regression tripwire.** `composeVideo` returns a soft warning when a branded spot is composed with no `audioUrl`, to catch revision passes that recompose without re-attaching the VO.

### Verification
- Unit: `resolveCompositionDuration`, `computeRenderPollBudget`, `buildRemotionOutputUrl`, and `composeVideo` (clamp/handoff/voiceover-warning) + full backend suite. `tsc` clean.
- Live (deployed test env): black-tail clamp (target 30 → 16s output), voiceover forwarding, and the **timeout handoff fired live** (fast return + "still finalizing" + the handed-off URL resolved once the detached render finished).
- Local Remotion render: voiceover bakes in (audio track present, differs from silent render), new slate confirmed.

### ⚠️ Deploy requires TWO parts
The composition-side behavior (voiceover `<Audio>` + new slate) renders in the **Remotion site**, not the backend. A backend-only deploy leaves them stale — verified: the test env ran this branch's backend yet rendered silent + old slate until the site was current.

**To close ENG-123 in prod, deploy BOTH:**
1. Backend (this PR) — clamp, handoff, `audioUrl` forwarding, tripwire warning.
2. **Remotion site redeploy** to the site prod serves from (`remotion lambda sites create --site-name=agentweb-compositions --region=us-east-1`) — confirm whether prod shares that site before redeploying (a shared site would affect prod immediately).

title: Coerce stringified array/object tool arguments before schema validation (ENG-127)
body:
What was wrong: read_knowledge_base_files consistently failed pre-execution schema validation with 'Argument "files" has the wrong type. Expected array.' even for valid arrays. title: feat: agent truthfulness bundle — finalize guard + instructive-error retryability + non-retryable fast-trip breaker (ENG-143/135/124)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

Linear: ENG-143, ENG-135, ENG-124 (generalizes the shipped ENG-104 single-tool pattern). Design source: `EMMA-HARNESS-PARITY-PLAN.md` § Build-Now Design / Truthfulness bundle (PR-T1 + the ENG-124 retry-spiral half).

## What was wrong (before)

1. Emma could claim completed actions the run never performed ("I've sent the email") — nothing checked the final message against the run's tool ledger, so action-hallucination shipped to users (the xCures 76×-images class, but for every high-harm action).
2. Tool errors fed back to the model said what failed but not whether retrying could help — terminal failures (auth, provider business-rule rejections, schema rejects) invited retry spirals (linkedin_outreach 15× in 16s), and the per-run breaker only tripped after 3 identical failures even when a retry was known-pointless.

## What this fixes (after)

1. **`finalizeGuard.ts`** (new, PURE, ports-injected like `core/toolDispatch.ts`) runs after the final assistant message, before emit/persist, behind **`AGENT_FINALIZE_GUARD` (env, DEFAULT OFF)**: cheap lexicon prefilter for 6 high-harm claim classes (email_sent, task_created_or_updated, post_published, schedule_created, crm_saved, asset_generated) → ONLY on hit, one judge call via the existing `callLLM` → deterministic match against successful ledger entries (`status==='success' && !toolResultError(result)`; asset claims via `mediaGenProducedAsset`) → mismatch → ONE corrective turn ("run log shows no successful <X> — restate the true outcome") → re-check → still mismatched → VISIBLE truthful correction appended + `claim_mismatch` recorded as a `computeRunVerdict` reason, so the run grades **degraded** and the 17:30 UTC failure-cluster cron sees the class.
2. **`errorRetryability.ts`** (new, PURE): every model-visible tool error at the dispatch boundary now ends with `[Retryable: yes/no — <actionable next step>]` derived from `toolErrorClassifier` classes. Non-retryable classes (auth / upstream_rejected / invalid_args / tool_unavailable / invalid_output) additionally **fast-trip the per-run circuit breaker at 2 identical failures instead of 3**.
   - `policy_blocked` (gateway policy rejections) is the sixth `FAST_TRIP_ERROR_CLASSES` member — also NOT retryable, also fast-trips at 2; now asserted in the positive `isFastTripErrorClass` test alongside the five above.

## NO-FALLBACK compliance

- `AGENT_FINALIZE_GUARD` is an A-or-B migration flag (env absent = feature off), NOT an on-error reroute.
- The guard NEVER silently rewrites: every text change is the model's own corrective restatement or a clearly visible appended correction.
- Judge/correction-call failure on this advisory gate = deliver the message unchanged (or original + visible correction) + a LOUD `agent_claim_check_error` telemetry event (`console.error` + durable Dev-AW-LoopEvents row). This best-effort behavior is explicitly documented at the call site — blocking chat delivery on a judge outage would be failing badly (a new hard dependency on the judge).

## Behavior-preserving proof

- **Flag OFF (default):** the pre-existing characterization harness (`backend/src/__tests__/agentMode/characterization/` — coreLoop + toolDispatch, 24 tests) passes UNCHANGED before and after this diff (snapshot files untouched; ran as baseline pre-change and again post-change). A new explicit test also pins that with the flag unset the corrective-turn transcript consumes ONE llm turn and delivers the claim unchanged.
- **Flag ON path pinned before anyone flips it:** new `finalizeGuard.characterization.test.ts` pins the corrective-turn transcript (main turn → judge turn → corrective turn = 3 llm turns, final content = corrected text, message shape unchanged).
- `npx tsc` clean; targeted + full suites green (counts below).
- **Two intended, non-flag-gated deltas (both "fewer errors / faster stop", charter-sanctioned):** (1) tool-error tool-messages gain the trailing `[Retryable: …]` line — the characterization contract is shape-level (tool sequence, final content, message shape) and is unaffected; (2) the breaker trips at 2 (not 3) identical failures for non-retryable classes. Two existing gateway tests used non-retryable-class error messages incidentally and were updated to retryable-class messages to preserve their original intent (reset-on-success; no-clear accounting) — noted inline in the test file.

## Complexity ledger

- **Lines:** +1,220 / −16 total; production code ≈ +630 (finalizeGuard 288 + errorRetryability 97 + monolith wiring ~155 + recorder/eventTypes/gateway/dispatch ~90); tests ≈ +560; docs 13.
- **Moving parts added:** 2 pure core modules (ports-injected, individually tested), 1 env flag (default OFF), 1 telemetry event type, 1 verdict reason. No new tables, deps, services, or transports.
- **What pays for it:** collapses the N-per-tool "reports success falsely" bug class into ONE enforcement seam — future truthfulness fixes are matcher entries, not per-tool patches; retry-spirals stop one attempt earlier with an explicit stop signal instead of more per-tool retry prose accumulating in `formatToolError`; claim mismatches self-file via the existing verdict → 17:30 cluster-cron pipeline (no new reporting system).
- **Monolith:** +~155 lines in `agentModeService.ts` (flag-gated wiring + two `callLLM` helpers). The logic lives in core and is unit-tested; the monolith only wires ports — this is the plan's designed seam (PR-T1), not drift.

## How to test

1. `cd backend && npx jest characterization` — **Expected:** 4 suites / 26 tests pass; the 24 pre-existing snapshots unchanged (flag OFF default).
2. `npx jest src/services/agentMode/core/__tests__/finalizeGuard.test.ts` — **Expected:** all pass, incl. corrective-turn, unresolved-mismatch (visible correction + claimMismatch), judge-failure deliver-unchanged.
3. `npx jest src/__tests__/agentToolGatewayService.test.ts` — **Expected:** pass, incl. "trips after TWO identical NON-retryable failures" and "still allows a third attempt after two identical RETRYABLE failures".
4. `npx jest src/__tests__/loops.runVerdict.test.ts` — **Expected:** `claimMismatch:true` → degraded with `claim_mismatch` reason; `claimCheckError` emits `agent_claim_check_error`.
5. Manual (test env, optional): set `AGENT_FINALIZE_GUARD=true`, ask Emma to "confirm you sent the email" in a session where no email tool ran. **Expected:** the reply restates the true outcome (or carries a visible ⚠️ Correction), and the run's verdict event shows `claim_mismatch`.

## Edge cases to check

- A reply paraphrasing a REAL success (email actually sent via `send_email`) must NOT be corrected — covered by the backed-claim test; worth one manual spot-check with the flag on.
- Media confirmation-gate pause (`awaitingUserConfirmation`) claiming "I generated the image" → corrected (covered; this is the xCures shape).
- Known limitation (advisory impact only): the breaker's threshold classification runs on the stored 80-char truncated error head (`ERROR_KEY_LENGTH`), so an error whose class-identifying marker appears past 80 chars classifies as unknown and gets the default threshold 3 instead of the fast-trip 2 — the breaker still trips, just one identical failure later.

## Test Evidence

- **Full backend suite: 14,951 passed, 1 failed, 3 skipped (918/919 suites).** The one failure is `socialPosts.test.ts › handles metrics fetch failure gracefully` failing with "socket hang up" under full-suite parallel load only — it passes 13/13 in isolation and this PR touches no social-posts code (pre-existing flake, unrelated).
- The full suite ran at the implementation commit; the one follow-up commit (suppressed-duplicate ledger mapping, `agentModeService.ts` only) was re-verified with targeted characterization + finalizeGuard suites (42/42) + clean tsc.
- Targeted runs (all green): characterization 26/26 (4 suites, 24 pre-existing byte-identical); core dispatch/guard/retryability + gateway + loops verdict/recorder 212/212 (7 suites); formatToolError-adjacent service suites 100/100 (4 suites).
- `npx tsc`: clean after every edit.
- TDD order: failing tests committed first (6 suites / 9 targeted failures), then implementation.

## Files changed

- New: `backend/src/services/agentMode/core/finalizeGuard.ts`, `backend/src/services/agentMode/core/errorRetryability.ts` (+ their test files)
- `backend/src/services/agentMode/core/toolDispatch.ts` — retryability line at the 3 `formatToolError` sites
- `backend/src/services/agentToolGatewayService.ts` — fast-trip threshold for non-retryable classes
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` — flag-gated guard wiring + judge/correction helpers + claimMismatch threading
- `backend/src/loops/instances/agent-mode/runRecorder.ts`, `eventTypes.ts` — `claim_mismatch` verdict reason, `claimCheckError` / `agent_claim_check_error`
- Tests: `__tests__/agentToolGatewayService.test.ts`, `__tests__/loops.runVerdict.test.ts`, `core/__tests__/toolDispatch.test.ts`, `__tests__/agentMode/characterization/finalizeGuard.characterization.test.ts`
- `dev.md` — investigation/assumptions note

## What was NOT tested

- No live-LLM run of the judge/corrective turn (all judge calls mocked/scripted) — real-world extraction quality of the judge prompt is unvalidated; the Okareo claim-faithfulness check (separate task in the plan) covers that.
- Lexicon prefilter recall against a real prod claim corpus (tuned on synthetic phrasings; false negatives skip the guard).
- The flag ON in a real environment — it ships OFF. The flip is Harsha's call, together with the ~10-line truthful-reporting system-prompt block, which is explicitly OUT of scope for this PR (taste lane) and is the follow-up Harsha flips with the flag.
- Judge token-cost under prod traffic (bounded by prefilter hits; unmeasured).

## Design forks settled (simpler option, stated per instructions)

- The guard consumes the loop's persisted `toolCalls` ledger mapped to a normalized `FinalizeLedgerEntry` (toolName/status/minimal result) instead of threading raw `DispatchToolResult[]` out of every iteration — the minimal results preserve the markers matching needs (encoded failures, `awaitingUserConfirmation`), with zero loop-state plumbing.
- On correction, the LAST assistant message is corrected IN PLACE (same message count) and stamped with `finalizeGuard` metadata for auditability, instead of appending a new system+assistant pair — keeps the responseMessages shape stable.
- Judge/corrective calls use the run's own `llmModel` (already in scope, harness-spied); a cheaper dedicated judge model is a one-line port change deliberately left for the flip decision.

## Related PRs

- Backend: standalone
- Customer Portal: standalone (zero frontend changes)

title: feat(run-survival): durable run records, idempotency submit-locks, incident dedupe, drain disclosure (ENG-40/147/145/146)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

Run-survival core for AgentMode: durable run records, cross-restart idempotency submit-locks, structural incident dedupe, and honest interruption disclosure. The **run store itself** (run records, idempotency submit-locks, incident dedupe) is behind the **`AGENT_RUN_STORE=true`** config gate (flag absent = store off; A-or-B switch, NOT an on-error fallback). **Five reliability deltas ship ungated (always-on)** — deliberately kept unconditional as reliability fixes; they are listed explicitly in the Behavior-preserving proof section so the ship decision is made on true information.

Linear: ENG-40, ENG-147, ENG-145, ENG-146

## What was wrong (before)
- No durable run identity: runIds existed for telemetry only, minted deep inside the service; nothing recorded that a run started, so a deploy-killed run left a zero-output mystery (ENG-40) and dedupe/disclosure had nothing to anchor on.
- No submit dedupe across restarts/retries: the in-memory `activeSessionGenerations` Set only blocks *concurrent* runs — a network retry of the same message runs twice (ENG-147's ~30-duplicate-sessions storm).
- One failing scheduled run could file multiple Linear incidents (validation-fail site + exception site, plus requeue re-fires) and flood oncall alerts (ENG-145/146).
- Worker death disclosed a generic "server restarted" with no statement of which in-flight tool calls were NOT executed; the drain-ceiling rejection ("Worker shutdown — drain ceiling exceeded") was not even classified as a shutdown; /generate kept accepting new runs during drain.

## What this fixes (after)
- **`AW-AgentRuns` table + `services/agentMode/runStore.ts`**: `run#<runId>` records (running -> completed/failed/interrupted, 30d ttl), `idem#<key>` conditional-put submit-locks (10m interactive / 24h scheduled), `incident#<runId>` conditional-put claims (24h). runId minted ONCE at intake and threaded controller -> worker -> `generateMarketingResponse`, where it becomes the telemetry `agentRuntimeRunId` (one run, one identity). Terminal updates are conditioned on `attribute_exists(pk)` — if `createRunRecord` threw (the documented loud-500 path), the outer catch's `markRunTerminal` is a no-op instead of upserting a phantom ttl-less `run#…` item.
- **Idempotency submit-lock** at both /generate claim sites, BEFORE `tryClaimSessionGeneration`; the loser gets the existing 409 `SESSION_BUSY` shape + the in-flight `runId`. Scheduled lane claims `(scheduleId + fireTime)` before any schedule mutation — duplicate triggers start nothing.
- **Incident dedupe**: `fileAutoIssue` gained optional `dedupeKey`; both scheduled-chat failure sites pass the run's runId -> structurally one issue per run. Oncall alerts at those sites keyed `(user, schedule, errorClass)` with a 1h window (reuses the existing alert-dedupe machinery).
- **Drain + disclosure**: `stopAcceptingRequests()` in gracefulShutdown -> /generate returns 503 `SHUTTING_DOWN`; worker death rejects each in-flight request with its own error carrying `pendingTools`; the persisted disclosure names the tools that were **NOT executed**; interactive run records marked `interrupted`; scheduled interruptions store an explicit interrupted-with-partial-summary result.

## How to test
Local (no AWS needed):
1. `cd backend && npx jest runStore.test intakeService.dedupeKey pendingTools runSurvival scheduledRunSurvival`
2. **Expected**: 5 suites, 47 tests pass.
3. `npx jest characterization`
4. **Expected**: 3 suites, 24 tests pass, unchanged from the main baseline.

On a test env (flag ON):
1. Run `NODE_ENV=development npx ts-node src/scripts/create-tables.ts` (creates `Dev-AW-AgentRuns`), enable DynamoDB TTL on the `ttl` attribute, set `AGENT_RUN_STORE=true`.
2. Send the SAME message to one session twice in quick succession (two curl POSTs to `/api/agent-mode/generate`).
3. **Expected**: first returns normally; second returns 409 `SESSION_BUSY` with a `runId` field; exactly one assistant reply in the session; `Dev-AW-AgentRuns` has one `run#…` item ending `status=completed`.
4. Start a long generation, then `kill -9` the worker child process mid-run.
5. **Expected**: session shows "The server restarted while processing your request… these in-flight tool calls were NOT executed: …"; run record is `status=interrupted, finishReason=worker_exit`; an immediate retry of `/generate` is accepted (no 10-min lockout).
6. `kill -TERM` the backend during an in-flight run.
7. **Expected**: new `/generate` requests get 503 `SHUTTING_DOWN` while the in-flight run drains (up to 10 min, pre-existing drain).

## Edge cases to check
- Identical message resent AFTER a run completes -> accepted (idem lock released at terminal state; ttl only bounds crash staleness).
- A scheduled run that fails validation AND whose requeue then throws -> still exactly one Linear issue (same runId dedupeKey at both sites).
- `AGENT_RUN_STORE=true` with the table missing -> /generate 500s loudly by design (NO-FALLBACK: run-record creation is core state). Create the table before flipping the flag. The 500 path's `markRunTerminal` is a conditional no-op — no phantom un-TTLed `run#…` item is ever written for a run that was never recorded.

## Test evidence
- New tests: **47 passed / 5 suites** (runStore DDB-fake unit tests; controller interactive + scheduled lanes; intake dedupe; worker pendingTools/ordering) — written failing-first (TDD), including the no-upsert `markRunTerminal` test.
- Characterization harness: **24 passed / 3 suites — unchanged** (baseline run before any edit, re-run after).
- Targeted regression (every touched area — all `agentModeController.*`, worker service, intake, agentModeErrors, characterization, runStore): **51 suites, 667 tests passed**.
- Full backend suite: **920 suites passed (1 skipped), 14,943 tests passed / 3 skipped, 0 failed** (258s, re-run after the no-upsert fix).
- `npx tsc`: clean.

## Behavior-preserving proof

**Scope of the flag claim — the run store only, NOT the whole PR.** `AGENT_RUN_STORE` gates run records, idempotency submit-locks, and incident dedupe (`claimIncident` inside `fileAutoIssue`): flag OFF = zero run-store calls and zero writes to `AW-AgentRuns`, pinned by the "flag off -> today's exact behavior" tests in both controller suites. Flag ON adds: a 409 `SESSION_BUSY` body gains `runId`; duplicate submits inside the idem window get 409 instead of a second run; one incident per run; durable run records.

**Five deltas ship ungated (always-on).** These are deliberate, unconditional reliability fixes — with the flag off, behavior is NOT byte-identical to main in these five places:

1. **503 `SHUTTING_DOWN` drain** — during graceful shutdown, `/generate` (and the shared-conversation variant) return 503 instead of accepting runs the deploy is about to kill (`instanceState.stopAcceptingRequests()`, wired in `server.ts` gracefulShutdown).
2. **Worker-death disclosure** — the persisted "server restarted" message now names the in-flight tool calls that were **NOT executed** (`pendingTools` captured in `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService`); previously a generic restart notice.
3. **Scheduled interrupted result shape** — a worker-shutdown scheduled run stores `interrupted: true` plus a new explicit interrupted-with-partial-summary `actualResponse` text, instead of the generic error shape / zero-output mystery.
4. **Oncall alert dedupe keys** — the scheduled failure sites (`validation_failed` / `zero_output` / `run_error`) now pass `(user, schedule, errorClass)` dedupe keys with a 1h window to the existing alert-dedupe machinery; previously unkeyed -> alert floods.
5. **Drain-ceiling classification** — `isWorkerShutdownError` now classifies the exact "Worker shutdown — drain ceiling exceeded" message as a shutdown; previously it fell through to the generic diagnosis path. Deliberately NOT a loose prefix match (existing tests pin that arbitrary "Worker shutdown …" strings stay unclassified).

Each delta is pinned by its own tests. None change chat outputs, tool selection, prompts, or model defaults on the happy path — they only change what happens during shutdown, worker death, and failure alerting.

**Characterization harness** (fixed session + stubbed LLM/tools -> pinned tool-call sequence + final message): **24/24 before and after, unchanged**.

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines**: +1,821 / −19 total, of which **+1,139 are tests** and +17 dev.md. Production code: **+665/−19** (runStore 282, create-tables 32, controller +262/−9, the rest thin threading).
- **Moving parts added**: 1 DynamoDB table (AW-AgentRuns), 1 env flag (`AGENT_RUN_STORE`), 1 module (runStore). No new dependency, no new process, no queue/engine invented.
- **What it earns / removes**: kills the ENG-145+146 duplicate-incident class *structurally* (conditional put, not convention); kills the ENG-147 duplicate-run class; unifies the controller's per-path runIds with the telemetry runId (one identity instead of N ad-hoc ones). The runId + run-record seam is exactly what the Inngest phase consumes — its event idempotency key is this SAME key, so nothing here gets deleted later. The zero-output requeue ladder is deliberately KEPT — its deletion belongs to the gated Inngest phase, not this PR.
- **Already existed on main — NOT rebuilt** (recon map was stale): B1 lock-leak release, B4 SSE-zombie clear-before-drop ordering, worker drain (10 min) + 13-min force-exit, EB `Timeout: 900` + ALB idle/dereg 600s, alert-dedupe machinery. This PR only uses them; the plan's "raise 5s force-exit + .ebextensions" item is already satisfied on main.

## Design forks settled (simpler option, stated per instructions)
- **Interruption disclosure is an assistant message, not wire-format synthetic `tool_result` blocks**: the `tool_use` ids live only in the dead worker process, so the parent cannot construct valid tool_use<->tool_result pairs; fabricating ids would corrupt the transcript. The disclosure names the interrupted tools explicitly ("NOT executed"), which is the truthful content the plan asks for. If the finalize-guard phase needs real synthetic tool_results, they must be written from inside the worker before exit.
- **Scheduled runVerifiedChat inner attempts keep their own telemetry runIds**: one scheduled run = N generations; forcing one id would emit N `agent_run_started` events under one id and corrupt telemetry grouping. The scheduled run *record* is keyed by the schedule-level runId (threaded as `preGeneratedRunId`).
- **Alert keying** uses `(userId, scheduleId, errorClass)` labels {validation_failed, run_error, zero_output} with the existing 1h window, matching the plan's B5 shape.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/agentMode/runStore.ts` (new) + `backend/src/scripts/create-tables.ts` — the store + table
- `backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts` — intake wiring (both /generate sites, scheduled trigger, runScheduledChat terminal/dedupe/disclosure)
- `backend/src/services/generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.ts`, `backend/src/workers/generateMarketingResponseWorker.ts`, `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` — runId threading + pendingTools capture
- `backend/src/services/intakeService.ts` — `dedupeKey` param
- `backend/src/utils/instanceState.ts`, `backend/src/server.ts` — drain acceptance flag
- `backend/src/utils/agentModeErrors.ts` — drain-ceiling classification
- 5 new test files, `dev.md` note

## What was NOT tested
- No live DynamoDB integration test — the run store is tested against a conditional-put-aware DocumentClient fake (put AND update conditions); the real table's TTL enablement is a manual step (documented in create-tables.ts).
- No end-to-end kill-the-worker test on a real test env (unit/controller tests simulate worker death via the existing mocked-worker harness).
- Flag-ON behavior under production traffic — ship with the flag off, create the table, then flip on the test env first.

title: feat(observability): OTel spine — gen_ai spans at run/model/tool seams, Langfuse + Okareo exporters (ENG-141)
body:
## Risk: Low | telemetry-only, zero chat-path changes, inert without env keys

## What was wrong (before)
No OTel instrumentation anywhere in the backend ([ENG-141](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-141)). Debugging an Emma run meant DynamoDB event spelunking — no trace view, no span timing at the run/model/tool boundaries, and no bridge into Okareo for eval ingest.

## What this fixes (after)
An OTel spine emitting `gen_ai`-semconv spans at the three seams that matter — `invoke_agent` (run lifecycle), `chat` (around `callLLM`, including the backup-model retry), `execute_tool` (`toolDispatch.runOne`) — exported to Langfuse (trace UI) and Okareo (eval ingest). Exporters register only when env keys are present; without keys the tracer is a no-op and nothing changes.

## Behavior-preserving proof
- Characterization suite: **24/24 unchanged** (characterization test files untouched by this diff — verified via `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat`)
- `npx tsc`: **clean** (exit 0)

- Full backend suite on this branch: **915 suites passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (916 of 917 ran) · 14,919 tests passed, 1 failed, 3 skipped (14,923 total) · 226.7s.** The single failure (`routes.mcpServers.test.ts` — PUT validation, 404 vs 200) passes **17/17 in isolation** and its files are untouched by this diff — a pre-existing parallel-load flake, same class as the known `socialPosts.test.ts` "socket hang up" flake (which did not reproduce this run).

Net **+1054/−20** (~520 of it tests + lockfile). Adds:

- Optional `traceId` dimension on `agent_run_started`

Earns its keep as the ENG-141 observability spine: instruments every run/model/tool call at the two extracted seams, feeds Langfuse (trace UI) + Okareo (eval ingest, closes the ENG-141 OTel bridge). No collector, no auto-instrumentation, exporters registered only when env keys present (config gating), content capture default OFF.
